   547	 succeeded in 0ms:
   548	    50	### Core engine (`core/`)
   549	    51	
   550	    52	**Language/tooling**: plain ESM JavaScript (`.mjs`) + JSDoc types checked by `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` (dev-only dep). No build step — hooks invoke source directly (`node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…"`), same as the proven codex plugin. **Zero runtime dependencies**; arg parsing via `node:util` `parseArgs`; **`node:test`** as the framework (golden-file helper ~40 lines with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`). Node >= 20. Every command's `run()` takes an injected `io` object (`{cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now}`); pure logic (reducers/renderers/resolvers/classifiers) is data-in/data-out; tests run over an in-memory fs fake plus a thin real-fs integration layer.
   551	    53	
   552	    54	**CLI surface** (`baton <cmd> --json`): `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover` (forced lock recovery). Frozen exit-code contract: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json` mode prints exactly one envelope `{ok, data, warnings, error}` on stdout. `baton wrap -- <cmd>` (PTY supervisor) is **deferred post-v1** — hook-driven detection suffices; the name/contract is reserved.
   553	    55	
   554	    56	**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
   555	    57	
   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
   557	    59	
   558	    60	**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker. On load, a present marker deterministically rolls the rotation forward (if the snapshot landed) or back (if not); the same marker pattern governs interrupted forced takeovers and interrupted purges (purge resumes from its marker until the whole tree is clean). Retention: last 10 rotations pruned with the history. Doctor warns at journal > 5 MB; perf test: 10k-event replay < 1 s. **Filesystem support boundary: v1 supports local filesystems only** — lock and rename atomicity are not guaranteed on network/shared mounts (NFS/SMB/cloud-sync folders); doctor detects and warns, README states it.
   559	    61	
   560	    62	**Root discovery & degraded modes** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): repo root = nearest ancestor containing `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree-aware: linked worktrees resolve to their own toplevel, shared state stays per-worktree), else cwd — `--root <path>` overrides; nested/monorepo launches therefore resolve to the same bundle deterministically, but **discovery never crosses the boundary of a nested independent git repository** (a `.git` between cwd and a candidate root stops the walk) unless `--root` says otherwise. Non-git directories: supported — `git` section is null, git-dependent features degrade with explicit warnings. Read-only sandboxes (EACCES/EROFS on `.handoff/`): checkpoint fails open with a warning naming the user-executed fallback (`baton checkpoint` run manually outside the sandbox; `receive --print-prompt` never needs writes until `--commit`). All git invocations carry a 5 s timeout (configurable); timeout → git section marked `unavailable`, never a hang.
   561	    63	
   562	    64	**Transcript policy** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): transcript-tail capture at PreCompact is **opt-in and off by default** (`capture.transcriptTail` in `baton.config.json`), bounded (last 10 messages, 8 KB cap), passed through a secret-redaction filter (common credential/token patterns; fixtures with planted secrets prove redaction), stored in a dedicated bundle field excluded from HANDOFF.md by default. `baton purge-transcript` removes the field from **every retained copy** — active snapshot, `.bak`, journal (rewrite-and-rotate under lock), and all `history/` freezes — with a test asserting planted secrets are absent from the entire `.handoff/` tree afterward. **Diagnostics logging contract (iteration 4)**: `.handoff/log/` entries are metadata-only and redacted — raw hook payloads never enter them (fixture-proven) — with bounded retention (last 50 entries / 7 days) and inclusion in the whole-tree purge test.
   563	    65	
   564	    66	**Checkpoint engine**: adapters send pre-normalized `baton/event@1` on stdin (the real API); raw hook payloads get best-effort per-platform extraction (`normalize.mjs`) that never throws — unknowns degrade to `note` events. Idempotent via dedupe keys; journal append always, snapshot rewrite throttled (≥10 events / 30 s / important event types). **Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on all soft failures** so a checkpoint can never break the host harness (`--strict` for CI). `finalize --reason "…" [--reason-class] [--to]` records the switch reason (class inferred from text via the classifier when omitted), refreshes git state, freezes history.
   565	    67	
   566	    68	**Limit detector**: two tiers — **structured signals first** (Claude Code `StopFailure` matcher error types; documented limit-specific fields in codex JSON output), text signatures as fallback. **Exit-code rule (iteration 3): a generic nonzero exit never classifies as usage-limit on its own** — exit 10 requires limit-specific structured or text evidence; nonzero without evidence = `other-error`. Fixture corpus includes non-limit failing processes. Signatures are **versioned data** (`core/data/signatures.v1.json`), seeded with the verified strings for all three platforms, matcher kinds `substring`/`regex`/`json-field`, per-signature confidence, precedence usage-limit > auth > throttle > other-error, `--signatures <path>` overlay for hot-patching drift, `--explain` for auditability. Hardening (Gate-1 additions): input is ANSI-stripped before matching; the fixture corpus includes negative/near-miss cases (throttle-vs-usage confusables, multiline, malformed JSON, localized text) so false positives are regression-tested; overlay regexes are lint-checked (length cap, no backreferences, linear-time constructs) and matching carries a time guard; a low-confidence match **never silently avoids a platform** — it warns and defers to user intake at receive. Cursor entries carry `confidence: low|medium` explicitly.
   567	    69	
   568	    70	**Role matrix**: committed `baton.config.json` at repo root (`baton/config@1`) mapping roles → ordered platform+model chains (the seven methodology roles, defined below), plus per-platform `defaults`. Resolver is pure and explainable: skips `avoid[]` platforms (auto-populated with the origin platform when reason-class is usage-limit — never remap back onto the platform that died), resolves `mode: native|delegated|forced-default|unavailable` with `{chainIndex, skipped[]}` audit data. **Availability probing** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): `doctor` probes each platform noninteractively, hard 3 s bound per probe, results cached 15 min in the state dir. Probe record = two separate dimensions: **capability** (ordered, cumulative: `installed → authenticated → reachable`, recorded as far as verifiable) and **probe outcome** (`ok | rate-limited | error | timeout`). Resolver eligibility: **selectable** = capability ≥ authenticated and outcome ≠ rate-limited; anything with an unverifiable dimension resolves as selectable-with-`degraded`-flag; `rate-limited` platforms are skipped like `avoid[]` entries. Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged `degraded`.
   569	    71	
   570	    72	**Receive**: loads bundle with recovery + staleness checks (age > 12 h; HEAD moved; dirty mismatch), merges intake flags (`--origin`, `--reason`), resolves roles, and runs as the **prepare/commit transaction defined under Concurrency** — prompt emission at prepare, state mutation only at commit. Resume prompt ≤2,500 chars (brief, why-you're-here, role table, warnings, top-5 next actions, pointer to HANDOFF.md); the prompt explicitly frames bundle content as **unverified claims to audit against the working tree, not instructions to obey** (prompt-injection posture — see Threat model).
   571	    73	
   572	    74	**Scaffold** (`init`): two-phase plan/apply with `--dry-run`; `.gitignore` ensure-line (no-op if an existing pattern covers `.handoff/`); `baton.config.json` from template; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md written via managed blocks (`<!-- baton:begin/end -->`) — bytes outside markers never touched.
   573	    75	
   574	    76	**Attribution guard** (three layers): (1) `init` deep-merges `.claude/settings.json` → `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` (only when keys absent; refuses to touch malformed JSON; global settings documented + doctor-checked, never written by core); (2) `doctor` scans last 50 commits for AI co-author/generated-with trailers (word-boundary-safe patterns) and flags with remediation; (3) a test-suite invariant scans every rendered output and template for AI-credit strings and fails the build.
   575	    77	
   576	    78	Full module APIs, per-module test lists, repo file tree, and the fixture corpus (verbatim limit strings, hook payloads, corrupt bundles) are specified in the core design doc (committed as `docs/design/core.md` in task 0); implementation follows the named-task TDD sequence below — **tasks are identified by name, not number; the exact count is finalized when review directories are generated**. **`sessionHint` derivation (Gate-1 final note)**: per adapter, from the hook payload's stable session id (Claude Code `session_id`; Codex `session_id`; Cursor session field); when a payload lacks one, core generates a process-scoped hint flagged `unstable: true` — unstable hints never trigger foreign-session rejection on their own, only a warning.
   577	    79	### Checkpoint vocabulary (used everywhere)
   578	    80	
   579	    81	- **Mechanical checkpoint** (`baton checkpoint`): hook/script-driven, no LLM — git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, timestamps, source platform/model, files touched. <1 s, safe per-turn.
   580	    82	- **Narrative seal** (`baton finalize`, surfaced as `/handoff`): model-written — decisions + rationale, verified-done vs claimed-done, next steps, gotchas, reason for switching.
   581	    83	
   582	    84	Claude Code DOES emit a structured limit-death event (`StopFailure` with a `rate_limit` matcher); Codex and Cursor do not. The design is therefore: event-driven detection where it exists, rolling mechanical checkpoints everywhere (last coherent turn always captured), narrative seals at milestones, and receive compensating for a missing seal by asking the user why they switched and re-deriving git facts live, auditing HANDOFF.md claims against them.
   583	    85	
   584	    86	### Claude Code adapter (Tier A — highest fidelity)
   585	    87	
   586	    88	Plugin root = **repo root**: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (author: SakshamUboweja) with path overrides pointing at `adapters/claude-code/{commands,skills,agents,hooks}` so `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` reaches `core/bin/baton.mjs` directly; `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` makes the repo its own single-entry marketplace (same shape as `openai/codex-plugin-cc`). **Spike task 0 verifies path-override support**; fallback = CI copy step vendoring `core/` under the adapter.
   587	    89	
   588	    90	Hooks (all fail-open — errors log to `.handoff/log/`, exit 0; a checkpoint must never break a session):
   589	    91	
   590	    92	| Event | Use | Timeout |
   591	    93	|---|---|---|
   592	    94	| `StopFailure` (matcher enum — e.g. `rate_limit`, `billing_error`, `server_error` — **snapshot verbatim from the official hooks reference during task 0**; fixtures generated from that canonical list; unknown future values normalize to `unknown` safely) | **The limit-death signal.** Classifies the error (matcher + payload through `baton detect`), writes a fail-open mechanical checkpoint stamped `trigger: stop-failure/<type>`, and on `rate_limit` marks the bundle limit-hit so the next SessionStart (any platform) surfaces it. Output/exit code are ignored by the harness — safe by construction. Tests cover the full snapshot enum. | 30 s |
   593	    95	| `Stop` | Routine mechanical checkpoint per assistant turn (proven codex stop-gate pattern; never emits `decision: block`) | 30 s |
   594	    96	| `PreCompact` | Snapshot context boundary before compaction; transcript-tail capture is **opt-in, off by default** (see core §transcript policy) | 60 s |
   595	    97	| `SessionEnd` | Clean-exit checkpoint | 30 s |
   596	    98	| `SessionStart` | Not a checkpoint: if a sealed or limit-hit bundle from another platform exists, inject "handoff pending — suggest `/baton:receive`" context | 10 s |
   597	    99	
   598	   100	`PostToolUse` rejected: per-tool-call spawns for incoherent mid-turn state; Stop gives the same worst-case staleness (one turn) at a fraction of the cost.
   599	   101	
   600	   102	Commands: **`/baton:handoff`** (model-invocable so Claude can propose it near limits; writes the narrative — auditing every "done" claim against tool evidence — then seals via finalize, then prints the destination's resume command); **`/baton:receive`** (`disable-model-invocation: true`; runs receive → one AskUserQuestion with two questions: origin platform with detected option first, reason for switch → ack runs the core commit transaction (received seal archived, this session adopted as owner, fresh `open` generation; double-receive prevented by the one-time token; command tests assert the active/open + archived/received outcome) → evidence audit of bundle git snapshot vs live HEAD/status → announce role-remap table → auto-continue next step, pausing only per AGENTS.md boundaries); **`/baton:baton-setup`** (doctor + choose surfaces + init + template scaffold with diff preview). Receive-side continuation is a **skill** (`handoff-protocol`), not an agent — the main thread must inherit the task; a subagent would strand context. Optional v2 `handoff-verifier` agent (fresh-context bundle audit) is out of v1 scope.
   601	   103	
   602	   104	### Codex adapter (Tier A− — hook-driven as of Codex >= 0.144)
   603	   105	
   604	   106	Gate-1 correction: Codex now ships lifecycle hooks, so the adapter is redesigned around them. Surfaces: (1) **repo `.codex/hooks.json`** (written by `init --codex`, merged never clobbered): `Stop` → mechanical checkpoint, `PreCompact` → context-boundary checkpoint, `SessionStart` → pending-handoff notice via injected context. No StopFailure equivalent exists on Codex, so a limit death is bounded by the last Stop checkpoint (one turn worst case). (2) `.agents/skills/baton-handoff/SKILL.md` per the Agent Skills standard — carries the receive/handoff protocol, invoked as `$baton-handoff` or by description match. (3) Repo `AGENTS.md` Handoff Protocol section as the always-on instruction layer (narrative checkpoints after subtasks / before risky ops / at wind-down). (4) `~/.codex/prompts/*.md` demoted to **legacy fallback only** (deprecated upstream), written only with `--with-legacy-prompts`. The notify shim is **cut** — hooks make it obsolete; `~/.codex/config.toml` is never touched. **Trust gate** (verified, Gate-1 iteration 2): Codex requires per-definition review of non-managed command hooks — trust is recorded against the hook's hash, and new/changed hooks are skipped until re-trusted via `/hooks`. Setup and doctor therefore report four distinct states per hook — installed / enabled / **trusted** / observed-executing (canary event) — and the fidelity claim is gated on the canary, with setup guiding the user through `/hooks` when review is pending. Hook definitions include `commandWindows` overrides. Fidelity statement ships verbatim in README + doctor: mechanical staleness ≤ 1 turn via Stop hook **once trusted**; narrative staleness bounded by protocol compliance; git state always re-derived at receive. Requires codex-cli >= 0.144 (doctor enforces; older versions fall back to protocol-only Tier C with an explicit warning).

   606	   108	### Cursor adapter (Tier A− — hook-driven; event names verified against official docs, Gate-1 iteration 2)
   607	   109	
   608	   110	Surfaces: `.cursor/hooks.json` (project-level, `{"version":1,"hooks":{...}}`) with the **verified** events — `stop` → mechanical checkpoint per agent turn (same semantics as Claude Code `Stop`); `afterFileEdit` → debounced checkpoint (debounce enforced by the CLI, one real checkpoint per 2 min); `beforeShellExecution` with a git-commit matcher → checkpoint before agent-issued commits (**documented limitation: commits made through the SCM UI are invisible to hooks — no pre-commit event exists**); `sessionStart` → pending-handoff notice; `preCompact` → context-boundary checkpoint. Plus `.cursor/commands/{receive,handoff,baton-setup}.md` (CLI loading unconfirmed — convenience layer; every behavior also reachable via AGENTS.md, which cursor-agent reads natively, and via the universal fallback **`baton receive --print-prompt`**) and a ≤5-line `.cursor/rules/baton-handoff.mdc` (`alwaysApply: true`). hooks.json written only after explicit confirmation, merged not clobbered; project hooks require a **trusted workspace** — doctor checks trust and gates the fidelity claim on an observed hook canary. Fidelity: mechanical staleness ≤ 1 turn via `stop` when trusted; untrusted/cloud contexts degrade to protocol-only with an explicit warning.

   610	   112	### Templates: ideal AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md
   611	   113	
   612	   114	Design rule resolving the two-model-family tension: **every shared invariant appears exactly once in AGENTS.md**; model-specific steering is quarantined (short Claude block in CLAUDE.md; scoped Codex notes only if ever needed). Budget: AGENTS.md ≤220 lines (handoff section ≤25), enforced by a template test. ALWAYS/NEVER reserved for true invariants (attribution, destructive ops, TDD ordering); judgment calls get decision rules.
   613	   115	
   614	   116	AGENTS.md sections (template `templates/AGENTS.md.tpl`, `{{TEST_CMD}}`-style variables filled by `baton init` from detection): 1 Project (one paragraph + directory map) · 2 Roles and models (points at committed config; "resolve via `baton remap`, never hardcode model names") · 3 Working phases (research → plan → test-authoring → implementation → review → handoff, one-line entry/exit criteria, "state your phase") · 4 TDD contract (no implementation before failing tests exist and are verifier-approved; test changes re-enter verification; progress claims must cite command output) · 5 Review gates (Gate 1 plan, per-subtask test review, Gate 2 dual independent final review; verdicts APPROVED/APPROVED_WITH_NOTES/BLOCKED) · 6 Handoff protocol (when/how to checkpoint and resume) · 7 Boundaries and stop rules (never force-push/hard-reset/delete without explicit instruction; pause for scope change/irreversible/credentials; otherwise "when you have enough information to act, act") · 8 Validation (command table; done = green + gate verdict) · 9 Git and attribution (sole author SakshamUboweja; zero AI attribution invariant; **commit cadence rule: commit after every completed subtask/green TDD cycle — small, regular commits to main so contributions accrue to Saksham's GitHub profile**; never commit `.handoff/`) · 10 Memory (`.handoff/notes.md`, gitignored, rides the bundle across handoffs).
   615	   117	
   616	   118	CLAUDE.md shim (~15 lines): line 1 `@AGENTS.md`; then ≤8 Claude-specific bullets — subagent delegation for parallel research/verification, concrete per-role mechanics (reviewer roles via codex companion, test-author via Agent-tool model override), plans in `docs/plans/`, attribution-setting reminder, **commit-cadence reminder (commit each completed subtask; never batch a day's work into one commit)**, prefer `/baton:*` commands, **user-facing outputs simple and concise: outcome first, plain language, no jargon walls**. Nothing duplicating AGENTS.md; no reasoning-echo instructions.

   720	   146	
   721	   147	When only one vendor is reachable, test-author/verifier fall back to different models in fresh sessions and every review artifact header carries `degraded: single-vendor` — weakening is auditable, never silent. Review artifacts extend the wt-* convention exactly: `reviews/<task-id>/{gate-1-plan, subtask-NN-tests, gate-2-final/{reviewer-a, reviewer-b, findings.md}}/iteration-NN/{prompt.md, verdict.md}`, templates ported from `wt-supervisor/reviews/_templates/`. The loop: plan doc in `docs/plans/` with goal + genuine constraints (falsifiable acceptance criteria) → Gate 1 → per-subtask test-first with the implementer forbidden from weakening/deleting tests (modifications re-enter verification) → dual independent fresh-context final reviews → collate `findings.md` → fix blocking items, re-review by the raising reviewer → loop until acceptance constraints are met with evidence attached. **Iteration budget (Saksham's rule): every review gate loops at most 5 times — hard stop after the 5th iteration; on exhaustion, the gate ends with the outstanding findings escalated to Saksham for a human decision instead of a 6th run.** This cap is encoded in the AGENTS.md template's review-gates section and applies to building this repo too.

   745	   171	
   746	   172	### Acceptance constraints (the loop's exit condition)
   747	   173

   833	    63	export function run(argv, io) {

   835	    65	  // Global --json intent is parsed BEFORE dispatch (gate-2 iter-2 M6): a
   836	    66	  // top-level `--json` with no command, or --help/--version, must still emit

   843	    73	    // No command — just flags (or nothing).

   852	    82	      return 0;
   853	    83	    }
   854	    84	    // Bare invocation (or a lone --json): a usage error.
   855	    85	    if (jsonWanted) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'usage', msg: 'no command given' } });
   856	    86	    else io.stdout.write(USAGE);

   862	    92	  const rest = args.filter((_, i) => i !== cmdIndex);

   866	    96	  const wantsJson = jsonWanted;

   870	   100	    return 2;
   871	   101	  }
   872	   102	  if (!COMMANDS.includes(cmd)) {

   875	   105	    return 2;
   876	   106	  }
   877	   107

   879	   109	    // Subcommand help honors the global --json envelope too (iter-3 F8): with
   880	   110	    // --json it must emit exactly one envelope, never raw usage text.
   881	   111	    const usage = `usage: baton ${cmd} [options]\n\nSee README for the ${cmd} contract.`;
   882	   112	    if (wantsJson) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: true, data: { usage } });
   883	   113	    else io.stdout.write(`${usage}\n`);
   884	   114	    return 0;
   885	   115	  }
   886	   116

   888	   118	  if (cmd === 'detect') return cmdDetect(rest, io);

   890	   120	  if (cmd === 'checkpoint') return cmdCheckpoint(rest, io);
   891	   121	  if (cmd === 'finalize') return cmdFinalize(rest, io);
   892	   122	  if (cmd === 'receive') return cmdReceive(rest, io);
   893	   123	  if (cmd === 'init') return cmdInit(rest, io);
   894	   124	  if (cmd === 'doctor') return cmdDoctor(rest, io);
   895	   125	  if (cmd === 'purge-transcript') return cmdPurgeTranscript(rest, io);
   896	   126	  if (cmd === 'session-start') return cmdSessionStart(rest, io);
   897	   127	  if (cmd === 'recover') return cmdRecover(rest, io);
   898	   128	
   899	   129	  const error = { code: 'not-implemented', msg: `baton ${cmd}: not implemented yet` };
   900	   130	  if (rest.includes('--json')) {
   901	   131	    emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error });
   902	   132	  } else {
   903	   133	    io.stderr.write(`${error.msg}\n`);
   904	   134	  }

   984	    76	 * token, so a stale receipt can never commit (plan §Concurrency).

   988	    80	function tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io) {
   989	    81	  let configDigest = 'absent';
   990	    82	  try {
   991	    83	    configDigest = dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(`${root}/baton.config.json`, 'utf8'));
   992	    84	  } catch {
   993	    85	    // no config — 'absent' is itself a bound value
   994	    86	  }

   996	    88	    generation: bundle.generation,
   997	    89	    journalSeq: bundle.journalSeq,
   998	    90	    // The seal state is a bound input too (gate-2 fix): a competing receiver
   999	    91	    // that lands between this token's derivation and its commit changes
  1000	    92	    // status/receive_log, so the loser's token cannot re-derive.
  1001	    93	    handoffStatus: bundle.handoff?.status ?? null,

  1003	    95	    origin: opts.origin,
  1004	    96	    reason: opts.reason,
  1005	    97	    // Explicit --reason-class is a bound intake input (gate-2 iter-2 M4): it

  1007	    99	    // drift that must re-prepare.

  1009	   101	    configDigest,
  1010	   102	    gitDigest: dedupeKey(opts.gitSnapshot ?? null),
  1011	   103	    probesDigest: dedupeKey(opts.probes ?? null),
  1012	   104	    platform: opts.platform,
  1013	   105	    sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
  1014	   106	  };

  1085	   177	    // recorded origin platform); typed intake only fills the gaps — a user

  1090	   182	    // medium+ confidence, else it warns and defers to explicit intake.

  1931	    35	 * mutations run under the repo lock, acquired WITHOUT waiting (gate-2 minor
  1932	    36	 * 16): a held lock means someone is mid-operation — reconciliation defers to
  1933	    37	 * the next unlocked load instead of writing behind their back.

  2290	   101	    pid: io.pid,
  2291	   102	    startTime: io.startTime,
  2292	   103	    fencingToken: token,
  2293	   104	    acquiredAt: io.now(),
  2294	   105	    heartbeatAt: io.now(),
  2295	   106	  });
  2296	   107	  return token;
  2297	   108	}
  2298	   109	
  2299	   110	/** @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p */
  2300	   111	function acquire(io, p) {
  2301	   112	  io.fs.mkdirSync(p.dir, { recursive: true });
  2302	   113	  try {
  2303	   114	    io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
  2304	   115	    return publishOwner(io, p);
  2305	   116	  } catch (err) {
  2306	   117	    if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code !== 'EEXIST') throw err;
  2307	   118	  }
  2308	   119	
  2309	   120	  const s = inspect(io, p);
  2310	   121	  switch (s.state) {
  2311	   122	    case 'free':
  2312	   123	      // Raced a release between mkdir failure and inspection; retry once. A
  2313	   124	      // competitor can win THIS mkdir too (gate-2 fix 12: observed under real
  2314	   125	      // barrier-released contention) — that is contention, not corruption.
  2315	   126	      try {
  2316	   127	        io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
  2317	   128	      } catch (err) {
  2318	   129	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') {
  2319	   130	          throw new LockHeldError('lock was re-acquired by a competitor mid-inspection — transient contention');
  2320	   131	        }
  2321	   132	        throw err;
  2322	   133	      }
  2323	   134	      return publishOwner(io, p);
  2324	   135	    case 'live':
  2325	   136	      throw new LockHeldError(
  2326	   137	        `lock is held by a live process (pid ${s.owner.pid} on ${s.owner.host}) — terminate that process first.`,
  2327	   138	      );
  2328	   139	    case 'cross-host':
  2329	   140	      throw new Error(
  2330	   141	        `lock is held from another host ('${s.owner.host}', this is '${io.host}') — cross-host locks are never provably safe to steal. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
  2331	   142	      );
  2332	   143	    case 'torn':
  2333	   144	      // During ACQUIRE, torn metadata is usually a competitor caught between
  2334	   145	      // its mkdir and owner.json publication — transient by construction, so
  2335	   146	      // LockHeldError lets withLock wait it out (gate-2 fix 12). A genuinely
  2336	   147	      // crashed publisher exhausts the retry budget and surfaces this same
  2337	   148	      // message; recovery semantics (recoverLock) are unchanged: never steal.
  2338	   149	      throw new LockHeldError(`${s.cause} — unsupported for automatic recovery. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`);
  2339	   150	    case 'dead': {
  2340	   151	      // Atomic dead-lock reclaim (gate-2 iter-2 B1, hardened iter-3 finding-1).
  2341	   152	      // rm-then-mkdir is NOT mutually exclusive: two contenders can both observe
  2342	   153	      // 'dead' before either removes the stale dir, then both rm+mkdir — the
  2343	   154	      // second silently clobbers the first, yielding two simultaneous holders and
  2344	   155	      // two takeover notes. rename() is the atomic arbiter instead: the stale
  2345	   156	      // lock dir has exactly one name, so only one process can move it aside (the
  2346	   157	      // rest get ENOENT). Winning the rename IS winning the reclaim; a contender
  2347	   158	      // that recreated the dir via the 'free' path first makes our mkdir EEXIST →
  2348	   159	      // transient contention. The fencing token stays the write-time backstop.
  2349	   160	      const aside = `${p.lockDir}.reclaim-${io.pid}-${io.newFencingToken()}`;
  2350	   161	      try {
  2351	   162	        io.fs.renameSync(p.lockDir, aside);
  2352	   163	      } catch (err) {
  2353	   164	        // Source already gone → another contender is reclaiming it; wait+retry.
  2354	   165	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'ENOENT') {
  2355	   166	          throw new LockHeldError('a competitor is reclaiming the dead lock — transient contention');
  2356	   167	        }
  2357	   168	        throw err;
  2358	   169	      }
  2359	   170	      io.fs.rmSync(aside, { recursive: true, force: true });
  2360	   171	      try {
  2361	   172	        io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
  2362	   173	      } catch (err) {
  2363	   174	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') {
  2364	   175	          throw new LockHeldError('a competitor re-claimed the dead lock first — transient contention');
  2365	   176	        }
  2366	   177	        throw err;
  2367	   178	      }
  2368	   179	      const token = publishOwner(io, p);
  2369	   180	      // Journal the takeover only now — we HOLD the lock (fresh dir + published
  2370	   181	      // owner), so the note's seq is allocated while holding it (plan
  2371	   182	      // §Concurrency "sequence numbers are allocated under the lock"), never
  2372	   183	      // racing a free-path competitor's concurrent append (iter-3 F2). The note
  2373	   184	      // is best-effort (0-or-1) and MUST NOT abort acquisition (iter-4 I7): if it
  2374	   185	      // threw here — after publishOwner, before the token is returned to withLock
  2375	   186	      // — the release finally would never run and the lock would leak with a live
  2376	   187	      // owner. Swallow it; the reclaim already succeeded.
  2377	   188	      try {
  2378	   189	        journalNote(io, p, `lock takeover: took over stale lock from dead pid ${s.owner.pid} (start time ${s.owner.startTime})`);
  2379	   190	      } catch {
  2380	   191	        // audit note is best-effort
  2381	   192	      }
  2382	   193	      return token;
  2383	   194	    }
  2384	   195	    /* c8 ignore next 2 */
  2385	   196	    default:
  2386	   197	      throw new Error('unreachable lock state');
  2387	   198	  }
  2388	   199	}

  2390	   201	/**
  2391	   202	 * Fence-guarded release: the lock dir is removed only while owner.json still
  2392	   203	 * carries OUR token. A holder that paused past a takeover must not delete the
  2393	   204	 * competitor's lock on its way out — release is a write like any other.
  2394	   205	 * @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p @param {string} token
  2395	   206	 */
  2396	   207	function release(io, p, token) {
  2397	   208	  try {
  2398	   209	    const current = JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(p.owner, 'utf8'));
  2399	   210	    if (current.fencingToken !== token) return; // a competitor took over — their lock, not ours
  2400	   211	  } catch {
  2401	   212	    return; // owner metadata gone or torn mid-hold — never guess; leave it for recovery
  2402	   213	  }
  2403	   214	  io.fs.rmSync(p.lockDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  2404	   215	}
  2405	   216	
  2406	   217	// A live same-host holder is transient by design — operation-scoped locks are
  2407	   218	// held for milliseconds — so contention waits instead of dropping the
  2408	   219	// operation (gate-2 fix 12: simultaneous checkpoints must all land). The budget
  2409	   220	// is generous (≈15 s): under heavy load a writer may be starved of scheduling
  2410	   221	// for seconds, and waiting is strictly safer than silently dropping its work.
  2411	   222	// Every other contended state (torn, cross-host) stays fail-fast: waiting
  2412	   223	// cannot make those provably safe.
  2413	   224	const DEFAULT_RETRY = { attempts: 600, delayMs: 25 };
  2414	   225	
  2415	   226	/** Synchronous sleep without burning a core: Atomics.wait on a throwaway buffer. */
  2416	   227	const sleepMs = (/** @type {number} */ ms) => {
  2417	   228	  Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms);
  2418	   229	};
  2419	   230	
  2420	   231	/**
  2421	   232	 * Acquire → run fn(token) → release (also on throw). Synchronous by design:
  2422	   233	 * everything the lock guards is sync fs work. Live-held locks are retried on
  2423	   234	 * a bounded budget (override via io.lockRetry = {attempts, delayMs}).
  2424	   235	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {(token: string) => any} fn
  2425	   236	 */
  2426	   237	export function withLock(root, io, fn) {
  2427	   238	  const p = lockPaths(root);
  2428	   239	  // Jail BEFORE any lock mutation (gate-2 iter-2 B2): a symlinked .handoff or
  2429	   240	  // .handoff/lock must never be created into or removed through — that would
  2430	   241	  // reach outside the repository. Checked once here, ahead of acquire.
  2431	   242	  const safe = checkHandoffTree(root, io);
  2432	   243	  if (!safe.ok) throw new Error(`${safe.problem} — refusing to acquire the lock`);
  2433	   244	  const retry = io.lockRetry ?? DEFAULT_RETRY;
  2434	   245	  /** @type {string} */
  2435	   246	  let token;
  2436	   247	  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
  2437	   248	    try {
  2438	   249	      token = acquire(io, p);
  2439	   250	      break;
  2440	   251	    } catch (err) {
  2441	   252	      if (err instanceof LockHeldError && attempt < retry.attempts) {
  2442	   253	        sleepMs(retry.delayMs);
  2443	   254	        continue;
  2444	   255	      }
  2445	   256	      throw err;
  2446	   257	    }
  2447	   258	  }
  2448	   259	  try {
  2449	   260	    return fn(token);
  2450	   261	  } finally {
  2451	   262	    release(io, p, token);
  2452	   263	  }
  2453	   264	}
  2454	   265	
  2455	   266	/**
  2456	   267	 * Fast-abort layer: re-read the published token immediately before a write; a
  2457	   268	 * holder that paused past its last check aborts instead of clobbering.
  2458	   269	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {string} token @param {() => any} fn
  2459	   270	 */
  2460	   271	export function guardedWrite(root, io, token, fn) {
  2461	   272	  const p = lockPaths(root);
  2462	   273	  let current = null;
  2463	   274	  try {
  2464	   275	    current = JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(p.owner, 'utf8'));
  2465	   276	  } catch {
  2466	   277	    throw new FencingError('lock owner metadata is gone — fencing check failed; aborting write');
  2467	   278	  }
  2468	   279	  if (current.fencingToken !== token) {
  2469	   280	    throw new FencingError(
  2470	   281	      `fencing token changed (held '${token}', current '${current.fencingToken}') — another process took over; aborting write`,
  2471	   282	    );
  2472	   283	  }
  2473	   284	  return fn();
  2474	   285	}

  2476	   287	/**
  2477	   288	 * Explicit recovery. `force` is an intent flag only — it never changes the
  2478	   289	 * decision: exactly one state recovers (provably-dead same-host owner).
  2479	   290	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {{force?: boolean}} [opts]
  2480	   291	 * @returns {{recovered: boolean, refusedReason: string | null}}
  2481	   292	 */
  2482	   293	export function recoverLock(root, io, opts = {}) {
  2483	   294	  void opts;
  2484	   295	  const p = lockPaths(root);
  2485	   296	  // Jail before recovery (gate-2 iter-2 B2): recoverLock removes the lock dir,
  2486	   297	  // so a symlinked managed tree must be refused first — even with force, a
  2487	   298	  // symlink is never provably safe to delete through.
  2488	   299	  const safe = checkHandoffTree(root, io);
  2489	   300	  if (!safe.ok) return { recovered: false, refusedReason: `${safe.problem} — refusing recovery` };
  2490	   301	  const s = inspect(io, p);
  2491	   302	  switch (s.state) {
  2492	   303	    case 'free':
  2493	   304	      return { recovered: true, refusedReason: null };
  2494	   305	    case 'dead': {
  2495	   306	      // Reclaim atomically via a single acquire() attempt + release, NOT an
  2496	   307	      // inspect-then-rmSync (iter-4 I1): the old bare rmSync had a TOCTOU — a
  2497	   308	      // competitor could win the rename-arbitrated dead-reclaim between this
  2498	   309	      // inspect() and the rmSync, publish a LIVE owner, and recovery would then
  2499	   310	      // delete a lock whose owner is alive. acquire() re-inspects atomically and
  2500	   311	      // shares the SAME rename arbitration, so recovery and a concurrent takeover
  2501	   312	      // are mutually exclusive: acquire either reclaims a still-dead lock (and
  2502	   313	      // journals the takeover under the lock) or throws because it is now
  2503	   314	      // live/torn — in which case we refuse rather than steal. release() then
  2504	   315	      // leaves the slot clear.
  2505	   316	      let token;
  2506	   317	      try {
  2507	   318	        token = acquire(io, p);
  2508	   319	      } catch (err) {
  2509	   320	        return { recovered: false, refusedReason: /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err) };
  2510	   321	      }
  2511	   322	      release(io, p, token);
  2512	   323	      return { recovered: true, refusedReason: null };
  2513	   324	    }
  2514	   325	    case 'live':
  2515	   326	      return {
  2516	   327	        recovered: false,
  2517	   328	        refusedReason: `lock is held by a live process (pid ${s.owner.pid} on ${s.owner.host}) — terminate that process first.`,
  2518	   329	      };
  2519	   330	    case 'cross-host':
  2520	   331	      return {
  2521	   332	        recovered: false,
  2522	   333	        refusedReason: `lock is held from another host ('${s.owner.host}', this is '${io.host}') — cross-host locks are never provably safe to steal, even with force. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
  2523	   334	      };
  2524	   335	    case 'torn':
  2525	   336	      return {
  2526	   337	        recovered: false,
  2527	   338	        refusedReason: `${s.cause} — unsupported for automatic recovery, even with force. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
  2528	   339	      };
  2529	   340	    /* c8 ignore next 2 */
  2530	   341	    default:
  2531	   342	      return { recovered: false, refusedReason: 'unreachable lock state' };
  2532	   343	  }
  2533	   344	}

  2674	    67	        baseReal = base;
  2675	    68	      }
  2676	    69	      // Compare on normalized forward-slash spellings (iter-3 F9): raw Windows
  2677	    70	      // backslash realpaths never satisfy a forward-slash containment, so
  2678	    71	      // opt-in capture would silently never fire.
  2679	    72	      return isContained(baseReal, fileReal);
  2680	    73	    };
  2681	    74	    if (!allowed.some(under)) return null;
  2682	    75	
  2683	    76	    const text = io.fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
  2684	    77	    const lines = text.split('\n').filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l.trim() !== '');
  2685	    78	    let tail = lines.slice(-TAIL_MESSAGES).join('\n');
  2686	    79	    if (Buffer.byteLength(tail) > TAIL_BYTES) {
  2687	    80	      tail = Buffer.from(tail).subarray(-TAIL_BYTES).toString('utf8');
  2688	    81	    }
  2689	    82	    return redactSecrets(tail);
  2690	    83	  } catch {
  2691	    84	    return null; // unreadable transcript is never a checkpoint failure
  2692	    85	  }
  2693	    86	}
  2694	    87	
  2695	    88	/** Event-shaped: an object carrying a string `type`. */
  2696	    89	const isEventShaped = (/** @type {any} */ v) => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) && typeof v.type === 'string';
  2697	    90	
  2698	    91	/**
  2699	    92	 * Tolerant stdin parse (live /baton:handoff failure: a model sent one event
  2700	    93	 * per line and the whole narrative checkpoint silently failed). Accept the
  2701	    94	 * canonical single JSON value, a bare array of events, or NDJSON where every
  2702	    95	 * line is an event object or a {schema, events} wrapper. All-or-nothing: one
  2703	    96	 * non-event element fails the whole parse — never a partial apply.
  2704	    97	 * @param {string} text @returns {{ok: true, raw: any} | {ok: false, why?: string}}
  2705	    98	 */
  2706	    99	function parseStdin(text) {
  2707	   100	  let single;
  2708	   101	  let singleOk = false;
  2709	   102	  try {
  2710	   103	    single = JSON.parse(text);
  2711	   104	    singleOk = true;
  2712	   105	  } catch {
  2713	   106	    singleOk = false;
  2714	   107	  }
  2715	   108	  if (singleOk) {
  2716	   109	    if (Array.isArray(single)) {
  2717	   110	      return single.every(isEventShaped) ? { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: single } } : { ok: false };
  2718	   111	    }
  2719	   112	    // A closest-miss of the documented wrapper — an events array whose schema
  2720	   113	    // key is missing or wrong — must ERROR, never silently degrade to a junk
  2721	   114	    // note with ok:true (the model cannot self-correct from a success
  2722	   115	    // envelope while its narrative was discarded).
  2723	   116	    if (single !== null && typeof single === 'object' && Array.isArray(single.events) && single.schema !== 'baton/event@1') {
  2724	   117	      return { ok: false, why: `stdin carries an events array but schema is ${single.schema === undefined ? 'missing' : JSON.stringify(single.schema)} — use {"schema":"baton/event@1","events":[…]}` };
  2725	   118	    }
  2726	   119	    // A single bare event object (string `type`, none of the raw-hook payload
  2727	   120	    // markers) is one of the two most likely readings of "pipe events on
  2728	   121	    // stdin" — accept it as that event instead of degrading it to a junk note.
  2729	   122	    if (
  2730	   123	      isEventShaped(single) &&
  2731	   124	      single.schema === undefined &&
  2732	   125	      !('hook_event_name' in single) &&
  2733	   126	      !('session_id' in single) &&
  2734	   127	      !('event' in single)
  2735	   128	    ) {
  2736	   129	      return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: [single] } };
  2737	   130	    }
  2738	   131	    return { ok: true, raw: single };
  2739	   132	  }
  2740	   133	  const lines = text.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l !== '');
  2741	   134	  if (lines.length === 0) return { ok: false };
  2742	   135	  /** @type {any[]} */
  2743	   136	  const events = [];
  2744	   137	  for (const line of lines) {
  2745	   138	    let v;
  2746	   139	    try {
  2747	   140	      v = JSON.parse(line);
  2748	   141	    } catch {
  2749	   142	      return { ok: false };
  2750	   143	    }
  2751	   144	    if (v && typeof v === 'object' && v.schema === 'baton/event@1' && Array.isArray(v.events)) {
  2752	   145	      if (!v.events.every(isEventShaped)) return { ok: false };
  2753	   146	      events.push(...v.events);
  2754	   147	    } else if (isEventShaped(v)) {
  2755	   148	      events.push(v);
  2756	   149	    } else {
  2757	   150	      return { ok: false };
  2758	   151	    }
  2759	   152	  }
  2760	   153	  return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events } };
  2761	   154	}
  2762	   155	
  2763	   156	/**
  2764	   157	 * `baton checkpoint` — mechanical checkpoint from a hook payload on stdin.
  2765	   158	 * Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on every soft failure so a checkpoint can never
  2766	   159	 * break the host harness; `--strict` opts into hard failures (CI).
  2767	   160	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
  2768	   161	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
  2769	   162	 */
  2770	   163	export async function cmdCheckpoint(args, io) {
  2771	   164	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { platform: 'string', model: 'string', trigger: 'string', debounce: 'string', strict: 'boolean', 'take-over': 'boolean' });
  2772	   165	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'checkpoint', parsed.error);
  2773	   166	  const flags = parsed.flags;
  2774	   167	  const strict = flags.strict === true;
  2775	   168	  const platform = typeof flags.platform === 'string' ? flags.platform : null;
  2776	   169	  if (!platform) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', '--platform <claude-code|codex|cursor> is required');
  2777	   170	  const pErr = platformError(platform);
  2778	   171	  if (pErr) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', pErr);
  2779	   172	
  2780	   173	  try {
  2781	   174	    return await run(flags, platform, io);
  2782	   175	  } catch (err) {

  2784	   177	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'checkpoint-failed', msg } });
  2785	   178	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: ${msg}\n`);
  2786	   179	    return strict ? 1 : 0;
  2787	   180	  }
  2788	   181	}

  2905	   298	      writeSnapshot(root, fresh, io);

  2907	   300	      active = fresh;
  2908	   301	      mustRewrite = true;
  2909	   302	    }

  2916	   309	  if (active === null) {

  2923	   316	    // (snapshot + .bak both lost) must restore the bundle's identity, not the
  2924	   317	    // "unknown" placeholder resolveBase seeds. bundle.seed carries bundleId,
  2925	   318	    // origin, task, and generation and is applied on replay.

  2978	    27	/**
  2979	    28	 * Repo-root discovery (plan §Root discovery): `--root` wins; else the nearest
  2980	    29	 * ancestor of io.cwd carrying `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`; else the
  2981	    30	 * nearest ancestor carrying `.git` (the repo toplevel — and a boundary the
  2982	    31	 * walk never crosses, so a nested repo resolves to itself); else io.cwd.
  2983	    32	 * @param {any} io @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
  2984	    33	 * @returns {string}
  2985	    34	 */
  2986	    35	export function resolveRoot(io, flags) {
  2987	    36	  if (typeof flags.root === 'string' && flags.root.length > 0) return flags.root;
  2988	    37	  // Normalize separators up front (gate-2 iter-2 M2): a Windows cwd arrives
  2989	    38	  // backslash-separated, but Node fs accepts forward slashes, so the ascent
  2990	    39	  // and the marker checks work in one forward-slash space. The last separator
  2991	    40	  // is either kind; the loop stops at a drive/UNC or filesystem root.
  2992	    41	  const start = normSep(io.cwd);
  2993	    42	  let dir = start;
  2994	    43	  while (true) {
  2995	    44	    try {
  2996	    45	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.handoff')) || io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, 'baton.config.json'))) return dir;
  2997	    46	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.git'))) return dir; // repo toplevel; never walk past a .git boundary
  2998	    47	    } catch {
  2999	    48	      break;
  3000	    49	    }
  3001	    50	    const cut = dir.lastIndexOf('/');
  3002	    51	    if (cut < 0) break;
  3003	    52	    const parent = cut === 0 ? '/' : dir.slice(0, cut);
  3004	    53	    // At a drive-relative ceiling ("C:") examine the drive ROOT ("C:/") once —
  3005	    54	    // a repo can live directly at C:/ (iter-3 F6) — then stop.
  3006	    55	    if (/^[A-Za-z]:$/.test(parent)) {
  3007	    56	      const driveRoot = `${parent}/`;
  3008	    57	      if (driveRoot !== dir) {
  3009	    58	        dir = driveRoot;
  3010	    59	        continue;
  3011	    60	      }
  3012	    61	      break;
  3013	    62	    }
  3014	    63	    if (parent === dir) break;
  3015	    64	    dir = parent;
  3016	    65	  }
  3017	    66	  return start;
  3018	    67	}

  3020	    69	/** The supported platform enum, validated wherever a platform id is intake. */

  3023	    72	/**
  3024	    73	 * Validate a platform id against the enum (surface-audit fold): a typo'd
  3025	    74	 * platform used to silently seed persistent state whose bogus origin then
  3026	    75	 * rejected the REAL platform's checkpoints as foreign.

  3030	    79	export function platformError(value) {

  3036	    85	/**
  3037	    86	 * Strict flag parser (surface-audit fold; docs/design/core.md §tooling always
  3038	    87	 * specified strict parsing). spec maps each flag name to 'string' | 'boolean';
  3039	    88	 * `json` and `root` are implied common flags. Errors — unknown flag, stray
  3040	    89	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
  3041	    90	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token
  3042	    91	 * flip SAFETY flags off (checkpoint/doctor --strict, remap --native-only,
  3043	    92	 * receive --print-prompt all read fail-dangerous exit 0).
  3044	    93	 * @param {string[]} args
  3045	    94	 * @param {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} spec
  3046	    95	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, error?: string}}
  3047	    96	 */
  3048	    97	export function parseFlagsStrict(args, spec) {
  3049	    98	  /** @type {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} */
  3050	    99	  const full = { json: 'boolean', root: 'string', ...spec };
  3051	   100	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
  3052	   101	  const flags = {};
  3053	   102	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {

  3082	   131	 * Minimal flag parser: `--key value` pairs (value = next token not starting
  3083	   132	 * with --), bare `--key` booleans, positionals collected in order.

  3085	   134	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, positionals: string[]}}
  3086	   135	 */
  3087	   136	export function parseFlags(args) {
  3088	   137	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
  3089	   138	  const flags = {};
  3090	   139	  /** @type {string[]} */
  3091	   140	  const positionals = [];
  3092	   141	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
  3093	   142	    const a = args[i];
  3094	   143	    if (a.startsWith('--')) {
  3095	   144	      const key = a.slice(2);
  3096	   145	      const next = args[i + 1];
  3097	   146	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
  3098	   147	        flags[key] = next;
  3099	   148	        i += 1;
  3100	   149	      } else {
  3101	   150	        flags[key] = true;
  3102	   151	      }
  3103	   152	    } else {
  3104	   153	      positionals.push(a);
  3105	   154	    }
  3106	   155	  }
  3107	   156	  return { flags, positionals };
  3108	   157	}

  3494	   148	      break;
  3495	   149	    default:
  3496	   150	      out.decisions.push({ seq, ts, summary: `[unhandled event type '${type}' recorded as note]` });
  3497	   151	      break;
  3498	   152	  }
  3499	   153	
  3500	   154	  out.updatedAt = ts;
  3501	   155	  // Harden against foreign/keyless entries (gate-2 fix): a missing seq must

  3503	   157	  // the ring (undefined in the ring dedupes every later keyless event).

  3714	   201	/**
  3715	   202	 * Classify one probe invocation per the two-dimension record: capability is
  3716	   203	 * the ordered ladder verified as far as the evidence goes; outcome is what the
  3717	   204	 * probe itself did. A server-issued limit response proves authentication.
  3718	   205	 * @param {{platform: string, bin: string, args: string[], capOnSuccess?: string}} probe @param {any} io @param {any} table
  3719	   206	 */
  3720	   207	async function runProbe(probe, io, table) {
  3721	   208	  try {
  3722	   209	    await io.execFile(probe.bin, probe.args, { timeout: PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS });
  3723	   210	    return { platform: probe.platform, capability: probe.capOnSuccess ?? 'reachable', outcome: 'ok' };
  3724	   211	  } catch (err) {
  3725	   212	    const e = /** @type {any} */ (err);
  3726	   213	    if (e?.code === 'ENOENT') return { platform: probe.platform, capability: null, outcome: 'error' };
  3727	   214	    if (e?.killed === true) return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'timeout' };
  3728	   215	    const text = `${e?.stdout ?? ''}\n${e?.stderr ?? ''}`;
  3729	   216	    if (table && classify({ text, exitCode: 1, platform: probe.platform, table, structured: null }).class === 'usage-limit') {
  3730	   217	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'authenticated', outcome: 'rate-limited' };
  3731	   218	    }
  3732	   219	    if (/authenticated as|logged in as/i.test(text) && /unreachable|ECONN|offline|network/i.test(text)) {
  3733	   220	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'authenticated', outcome: 'error' };
  3734	   221	    }
  3735	   222	    if (/not logged in|log ?in first|unauthorized|authenticat/i.test(text)) {
  3736	   223	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'error' };
  3737	   224	    }
  3738	   225	    return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'error' };
  3739	   226	  }
  3740	   227	}

  4958	     6	reviews/

  4970	    18

  4987	     1	# Core engine design — module APIs and test lists
  4988	     2	
  4989	     3	Authoritative plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md` (Gate-1 approved). Where this doc and the plan differ, **the plan wins** — the Concurrency, Receive-transaction, Journal-rotation, Lock-model, and Detector sections were amended across Gate-1 iterations 1–5 and are specified there in full.
  4990	     4	
  4991	     5	## Language and tooling
  4992	     6	
  4993	     7	Plain ESM JavaScript (`.mjs`) with JSDoc types, checked by `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` (dev-only). No build step: hooks invoke source directly. Zero runtime dependencies; strict spec-based flag parsing (`parseFlagsStrict` in commands/shared.mjs — unknown flags, stray positionals, and missing string-flag values are exit-2 usage errors, so a garbled safety flag can never silently lose intent); `node:test` with a small golden-file helper (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm test` regenerates). Node >= 20.
  4994	     8	
  4995	     9	Testability backbone: every command's `run()` takes an injected `io` object — `{ cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now }`. Pure logic (reducers, renderers, resolvers, classifiers) takes plain data and returns plain data. Unit tests run over an in-memory fs fake (`tests/helpers/memfs.mjs`); a thin integration layer uses `fs.mkdtemp` on the real fs.

  5040	    54	## Bundle schema (`baton/bundle@1`)
  5041	    55	
  5042	    56	`bundle.json` fields: `schema`, `bundleId`, `generation`, `createdAt/updatedAt`, `origin {platform, model, sessionHint, unstable}`, `task {goal, constraints[], acceptance[]}`, `plan.steps[] {id, title, status: pending|active|done|blocked, note}`, `decisions[] {seq, ts, summary, detail(capped)}`, `files {touched[] {path, op, lastTs}, truncated}`, `roles.assignments`, `git {branch, headSha, dirty, dirtySummary[], contentDigest, summaryTruncated} | null`, `handoff {status: open|sealed|received, reason, reasonClass, toPlatformHint, finalizedAt, receive_log[]}`, `journalSeq`, `compaction {droppedDecisions, note}`, `dedupeRing: string[]` (merge idempotency ring, capped 500, oldest evicted), transcript field (opt-in, redacted).
  5043	    57	
  5044	    58	`journal.ndjson` entry: `{seq, ts, type, dedupeKey, writerId, source, payload}`. Types: `decision | plan.set | plan.step | file.touch | note | roles.remap | task.update | git.update`. Every type is self-applicable for replay over `emptyBundle()`.
  5045	    59	
  5046	    60	Size budget (pure `compact.mjs`): decisions capped first-20 + last-150 + marker; `detail` <= 2000 chars; `files.touched` <= 300 (LRU by `lastTs`, sets `files.truncated: true`); `git.dirtySummary` <= 100 lines (sets `git.summaryTruncated: true`; skipped when `git` is null). Deterministic truncation only — no LLM summarization.
  5047	    61	
  5048	    62	## Module APIs
  5049	    63	
  5050	    64	```js
  5051	    65	// bundle/schema.mjs
  5052	    66	emptyBundle({platform, model, goal}, nowIso) -> Bundle
  5053	    67	validateBundle(obj) -> {ok, errors: [{path, msg}]}    // hand-rolled, no deps
  5054	    68	migrate(obj) -> Bundle                                 // identity in v1
  5055	    69	
  5056	    70	// bundle/store.mjs  (all take io)
  5057	    71	bundlePaths(root) -> {dir, snapshot, bak, journal, handoffMd, historyDir, lockDir, logDir}
  5058	    72	loadBundle(root, io) -> {bundle, warnings[]}           // snapshot + replay + recovery
  5059	    73	writeSnapshot(root, bundle, io) -> void                // bak -> tmp -> rename, under lock
  5060	    74	appendJournal(root, entry, io) -> seq                  // seq allocated under lock
  5061	    75	rotateJournal(root, kind, io) -> historyPath           // marker-based, crash-safe (plan §rotation)
  5062	    76	
  5063	    77	// bundle/lock.mjs — operation-scoped; see plan §Lock model for takeover rules
  5064	    78	withLock(root, io, fn) -> result                       // acquire -> fn -> release
  5065	    79	recoverLock(root, io, {force}) -> {recovered, refusedReason}
  5066	    80	
  5067	    81	// bundle/merge.mjs (pure)
  5068	    82	applyEvent(bundle, event) -> Bundle                    // idempotent via dedupeKey ring (500)
  5069	    83	
  5070	    84	// bundle/normalize.mjs
  5071	    85	normalizeHookPayload(raw, platform) -> Event[]         // never throws; unknowns -> note
  5072	    86	
  5073	    87	// bundle/render.mjs (pure)
  5074	    88	renderHandoffMd(bundle) -> string                      // golden-tested, no AI-credit strings
  5075	    89	
  5076	    90	// detect/
  5077	    91	loadSignatures({builtinPath, overlayPath}, io) -> Table // validates, lints regexes
  5078	    92	classify({text, exitCode, platform, table, structured}) ->
  5079	    93	  {class, signatureId, confidence, resetHint, tried?}   // exit-code rule: plan §detector
  5080	    94	
  5081	    95	// roles/
  5082	    96	loadConfig(cwd, io) -> {config, errors[]}
  5083	    97	resolveRoles({config, to, avoid, nativeOnly, probes}) ->
  5084	    98	  {assignments: {[role]: {platform, model, mode, chainIndex, skipped[]}}, notes[]}
  5085	    99	
  5086	   100	// receive/txn.mjs — see plan §Concurrency for full transition semantics
  5087	   101	prepare(root, {platform, origin, reason}, io) -> {token, prompt, assignments, warnings[]}
  5088	   102	commit(root, token, io) -> {adopted, generation, archivedTo}   // rejects bound-input drift
  5089	   103	
  5090	   104	// scaffold/
  5091	   105	planInit(cwd, opts, io) -> Action[]                    // {path, kind, reason, preview}
  5092	   106	applyActions(actions, io) -> Applied[]
  5093	   107	mergeAttribution(existingJsonText|null, {force}) -> {text, changed, warnings} | {error}
  5094	   108	
  5095	   109	// git/
  5096	   110	snapshot({execFile, cwd}) -> {branch, headSha, dirty, dirtySummary, contentDigest} // 5s timeout
  5097	   111	scanCommitsForAiTrailers({execFile, cwd, limit: 50}) -> [{sha, line, pattern}]
  5098	   112	```
  5099	   113	
  5100	   114	## Per-module test lists
  5101	   115	
  5102	   116	- **fsx**: atomic write visible-only-after-rename; `.bak` rotation; leftover `.tmp` ignored/cleaned; `safeReadJson` on garbage; Windows rename-retry (EPERM).
  5103	   117	- **jsonl/ids**: append+read roundtrip; torn last line dropped with warning; seq monotonic; dedupeKey stable across key order.
  5104	   118	- **schema**: empty bundle validates; pathed error per missing field; unknown fields tolerated; `@2` rejected by migrate.
  5105	   119	- **merge**: each event type mutates its section; double-apply = identical bundle; unknown type degrades to note; seq ordering.
  5106	   120	- **compact**: over-budget collapse deterministic (byte-identical); under-budget identity; truncation markers.
  5107	   121	- **store**: snapshot+replay equals pure reduction; corrupt snapshot -> `.bak` recovery; both corrupt -> journal rebuild; torn tail; marker-based rotation roll-forward/back; kill-mid-write sim.
  5108	   122	- **lock**: mutual exclusion; provably-dead takeover; live same-host owner refused (incl. `--force`); torn metadata refused; pause-after-final-fence-check; crash between creation and metadata publication.
  5109	   123	- **normalize**: `baton/event@1` passthrough; per-harness fixture extraction (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor payloads); malformed-input fuzz never throws.
  5110	   124	- **render / receive-prompt**: goldens (minimal, mid-session, finalized, stale, degraded-role); char caps; attribution invariant; determinism.
  5111	   125	- **signatures/classifier**: verbatim positive fixtures per platform; negative/near-miss corpus; ANSI stripping; precedence; reset-hint extraction; exit-code interplay matrix; non-limit failing-process fixtures; overlay override; bad-regex rejection; time guard.
  5112	   126	- **matrix/resolve**: config validation (pathed errors); chain walking with avoid/disabled/rate-limited skips; native/delegated/forced-default/unavailable; probe-eligibility rules; determinism.
  5113	   127	- **txn**: token binds journalSeq + intake + config digest + session + probe snapshot + content-sensitive git digest; one rejection test per bound input; `sealed->received` and `open->received` (degraded seal); ownership adoption + new generation; chained A->B->C; competing receivers; double-commit.
  5114	   128	- **scaffold**: gitignore variants (covering pattern no-op, CRLF, trailing newline, idempotent double-run); managed-block replace/append/corrupt-marker-refuse with outside-bytes invariance; attribution merge (absent/present/non-empty/malformed-refuse); `--dry-run` zero writes; real-fs `mkdtemp` + `git init` integration.
  5115	   129	- **git**: snapshot on clean/dirty/detached/not-a-repo/timeout; guard trailer fixtures incl. word-boundary false-positive ("Claudette Smith" not flagged).
  5116	   130	- **doctor**: check aggregation; `--strict` exit; probe states; version floors; network-FS warning.
  5117	   131	- **purge-transcript**: whole-tree secret removal (snapshot, bak, journal, history, log); interruption resume via marker; packaged-bin invocation.
  5118	   132	- **invariants**: no AI-credit strings in any rendered output, golden, or template.
  5119	   133	- **integration**: e2e failover (init -> 25 checkpoints -> kill-mid-write -> finalize usage-limit -> receive on second platform -> golden prompt); chained A->B->C; six-direction contract matrix; cli-spawn exit codes and `--json` stdout purity.
  5120	   134	
  5121	   135	## CLI contract
  5122	   136	
  5123	   137	Commands: `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover`, `session-start`. Exit codes: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json`: exactly one `{ok, data, warnings, error}` envelope on stdout, diagnostics on stderr. Checkpoint soft-fails to exit 0 in hook contexts (`--strict` opts out). `session-start` is the cheap adapter SessionStart gate: soft paths always exit 0 and its BARE stdout is harness-shaped context (not an envelope); with `--json` it honors the envelope contract (`data: {pending, shaped}`). `wrap` is reserved, not implemented in v1.

  5138	    11	## Claude Code
  5139	    12	
  5140	    13	- Hook events include `Stop`, `StopFailure`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `SessionStart`, `SessionEnd`, `PostToolUseFailure`, and others.
  5141	    14	- **`StopFailure`** fires when a turn ends due to an API error; output and exit code are ignored (observability-only). Matcher filters by error type. **Enum snapshot (2026-07-11, code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks):** `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`, `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `billing_error`, `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `unknown`. Note: a Gate-1 reviewer disputed `overloaded`'s presence in the current enum — fixtures are generated from this snapshot and unknown values normalize to `unknown`, so drift is safe either way. Re-snapshot before freezing fixtures.
  5142	    15	- Limit strings (fallback tier): `You've hit your session limit · resets …` / `weekly limit` / `Opus limit`; throttle: `Server is temporarily limiting requests (not your usage limit)`; `API Error: Request rejected (429)`.
  5143	    16	- **Live capture (2026-07-12, this machine)**: a subagent died with `Agent terminated early due to an API error: You've hit your session limit · resets 2am (Asia/Dubai)` — reset hints can carry a timezone suffix in parentheses; the resetHint extractor and fixtures must cover this variant.
  5144	    17	- Attribution: `"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}` in settings.json (`includeCoAuthoredBy` is deprecated).
  5145	    18	
  5146	    19	## Codex CLI (>= 0.144; this machine: 0.144.1)
  5147	    20	
  5148	    21	- Lifecycle hooks: `SessionStart`, `SubagentStart`, `PreToolUse`, `PermissionRequest`, `PostToolUse`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `SubagentStop`, `Stop`. Config: `~/.codex/hooks.json`, `<repo>/.codex/hooks.json`, or config.toml `[hooks]` tables. Payload: stdin JSON with `session_id`, `cwd`, `hook_event_name`, `model`, `transcript_path` (+ `turn_id` for turn-scoped).

  5597	     3	 * transform: a covering non-comment line ('.handoff/' or '.handoff') makes
  5598	     4	 * this a byte-for-byte no-op; otherwise the pattern is appended on its own
  5599	     5	 * line with a single trailing newline.
  5600	     6	 * @param {string | null} existingText current .gitignore body, or null when absent
  5601	     7	 * @param {string} pattern the ignore entry to guarantee (e.g. '.handoff/')
  5602	     8	 * @returns {{text: string, changed: boolean}}
  5603	     9	 */
  5604	    10	export function ensureIgnoreLine(existingText, pattern) {
  5605	    11	  const body = existingText ?? '';
  5606	    12	  const bare = pattern.endsWith('/') ? pattern.slice(0, -1) : pattern;
  5607	    13	  const covers = body
  5608	    14	    .split(/\r?\n/)
  5609	    15	    .map((l) => l.trim())
  5610	    16	    .some((l) => l === pattern || l === bare);
  5611	    17	  if (covers) return { text: body, changed: false };
  5612	    18	
  5613	    19	  if (body === '') return { text: pattern + '\n', changed: true };
  5614	    20	  const joined = body.endsWith('\n') ? body : body + '\n';
  5615	    21	  return { text: joined + pattern + '\n', changed: true };
  5616	    22	}

  6044	     9	
  6045	    10	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  6046	    11	// Contract choices for core/src/receive/txn.mjs (docs/design/core.md §Module APIs
  6047	    12	// prepare/commit; §Per-module test lists "txn"; plan §Concurrency — the receive
  6048	    13	// prepare/commit two-phase transaction, receipt-token bindings incl. the
  6049	    14	// content-sensitive git digest, open->received degraded seal, ownership adoption +
  6050	    15	// new generation, chained failover, competing receivers, double-commit).
  6051	    16	//
  6052	    17	// SIGNATURES (pinned — the task overrides core.md's 3-arg commit):
  6053	    18	//   prepare(root, opts, io) -> { token, prompt, assignments, warnings }
  6054	    19	//   commit(root, token, opts, io) -> { adopted, generation, archivedTo }
  6055	    20	//   Both are SYNCHRONOUS. The plan pins that the receive COMMAND wires
  6056	    21	//   core/src/git/snapshot.mjs in and passes the result as opts.gitSnapshot; txn
  6057	    22	//   itself never spawns git — it takes the snapshot as plain data.
  6058	    23	//
  6059	    24	//   opts (same shape for prepare and commit):
  6060	    25	//     { platform,       // destination harness we are resuming ON (e.g. 'codex')
  6061	    26	//       origin,         // intake: the harness handed off FROM (e.g. 'claude-code')
  6062	    27	//       reason,         // intake: why the switch happened (free text)
  6063	    28	//       gitSnapshot,    // the caller-computed git snapshot object (git/snapshot.mjs)
  6064	    29	//       probes,         // optional probe map for resolveRoles (default null)
  6065	    30	//       sessionHint }   // the RECEIVING session's hint, used for ownership adoption
  6066	    31	//
  6067	    32	// TOKEN BINDING (THE pin). prepare captures a REVISION FINGERPRINT and returns it
  6068	    33	//   as an opaque token. It binds every one of these inputs (one rejection test per
  6069	    34	//   input below — verifier fold F3 completed the set):
  6070	    35	//     - bundle REVISION: generation + journalSeq (as loadBundle reports them)
  6071	    36	//     - intake: origin + reason
  6072	    37	//     - config digest: a hash of the baton.config.json bytes at <root>
  6073	    38	//     - GIT digest: a hash of the WHOLE opts.gitSnapshot object (PIN — the git
  6074	    39	//       state is bound by hashing the caller-passed object, so headSha, dirty,
  6075	    40	//       AND contentDigest are each binding: a HEAD move with an UNCHANGED
  6076	    41	//       contentDigest still drifts the token, and vice versa)
  6077	    42	//     - probe snapshot: a hash of opts.probes
  6078	    43	//     - target platform (opts.platform)
  6079	    44	//     - receiving session (opts.sessionHint) — plan: the token binds "target
  6080	    45	//       platform+session"
  6081	    46	//   prepare mutates NOTHING (it cannot persist a "prepared" record — the token is
  6082	    47	//   self-contained). commit RE-DERIVES every bound input from current disk state +
  6083	    48	//   its own opts and compares to the token; ANY drift throws an Error whose message
  6084	    49	//   names re-prepare (matches /re-?prepare/i) and performs NO mutation (the
  6085	    50	//   .handoff tree is byte-identical before and after the rejected commit). Because
  6086	    51	//   a successful commit bumps `generation`, an already-spent token (double-commit)
  6087	    52	//   and a losing competitor's token (competing receivers) both fail the revision
  6088	    53	//   check with no extra bookkeeping.
  6089	    54	//
  6090	    55	// COMMIT SUCCESS (one atomic transition):
  6091	    56	//   - Archives the current bundle to history/ via rotateJournal kind 'receive'
  6092	    57	//     (a history/<stem>.receive.json + .ndjson pair). archivedTo === that stem.
  6093	    58	//     The archived .receive freeze is the RECEIVED seal (handoff.status
  6094	    59	//     'received' — asserted on BOTH the sealed and open paths, verifier fold F7:
  6095	    60	//     archiving the pre-commit sealed bundle unchanged would be wrong); it
  6096	    61	//     retains the receipt data (the receive_log entry for THIS receive rides in
  6097	    62	//     the archived freeze). For an OPEN source bundle it is the receive-generated
  6098	    63	//     DEGRADED seal (handoff.reason from intake, reasonClass classified from the
  6099	    64	//     reason text against the intake ORIGIN platform via the built-in signature
  6100	    65	//     table); for a SEALED source the finalize reason/reasonClass are retained.
  6101	    66	//   - Adopts ownership: origin becomes the RECEIVING side — origin.platform ===
  6102	    67	//     opts.platform, origin.sessionHint === opts.sessionHint.
  6103	    68	//   - Opens a fresh writable generation: generation + 1, handoff.status 'open'.
  6104	    69	//   - Appends a receive_log entry { origin, reason, at }; for the OPEN (degraded)
  6105	    70	//     path the entry additionally carries degradedSeal: true (PIN: that flag lives
  6106	    71	//     on the receive_log entry). The sealed path's entry has NO truthy degradedSeal.
  6107	    72	//   - Returns { adopted: <truthy>, generation: <new gen>, archivedTo: <stem> }.
  6108	    73	//
  6109	    74	// STALENESS (prepare warnings, plan §Receive): OPEN source bundle -> a warning
  6110	    75	//   notes the missing seal; age > 12h (now - finalizedAt), HEAD moved
  6111	    76	//   (bundle.git.headSha !== opts.gitSnapshot.headSha), and a dirty mismatch each
  6112	    77	//   add a warning. Asserted as substring matches, not byte-exact strings.
  6113	    78	//
  6114	    79	// All txn tests seed: the bundle, baton.config.json at <root>, AND the built-in
  6115	    80	// signature table at its module-resolved path (loadSignatures reads via io.fs), so
  6116	    81	// role resolution and reasonClass classification both work over memfs.
