  1416	   295	     5	## Context
  1417	   296	     6	
  1418	   297	     7	Saksham's AI-coding workflow spans three harnesses — Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, and Cursor — and breaks whenever one platform's usage limits run out mid-task. Work state, plan context, and the writer/reviewer role assignments are trapped in the dying session. His handwritten notes describe a three-layer system (ideal-loop creator with smoke-test gate; dual-worktree adversarial write/review pipeline; cross-platform workflow portability). **Milestone 1 (this plan): the cross-platform failover layer** — chosen by Saksham as the foundation, since it addresses the stated pain point and the other layers run on top of it.
  1419	   298	     8	
  1420	   299	     9	Research confirmed the white space: Databricks' Omnigent (June 2026) is the closest analog but replaces native configs with its own YAML and ships **no usage-limit failover**; nothing else does harness-level failover either (closest is model-level switching). The portability standards to build on already exist: AGENTS.md (Linux Foundation/AAIF-governed; native in Codex + Cursor; bridged into Claude Code via an `@AGENTS.md` import in CLAUDE.md) and the Agent Skills standard (SKILL.md; native in Claude Code + Codex).
  1421	   300	    10	
  1422	   301	    11	## Locked decisions (from Saksham, this session)
  1423	   302	    12	
  1424	   303	    13	1. **First milestone**: cross-platform failover layer. Loop-creator and dual-worktree pipelines are later milestones; leave seams.
  1425	   304	    14	2. **Capture**: continuous checkpointing via harness hooks **plus** an explicit `/handoff` finalize command that records reason-for-switching.
  1426	   305	    15	3. **Platforms**: all three from v1. Claude Code gets the deep integration (plugin with hooks); Codex and Cursor get lighter native adapters.
  1427	   306	    16	4. **Receive flow**: intake (original platform + reason) → load bundle → role-matrix remap → auto-continue the task.
  1428	   307	    17	5. **Bundle home**: gitignored `.handoff/` directory inside the repo.
  1429	   308	    18	6. **Architecture**: one repo — harness-agnostic core Node CLI + three native adapters + templates + tests.
  1430	   309	    19	7. **Attribution (hard invariant)**: ZERO AI mentions in git history — no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated with Claude Code" — permanently. During initial construction (pre-v1), all commits are authored solely by `SakshamUboweja <ssakshamu@gmail.com>` with frequent, regular commits to main (contributions accrue to his GitHub profile); external human OSS contributors are welcome post-v1. Enforced via `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` in Claude Code settings (the old `includeCoAuthoredBy` boolean is deprecated) + a doctor check.
  1431	   310	    20	8. **AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md**: the tool scaffolds an ideal pair into any project (this repo dogfoods them). Design grounded in the official Fable 5 and GPT 5.6 prompting guides (fetched; distilled below). Strongest models get latitude on the design.
  1432	   311	    21	9. **Development methodology** (governs building this repo AND is encoded in the templates as the product's workflow):
  1433	   312	    22	   - Fable 5 writes the plan doc → **GPT 5.6 Sol xhigh reviews it (Gate 1)**.
  1434	   313	    23	   - Decompose into tasks/subtasks.
  1435	   314	    24	   - Per subtask: **Opus 4.8 writes unit tests first, GPT 5.5 xhigh verifies the tests**; the two keep each other in line during implementation.
  1436	   315	    25	   - At the end: **GPT 5.6 Sol xhigh and Fable 5 xhigh run independent reviews**; feedback is collated and implemented.
  1437	   316	    26	   - Overall: a goal with genuine constraints, looped until the constraints are met. Review artifacts under `reviews/<task-id>/` with verdicts `{APPROVED, APPROVED_WITH_NOTES, BLOCKED}` (pattern from Saksham's wt-* repos).
  1438	   317	    27	
  1439	   318	    28	## Research findings that shape the design (verified 2026-07-11)
  1440	   319	    29	
  1441	   320	    30	- **Codex plugin (installed, v1.0.4) is the implementation pattern**: single Node entrypoint invoked as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<x>.mjs" <subcmd>`; hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop) read event JSON on stdin and can emit `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; commands/agents/skills as markdown with frontmatter; per-workspace state dir; structured-output JSON schemas for reviews. It has **no usage-limit handling** — our failover logic is net-new.
  1442	   321	    31	- **Superpowers plugin (installed) is the cross-harness packaging pattern**: one repo ships `hooks/hooks.json` (Claude) + `hooks-cursor.json` (Cursor, camelCase events), a polyglot `run-hook.cmd`, and `.codex-plugin` / `.cursor-plugin` / `AGENTS.md` descriptors. Hook output differs per harness (Claude: `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`; Cursor: `additional_context`) — branch on `$CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT`.
  1443	   322	    32	- **Limit-detection signals** (Gate-1 verified, 2026-07-11): structured signals FIRST, text signatures as fallback tier.
  1444	   323	    33	  - Claude Code: **`StopFailure` hook event** fires when a turn ends on an API error, with matcher filtering by error type (`rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `billing_error`, `server_error`, …) — the primary, structured limit-death signal. Output/exit code ignored (observability-only), so a checkpoint there is safe by construction. Text fallback: the stable strings `You've hit your session limit · resets …` / `weekly limit` / `Opus limit`.
  1445	   324	    34	  - Codex (>= 0.144): **lifecycle hooks exist** (`SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `SubagentStop`, `Stop`; configured via `~/.codex/hooks.json`, `<repo>/.codex/hooks.json`, or config.toml `[hooks]`; stdin JSON with `session_id`, `cwd`, `model`, `transcript_path`). No StopFailure equivalent → limit death bounded by last Stop checkpoint. Text fallback: `You've hit your usage limit…`; `codex exec --json` exits non-zero.
  1446	   325	    35	  - Cursor: weakest — BYO-key returns `{"error":"Too Many Requests", …}`; managed-billing schema undocumented. Heuristics + timeouts, `confidence: low`.
  1447	   326	    36	- **Session handoff prior art**: HANDOFF.md markdown is the accepted lossy-universal mechanism; schema-level session transplants (authsec-bridge) are brittle — v1 stays markdown+JSON, no session-file surgery.
  1448	   327	    37	- **Local surfaces available on this machine**: `codex` CLI (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh) with empty-but-supported `~/.codex/prompts/`; `cursor-agent` CLI (reads AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md natively); `.agents/skills` is the official Codex skills path; Cursor project hooks via `.cursor/hooks.json` (onPreEdit/onPostEdit/onPreCommit/onApprove).
  1449	   328	    38	- **Running the methodology's models from Claude Code**: Agent tool model overrides (opus/fable) + codex companion (`… codex-companion.mjs task --model gpt-5.6-sol|gpt-5.5 --effort xhigh`, read-only sandbox, structured output).
  1450	   329	    39	
  1451	   330	    40	## Prompting-guide distillation (for the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md templates)
  1452	   331	    41	
  1453	   332	    42	- **Fable 5** (platform.claude.com guide): strong instruction-following — brief steering beats enumeration; state boundaries (pause only for destructive/irreversible/scope-change/user-only input); "when you have enough information to act, act"; audit progress claims against tool evidence; parallel subagents with async communication; provide a memory/notes location; fresh-context verifier subagents beat self-critique; over-prescriptive skills degrade output; never instruct reasoning echo (triggers refusals).
  1454	   333	    43	- **GPT 5.6** (developers.openai.com guide): hierarchy Role → Goal → Success criteria → Constraints → Tools → Stop rules; outcome definition over process prescription; trimming repeated rules improved evals 10–15% and cut tokens 41–66%; ALWAYS/NEVER only for true invariants; state each policy once; name the current phase for long work; explicit validation guidance; avoid contradictions, universal defaults, blanket brevity, personality words.
  1455	   334	    44	- **Template consequence**: shared invariants live exactly once in AGENTS.md (lean, hierarchical); CLAUDE.md is an `@AGENTS.md` import plus a short Claude-specific block (memory location, subagent guidance); any Codex-specific steering gets its own clearly-scoped short section.
  1456	   335	    45	
  1457	   336	    46	## Design
  1458	   337	    47	
  1459	   338	    48	_(Sections below synthesized from two Plan-agent designs — core engine; adapters/templates/methodology — merged after Gate-1 review.)_
  1460	   339	    49	
  1461	   340	    50	### Core engine (`core/`)
  1462	   341	    51	
  1463	   342	    52	**Language/tooling**: plain ESM JavaScript (`.mjs`) + JSDoc types checked by `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` (dev-only dep). No build step — hooks invoke source directly (`node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…"`), same as the proven codex plugin. **Zero runtime dependencies**; arg parsing via `node:util` `parseArgs`; **`node:test`** as the framework (golden-file helper ~40 lines with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`). Node >= 20. Every command's `run()` takes an injected `io` object (`{cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now}`); pure logic (reducers/renderers/resolvers/classifiers) is data-in/data-out; tests run over an in-memory fs fake plus a thin real-fs integration layer.
  1464	   343	    53	
  1465	   344	    54	**CLI surface** (`baton <cmd> --json`): `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover` (forced lock recovery). Frozen exit-code contract: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json` mode prints exactly one envelope `{ok, data, warnings, error}` on stdout. `baton wrap -- <cmd>` (PTY supervisor) is **deferred post-v1** — hook-driven detection suffices; the name/contract is reserved.
  1466	   345	    55	
  1467	   346	    56	**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
  1468	   347	    57	
  1469	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
  1470	   349	    59	
  1471	   350	    60	**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker. On load, a present marker deterministically rolls the rotation forward (if the snapshot landed) or back (if not); the same marker pattern governs interrupted forced takeovers and interrupted purges (purge resumes from its marker until the whole tree is clean). Retention: last 10 rotations pruned with the history. Doctor warns at journal > 5 MB; perf test: 10k-event replay < 1 s. **Filesystem support boundary: v1 supports local filesystems only** — lock and rename atomicity are not guaranteed on network/shared mounts (NFS/SMB/cloud-sync folders); doctor detects and warns, README states it.
  1472	   351	    61	
  1473	   352	    62	**Root discovery & degraded modes** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): repo root = nearest ancestor containing `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree-aware: linked worktrees resolve to their own toplevel, shared state stays per-worktree), else cwd — `--root <path>` overrides; nested/monorepo launches therefore resolve to the same bundle deterministically, but **discovery never crosses the boundary of a nested independent git repository** (a `.git` between cwd and a candidate root stops the walk) unless `--root` says otherwise. Non-git directories: supported — `git` section is null, git-dependent features degrade with explicit warnings. Read-only sandboxes (EACCES/EROFS on `.handoff/`): checkpoint fails open with a warning naming the user-executed fallback (`baton checkpoint` run manually outside the sandbox; `receive --print-prompt` never needs writes until `--commit`). All git invocations carry a 5 s timeout (configurable); timeout → git section marked `unavailable`, never a hang.
  1474	   353	    63	
  1475	   354	    64	**Transcript policy** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): transcript-tail capture at PreCompact is **opt-in and off by default** (`capture.transcriptTail` in `baton.config.json`), bounded (last 10 messages, 8 KB cap), passed through a secret-redaction filter (common credential/token patterns; fixtures with planted secrets prove redaction), stored in a dedicated bundle field excluded from HANDOFF.md by default. `baton purge-transcript` removes the field from **every retained copy** — active snapshot, `.bak`, journal (rewrite-and-rotate under lock), and all `history/` freezes — with a test asserting planted secrets are absent from the entire `.handoff/` tree afterward. **Diagnostics logging contract (iteration 4)**: `.handoff/log/` entries are metadata-only and redacted — raw hook payloads never enter them (fixture-proven) — with bounded retention (last 50 entries / 7 days) and inclusion in the whole-tree purge test.
  1476	   355	    65	
  1477	   356	    66	**Checkpoint engine**: adapters send pre-normalized `baton/event@1` on stdin (the real API); raw hook payloads get best-effort per-platform extraction (`normalize.mjs`) that never throws — unknowns degrade to `note` events. Idempotent via dedupe keys; journal append always, snapshot rewrite throttled (≥10 events / 30 s / important event types). **Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on all soft failures** so a checkpoint can never break the host harness (`--strict` for CI). `finalize --reason "…" [--reason-class] [--to]` records the switch reason (class inferred from text via the classifier when omitted), refreshes git state, freezes history.
  1478	   357	    67	
  1479	   358	    68	**Limit detector**: two tiers — **structured signals first** (Claude Code `StopFailure` matcher error types; documented limit-specific fields in codex JSON output), text signatures as fallback. **Exit-code rule (iteration 3): a generic nonzero exit never classifies as usage-limit on its own** — exit 10 requires limit-specific structured or text evidence; nonzero without evidence = `other-error`. Fixture corpus includes non-limit failing processes. Signatures are **versioned data** (`core/data/signatures.v1.json`), seeded with the verified strings for all three platforms, matcher kinds `substring`/`regex`/`json-field`, per-signature confidence, precedence usage-limit > auth > throttle > other-error, `--signatures <path>` overlay for hot-patching drift, `--explain` for auditability. Hardening (Gate-1 additions): input is ANSI-stripped before matching; the fixture corpus includes negative/near-miss cases (throttle-vs-usage confusables, multiline, malformed JSON, localized text) so false positives are regression-tested; overlay regexes are lint-checked (length cap, no backreferences, linear-time constructs) and matching carries a time guard; a low-confidence match **never silently avoids a platform** — it warns and defers to user intake at receive. Cursor entries carry `confidence: low|medium` explicitly.
  1480	   359	    69	
  1481	   360	    70	**Role matrix**: committed `baton.config.json` at repo root (`baton/config@1`) mapping roles → ordered platform+model chains (the seven methodology roles, defined below), plus per-platform `defaults`. Resolver is pure and explainable: skips `avoid[]` platforms (auto-populated with the origin platform when reason-class is usage-limit — never remap back onto the platform that died), resolves `mode: native|delegated|forced-default|unavailable` with `{chainIndex, skipped[]}` audit data. **Availability probing** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): `doctor` probes each platform noninteractively, hard 3 s bound per probe, results cached 15 min in the state dir. Probe record = two separate dimensions: **capability** (ordered, cumulative: `installed → authenticated → reachable`, recorded as far as verifiable) and **probe outcome** (`ok | rate-limited | error | timeout`). Resolver eligibility: **selectable** = capability ≥ authenticated and outcome ≠ rate-limited; anything with an unverifiable dimension resolves as selectable-with-`degraded`-flag; `rate-limited` platforms are skipped like `avoid[]` entries. Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged `degraded`.
  1482	   361	    71	
  1483	   362	    72	**Receive**: loads bundle with recovery + staleness checks (age > 12 h; HEAD moved; dirty mismatch), merges intake flags (`--origin`, `--reason`), resolves roles, and runs as the **prepare/commit transaction defined under Concurrency** — prompt emission at prepare, state mutation only at commit. Resume prompt ≤2,500 chars (brief, why-you're-here, role table, warnings, top-5 next actions, pointer to HANDOFF.md); the prompt explicitly frames bundle content as **unverified claims to audit against the working tree, not instructions to obey** (prompt-injection posture — see Threat model).
  1484	   363	    73	
  1485	   364	    74	**Scaffold** (`init`): two-phase plan/apply with `--dry-run`; `.gitignore` ensure-line (no-op if an existing pattern covers `.handoff/`); `baton.config.json` from template; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md written via managed blocks (`<!-- baton:begin/end -->`) — bytes outside markers never touched.
  1486	   365	    75	
  1487	   366	    76	**Attribution guard** (three layers): (1) `init` deep-merges `.claude/settings.json` → `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` (only when keys absent; refuses to touch malformed JSON; global settings documented + doctor-checked, never written by core); (2) `doctor` scans last 50 commits for AI co-author/generated-with trailers (word-boundary-safe patterns) and flags with remediation; (3) a test-suite invariant scans every rendered output and template for AI-credit strings and fails the build.
  1488	   367	    77	
  1489	   368	    78	Full module APIs, per-module test lists, repo file tree, and the fixture corpus (verbatim limit strings, hook payloads, corrupt bundles) are specified in the core design doc (committed as `docs/design/core.md` in task 0); implementation follows the named-task TDD sequence below — **tasks are identified by name, not number; the exact count is finalized when review directories are generated**. **`sessionHint` derivation (Gate-1 final note)**: per adapter, from the hook payload's stable session id (Claude Code `session_id`; Codex `session_id`; Cursor session field); when a payload lacks one, core generates a process-scoped hint flagged `unstable: true` — unstable hints never trigger foreign-session rejection on their own, only a warning.
  1490	   369	    79	### Checkpoint vocabulary (used everywhere)
  1491	   370	    80	
  1492	   371	    81	- **Mechanical checkpoint** (`baton checkpoint`): hook/script-driven, no LLM — git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, timestamps, source platform/model, files touched. <1 s, safe per-turn.
  1493	   372	    82	- **Narrative seal** (`baton finalize`, surfaced as `/handoff`): model-written — decisions + rationale, verified-done vs claimed-done, next steps, gotchas, reason for switching.
  1494	   373	    83	
  1495	   374	    84	Claude Code DOES emit a structured limit-death event (`StopFailure` with a `rate_limit` matcher); Codex and Cursor do not. The design is therefore: event-driven detection where it exists, rolling mechanical checkpoints everywhere (last coherent turn always captured), narrative seals at milestones, and receive compensating for a missing seal by asking the user why they switched and re-deriving git facts live, auditing HANDOFF.md claims against them.

  1668	   547	 succeeded in 0ms:
  1669	   548	    50	### Core engine (`core/`)
  1670	   549	    51	
  1671	   550	    52	**Language/tooling**: plain ESM JavaScript (`.mjs`) + JSDoc types checked by `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` (dev-only dep). No build step — hooks invoke source directly (`node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…"`), same as the proven codex plugin. **Zero runtime dependencies**; arg parsing via `node:util` `parseArgs`; **`node:test`** as the framework (golden-file helper ~40 lines with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`). Node >= 20. Every command's `run()` takes an injected `io` object (`{cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now}`); pure logic (reducers/renderers/resolvers/classifiers) is data-in/data-out; tests run over an in-memory fs fake plus a thin real-fs integration layer.
  1672	   551	    53	
  1673	   552	    54	**CLI surface** (`baton <cmd> --json`): `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover` (forced lock recovery). Frozen exit-code contract: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json` mode prints exactly one envelope `{ok, data, warnings, error}` on stdout. `baton wrap -- <cmd>` (PTY supervisor) is **deferred post-v1** — hook-driven detection suffices; the name/contract is reserved.
  1674	   553	    55	
  1675	   554	    56	**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
  1676	   555	    57	
  1677	   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
  1678	   557	    59	
  1679	   558	    60	**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker. On load, a present marker deterministically rolls the rotation forward (if the snapshot landed) or back (if not); the same marker pattern governs interrupted forced takeovers and interrupted purges (purge resumes from its marker until the whole tree is clean). Retention: last 10 rotations pruned with the history. Doctor warns at journal > 5 MB; perf test: 10k-event replay < 1 s. **Filesystem support boundary: v1 supports local filesystems only** — lock and rename atomicity are not guaranteed on network/shared mounts (NFS/SMB/cloud-sync folders); doctor detects and warns, README states it.
  1680	   559	    61	
  1681	   560	    62	**Root discovery & degraded modes** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): repo root = nearest ancestor containing `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree-aware: linked worktrees resolve to their own toplevel, shared state stays per-worktree), else cwd — `--root <path>` overrides; nested/monorepo launches therefore resolve to the same bundle deterministically, but **discovery never crosses the boundary of a nested independent git repository** (a `.git` between cwd and a candidate root stops the walk) unless `--root` says otherwise. Non-git directories: supported — `git` section is null, git-dependent features degrade with explicit warnings. Read-only sandboxes (EACCES/EROFS on `.handoff/`): checkpoint fails open with a warning naming the user-executed fallback (`baton checkpoint` run manually outside the sandbox; `receive --print-prompt` never needs writes until `--commit`). All git invocations carry a 5 s timeout (configurable); timeout → git section marked `unavailable`, never a hang.
  1682	   561	    63	
  1683	   562	    64	**Transcript policy** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): transcript-tail capture at PreCompact is **opt-in and off by default** (`capture.transcriptTail` in `baton.config.json`), bounded (last 10 messages, 8 KB cap), passed through a secret-redaction filter (common credential/token patterns; fixtures with planted secrets prove redaction), stored in a dedicated bundle field excluded from HANDOFF.md by default. `baton purge-transcript` removes the field from **every retained copy** — active snapshot, `.bak`, journal (rewrite-and-rotate under lock), and all `history/` freezes — with a test asserting planted secrets are absent from the entire `.handoff/` tree afterward. **Diagnostics logging contract (iteration 4)**: `.handoff/log/` entries are metadata-only and redacted — raw hook payloads never enter them (fixture-proven) — with bounded retention (last 50 entries / 7 days) and inclusion in the whole-tree purge test.
  1684	   563	    65	
  1685	   564	    66	**Checkpoint engine**: adapters send pre-normalized `baton/event@1` on stdin (the real API); raw hook payloads get best-effort per-platform extraction (`normalize.mjs`) that never throws — unknowns degrade to `note` events. Idempotent via dedupe keys; journal append always, snapshot rewrite throttled (≥10 events / 30 s / important event types). **Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on all soft failures** so a checkpoint can never break the host harness (`--strict` for CI). `finalize --reason "…" [--reason-class] [--to]` records the switch reason (class inferred from text via the classifier when omitted), refreshes git state, freezes history.
  1686	   565	    67	
  1687	   566	    68	**Limit detector**: two tiers — **structured signals first** (Claude Code `StopFailure` matcher error types; documented limit-specific fields in codex JSON output), text signatures as fallback. **Exit-code rule (iteration 3): a generic nonzero exit never classifies as usage-limit on its own** — exit 10 requires limit-specific structured or text evidence; nonzero without evidence = `other-error`. Fixture corpus includes non-limit failing processes. Signatures are **versioned data** (`core/data/signatures.v1.json`), seeded with the verified strings for all three platforms, matcher kinds `substring`/`regex`/`json-field`, per-signature confidence, precedence usage-limit > auth > throttle > other-error, `--signatures <path>` overlay for hot-patching drift, `--explain` for auditability. Hardening (Gate-1 additions): input is ANSI-stripped before matching; the fixture corpus includes negative/near-miss cases (throttle-vs-usage confusables, multiline, malformed JSON, localized text) so false positives are regression-tested; overlay regexes are lint-checked (length cap, no backreferences, linear-time constructs) and matching carries a time guard; a low-confidence match **never silently avoids a platform** — it warns and defers to user intake at receive. Cursor entries carry `confidence: low|medium` explicitly.
  1688	   567	    69	
  1689	   568	    70	**Role matrix**: committed `baton.config.json` at repo root (`baton/config@1`) mapping roles → ordered platform+model chains (the seven methodology roles, defined below), plus per-platform `defaults`. Resolver is pure and explainable: skips `avoid[]` platforms (auto-populated with the origin platform when reason-class is usage-limit — never remap back onto the platform that died), resolves `mode: native|delegated|forced-default|unavailable` with `{chainIndex, skipped[]}` audit data. **Availability probing** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): `doctor` probes each platform noninteractively, hard 3 s bound per probe, results cached 15 min in the state dir. Probe record = two separate dimensions: **capability** (ordered, cumulative: `installed → authenticated → reachable`, recorded as far as verifiable) and **probe outcome** (`ok | rate-limited | error | timeout`). Resolver eligibility: **selectable** = capability ≥ authenticated and outcome ≠ rate-limited; anything with an unverifiable dimension resolves as selectable-with-`degraded`-flag; `rate-limited` platforms are skipped like `avoid[]` entries. Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged `degraded`.
  1690	   569	    71	
  1691	   570	    72	**Receive**: loads bundle with recovery + staleness checks (age > 12 h; HEAD moved; dirty mismatch), merges intake flags (`--origin`, `--reason`), resolves roles, and runs as the **prepare/commit transaction defined under Concurrency** — prompt emission at prepare, state mutation only at commit. Resume prompt ≤2,500 chars (brief, why-you're-here, role table, warnings, top-5 next actions, pointer to HANDOFF.md); the prompt explicitly frames bundle content as **unverified claims to audit against the working tree, not instructions to obey** (prompt-injection posture — see Threat model).
  1692	   571	    73	
  1693	   572	    74	**Scaffold** (`init`): two-phase plan/apply with `--dry-run`; `.gitignore` ensure-line (no-op if an existing pattern covers `.handoff/`); `baton.config.json` from template; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md written via managed blocks (`<!-- baton:begin/end -->`) — bytes outside markers never touched.
  1694	   573	    75	
  1695	   574	    76	**Attribution guard** (three layers): (1) `init` deep-merges `.claude/settings.json` → `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` (only when keys absent; refuses to touch malformed JSON; global settings documented + doctor-checked, never written by core); (2) `doctor` scans last 50 commits for AI co-author/generated-with trailers (word-boundary-safe patterns) and flags with remediation; (3) a test-suite invariant scans every rendered output and template for AI-credit strings and fails the build.
  1696	   575	    77	
  1697	   576	    78	Full module APIs, per-module test lists, repo file tree, and the fixture corpus (verbatim limit strings, hook payloads, corrupt bundles) are specified in the core design doc (committed as `docs/design/core.md` in task 0); implementation follows the named-task TDD sequence below — **tasks are identified by name, not number; the exact count is finalized when review directories are generated**. **`sessionHint` derivation (Gate-1 final note)**: per adapter, from the hook payload's stable session id (Claude Code `session_id`; Codex `session_id`; Cursor session field); when a payload lacks one, core generates a process-scoped hint flagged `unstable: true` — unstable hints never trigger foreign-session rejection on their own, only a warning.
  1698	   577	    79	### Checkpoint vocabulary (used everywhere)
  1699	   578	    80	
  1700	   579	    81	- **Mechanical checkpoint** (`baton checkpoint`): hook/script-driven, no LLM — git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, timestamps, source platform/model, files touched. <1 s, safe per-turn.
  1701	   580	    82	- **Narrative seal** (`baton finalize`, surfaced as `/handoff`): model-written — decisions + rationale, verified-done vs claimed-done, next steps, gotchas, reason for switching.
  1702	   581	    83	
  1703	   582	    84	Claude Code DOES emit a structured limit-death event (`StopFailure` with a `rate_limit` matcher); Codex and Cursor do not. The design is therefore: event-driven detection where it exists, rolling mechanical checkpoints everywhere (last coherent turn always captured), narrative seals at milestones, and receive compensating for a missing seal by asking the user why they switched and re-deriving git facts live, auditing HANDOFF.md claims against them.

  1708	   587	    89	
  1709	   588	    90	Hooks (all fail-open — errors log to `.handoff/log/`, exit 0; a checkpoint must never break a session):
  1710	   589	    91	
  1711	   590	    92	| Event | Use | Timeout |
  1712	   591	    93	|---|---|---|
  1713	   592	    94	| `StopFailure` (matcher enum — e.g. `rate_limit`, `billing_error`, `server_error` — **snapshot verbatim from the official hooks reference during task 0**; fixtures generated from that canonical list; unknown future values normalize to `unknown` safely) | **The limit-death signal.** Classifies the error (matcher + payload through `baton detect`), writes a fail-open mechanical checkpoint stamped `trigger: stop-failure/<type>`, and on `rate_limit` marks the bundle limit-hit so the next SessionStart (any platform) surfaces it. Output/exit code are ignored by the harness — safe by construction. Tests cover the full snapshot enum. | 30 s |
  1714	   593	    95	| `Stop` | Routine mechanical checkpoint per assistant turn (proven codex stop-gate pattern; never emits `decision: block`) | 30 s |
  1715	   594	    96	| `PreCompact` | Snapshot context boundary before compaction; transcript-tail capture is **opt-in, off by default** (see core §transcript policy) | 60 s |
  1716	   595	    97	| `SessionEnd` | Clean-exit checkpoint | 30 s |
  1717	   596	    98	| `SessionStart` | Not a checkpoint: if a sealed or limit-hit bundle from another platform exists, inject "handoff pending — suggest `/baton:receive`" context | 10 s |
  1718	   597	    99	
  1719	   598	   100	`PostToolUse` rejected: per-tool-call spawns for incoherent mid-turn state; Stop gives the same worst-case staleness (one turn) at a fraction of the cost.
  1720	   599	   101	
  1721	   600	   102	Commands: **`/baton:handoff`** (model-invocable so Claude can propose it near limits; writes the narrative — auditing every "done" claim against tool evidence — then seals via finalize, then prints the destination's resume command); **`/baton:receive`** (`disable-model-invocation: true`; runs receive → one AskUserQuestion with two questions: origin platform with detected option first, reason for switch → ack runs the core commit transaction (received seal archived, this session adopted as owner, fresh `open` generation; double-receive prevented by the one-time token; command tests assert the active/open + archived/received outcome) → evidence audit of bundle git snapshot vs live HEAD/status → announce role-remap table → auto-continue next step, pausing only per AGENTS.md boundaries); **`/baton:baton-setup`** (doctor + choose surfaces + init + template scaffold with diff preview). Receive-side continuation is a **skill** (`handoff-protocol`), not an agent — the main thread must inherit the task; a subagent would strand context. Optional v2 `handoff-verifier` agent (fresh-context bundle audit) is out of v1 scope.

  1724	   603	   105	
  1725	   604	   106	Gate-1 correction: Codex now ships lifecycle hooks, so the adapter is redesigned around them. Surfaces: (1) **repo `.codex/hooks.json`** (written by `init --codex`, merged never clobbered): `Stop` → mechanical checkpoint, `PreCompact` → context-boundary checkpoint, `SessionStart` → pending-handoff notice via injected context. No StopFailure equivalent exists on Codex, so a limit death is bounded by the last Stop checkpoint (one turn worst case). (2) `.agents/skills/baton-handoff/SKILL.md` per the Agent Skills standard — carries the receive/handoff protocol, invoked as `$baton-handoff` or by description match. Setup and doctor therefore report four distinct states per hook — installed / enabled / **trusted** / observed-executing (canary event) — and the fidelity claim is gated on the canary, with setup guiding the user through `/hooks` when review is pending. Hook definitions include `commandWindows` overrides.   1867	   746	   172	### Acceptance constraints (the loop's exit condition)
  1868	   747	   173

  3186	  2065	   169	  const p = bundlePaths(root);

  3258	  2137	   241	 * @param {string} root @param {'finalize'|'takeover'|'receive'} kind @param {any} io @param {string} token
  3259	  2138	   242	 * @returns {string} the history stem for this rotation

  3261	  2140	   244	export function rotateJournalIn(root, kind, io, token) {
  3262	  2141	   245	  const p = bundlePaths(root);
  3263	  2142	   246	  return guardedWrite(root, io, token, () => {

  3278	  2157	   261	    } else {

  3280	  2159	   263	    }

  3285	  2164	   268	    }
  3286	  2165	   269	    atomicWriteText(io.fs, p.journal, '');
  3287	  2166	   270

  3289	  2168	   272	    const freezes = io.fs

  3299	  2178	   282	        } catch {

  3303	  2182	   286	    }
  3304	  2183	   287	
  3305	  2184	   288	    io.fs.unlinkSync(markerPath(p));

  3307	  2186	   290	  });
  3308	  2187	   291	}

  3338	  2217	    28	/** @param {string} root */
  3339	  2218	    29	function lockPaths(root) {
  3340	  2219	    30	  const dir = `${root}/.handoff`;
  3341	  2220	    31	  return {
  3342	  2221	    32	    dir,
  3343	  2222	    33	    lockDir: `${dir}/lock`,
  3344	  2223	    34	    owner: `${dir}/lock/owner.json`,
  3345	  2224	    35	    journal: `${dir}/journal.ndjson`,

  3348	  2227	    38	
  3349	  2228	    39	const ESCAPE_HATCH =
  3350	  2229	    40	  'Verify manually that no baton process still holds it, then delete .handoff/lock to clear.';
  3351	  2230	    41	
  3352	  2231	    42	/**
  3353	  2232	    43	 * Inspect the current lock state.
  3354	  2233	    44	 * @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p
  3355	  2234	    45	 * @returns {{state: 'free'} | {state: 'torn', cause: string} | {state: 'live'|'dead'|'cross-host', owner: any}}
  3356	  2235	    46	 */
  3357	  2236	    47	function inspect(io, p) {
  3358	  2237	    48	  if (!io.fs.existsSync(p.lockDir)) return { state: 'free' };
  3359	  2238	    49	  if (!io.fs.existsSync(p.owner)) {
  3360	  2239	    50	    return { state: 'torn', cause: 'owner.json is missing (torn lock metadata)' };
  3361	  2240	    51	  }
  3362	  2241	    52	  let owner;
  3363	  2242	    53	  try {
  3364	  2243	    54	    owner = JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(p.owner, 'utf8'));
  3365	  2244	    55	  } catch {
  3366	  2245	    56	    return { state: 'torn', cause: 'owner.json is unparseable (torn lock metadata)' };
  3367	  2246	    57	  }
  3368	  2247	    58	  if (owner.host !== io.host) return { state: 'cross-host', owner };
  3369	  2248	    59	  if (io.processAlive(owner.pid, owner.startTime)) return { state: 'live', owner };
  3370	  2249	    60	  return { state: 'dead', owner };
  3371	  2250	    61	}

  3373	  2252	    63	/** @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p @param {string} text */
  3374	  2253	    64	function journalNote(io, p, text) {
  3375	  2254	    65	  io.fs.mkdirSync(p.dir, { recursive: true });
  3376	  2255	    66	  // Allocate seq + dedupeKey like every other journal entry (gate-2 fix,
  3377	  2256	    67	  // reviewer-b finding 2): a keyless, seq-less note poisons journalSeq to NaN
  3378	  2257	    68	  // on replay and dedupes every later keyless event. We are already inside the
  3379	  2258	    69	  // lock here, so reading the tail for allocation is race-free.
  3380	  2259	    70	  let tailSeq = 0;
  3381	  2260	    71	  try {

  3383	  2262	    73	    if (typeof snap?.journalSeq === 'number') tailSeq = snap.journalSeq;
  3384	  2263	    74	  } catch {

  3386	  2265	    76	  }
  3387	  2266	    77	  try {
  3388	  2267	    78	    for (const e of readAllTolerant(io.fs, p.journal).entries) {
  3389	  2268	    79	      if (typeof e.seq === 'number' && e.seq > tailSeq) tailSeq = e.seq;
  3390	  2269	    80	    }
  3391	  2270	    81	  } catch {
  3392	  2271	    82	    // no journal yet
  3393	  2272	    83	  }
  3394	  2273	    84	  const ts = io.now();
  3395	  2274	    85	  appendEntry(io.fs, p.journal, {
  3396	  2275	    86	    seq: tailSeq + 1,
  3397	  2276	    87	    ts,
  3398	  2277	    88	    type: 'note',

  3400	  2279	    90	    writerId: ['lock', io.host, io.pid].join('-'),
  3401	  2280	    91	    source: 'lock',

  3406	  2285	    96	/** @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p */
  3407	  2286	    97	function publishOwner(io, p) {

  3409	  2288	    99	  atomicWriteJson(io.fs, p.owner, {
  3410	  2289	   100	    host: io.host,

  3420	  2299	   110	/** @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p */
  3421	  2300	   111	function acquire(io, p) {
  3422	  2301	   112	  io.fs.mkdirSync(p.dir, { recursive: true });
  3423	  2302	   113	  try {
  3424	  2303	   114	    io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
  3425	  2304	   115	    return publishOwner(io, p);
  3426	  2305	   116	  } catch (err) {
  3427	  2306	   117	    if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code !== 'EEXIST') throw err;
  3428	  2307	   118	  }
  3429	  2308	   119	
  3430	  2309	   120	  const s = inspect(io, p);
  3431	  2310	   121	  switch (s.state) {
  3432	  2311	   122	    case 'free':
  3433	  2312	   123	      // Raced a release between mkdir failure and inspection; retry once. A
  3434	  2313	   124	      // competitor can win THIS mkdir too (gate-2 fix 12: observed under real
  3435	  2314	   125	      // barrier-released contention) — that is contention, not corruption.
  3436	  2315	   126	      try {
  3437	  2316	   127	        io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
  3438	  2317	   128	      } catch (err) {
  3439	  2318	   129	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') {
  3440	  2319	   130	          throw new LockHeldError('lock was re-acquired by a competitor mid-inspection — transient contention');
  3441	  2320	   131	        }
  3442	  2321	   132	        throw err;
  3443	  2322	   133	      }
  3444	  2323	   134	      return publishOwner(io, p);
  3445	  2324	   135	    case 'live':
  3446	  2325	   136	      throw new LockHeldError(
  3447	  2326	   137	        `lock is held by a live process (pid ${s.owner.pid} on ${s.owner.host}) — terminate that process first.`,
  3448	  2327	   138	      );
  3449	  2328	   139	    case 'cross-host':
  3450	  2329	   140	      throw new Error(
  3451	  2330	   141	        `lock is held from another host ('${s.owner.host}', this is '${io.host}') — cross-host locks are never provably safe to steal. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
  3452	  2331	   142	      );
  3453	  2332	   143	    case 'torn':
  3454	  2333	   144	      // During ACQUIRE, torn metadata is usually a competitor caught between
  3455	  2334	   145	      // its mkdir and owner.json publication — transient by construction, so
  3456	  2335	   146	      // LockHeldError lets withLock wait it out (gate-2 fix 12). A genuinely
  3457	  2336	   147	      // crashed publisher exhausts the retry budget and surfaces this same
  3458	  2337	   148	      // message; recovery semantics (recoverLock) are unchanged: never steal.
  3459	  2338	   149	      throw new LockHeldError(`${s.cause} — unsupported for automatic recovery. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`);
  3460	  2339	   150	    case 'dead': {
  3461	  2340	   151	      // Atomic dead-lock reclaim (gate-2 iter-2 B1, hardened iter-3 finding-1).
  3462	  2341	   152	      // rm-then-mkdir is NOT mutually exclusive: two contenders can both observe
  3463	  2342	   153	      // 'dead' before either removes the stale dir, then both rm+mkdir — the
  3464	  2343	   154	      // second silently clobbers the first, yielding two simultaneous holders and
  3465	  2344	   155	      // two takeover notes. rename() is the atomic arbiter instead: the stale
  3466	  2345	   156	      // lock dir has exactly one name, so only one process can move it aside (the
  3467	  2346	   157	      // rest get ENOENT). Winning the rename IS winning the reclaim; a contender
  3468	  2347	   158	      // that recreated the dir via the 'free' path first makes our mkdir EEXIST →
  3469	  2348	   159	      // transient contention. The fencing token stays the write-time backstop.
  3470	  2349	   160	      const aside = `${p.lockDir}.reclaim-${io.pid}-${io.newFencingToken()}`;
  3471	  2350	   161	      try {
  3472	  2351	   162	        io.fs.renameSync(p.lockDir, aside);
  3473	  2352	   163	      } catch (err) {
  3474	  2353	   164	        // Source already gone → another contender is reclaiming it; wait+retry.
  3475	  2354	   165	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'ENOENT') {
  3476	  2355	   166	          throw new LockHeldError('a competitor is reclaiming the dead lock — transient contention');
  3477	  2356	   167	        }
  3478	  2357	   168	        throw err;
  3479	  2358	   169	      }
  3480	  2359	   170	      io.fs.rmSync(aside, { recursive: true, force: true });
  3481	  2360	   171	      try {
  3482	  2361	   172	        io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
  3483	  2362	   173	      } catch (err) {
  3484	  2363	   174	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') {
  3485	  2364	   175	          throw new LockHeldError('a competitor re-claimed the dead lock first — transient contention');
  3486	  2365	   176	        }
  3487	  2366	   177	        throw err;
  3488	  2367	   178	      }
  3489	  2368	   179	      const token = publishOwner(io, p);
  3490	  2369	   180	      // Journal the takeover only now — we HOLD the lock (fresh dir + published
  3491	  2370	   181	      // owner), so the note's seq is allocated while holding it (plan

  3521	  2400	   211	  } catch {

  3523	  2402	   213	  }

  3525	  2404	   215	}
  3526	  2405	   216	
  3527	  2406	   217	// A live same-host holder is transient by design — operation-scoped locks are
  3528	  2407	   218	// held for milliseconds — so contention waits instead of dropping the
  3529	  2408	   219	// operation (gate-2 fix 12: simultaneous checkpoints must all land). The budget
  3530	  2409	   220	// is generous (≈15 s): under heavy load a writer may be starved of scheduling
  3531	  2410	   221	// for seconds, and waiting is strictly safer than silently dropping its work.
  3532	  2411	   222	// Every other contended state (torn, cross-host) stays fail-fast: waiting
  3533	  2412	   223	// cannot make those provably safe.

  3537	  2416	   227	const sleepMs = (/** @type {number} */ ms) => {
  3538	  2417	   228	  Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms);
  3539	  2418	   229	};

  3548	  2427	   238	  const p = lockPaths(root);
  3549	  2428	   239	  // Jail BEFORE any lock mutation (gate-2 iter-2 B2): a symlinked .handoff or

  3560	  2439	   250	      break;

  3566	  2445	   256	      throw err;
  3567	  2446	   257	    }
  3568	  2447	   258	  }
  3569	  2448	   259	  try {

  3571	  2450	   261	  } finally {
  3572	  2451	   262	    release(io, p, token);
  3573	  2452	   263	  }
  3574	  2453	   264	}

  3577	  2456	   267	 * Fast-abort layer: re-read the published token immediately before a write; a
  3578	  2457	   268	 * holder that paused past its last check aborts instead of clobbering.
  3579	  2458	   269	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {string} token @param {() => any} fn

  3581	  2460	   271	export function guardedWrite(root, io, token, fn) {
  3582	  2461	   272	  const p = lockPaths(root);
  3583	  2462	   273	  let current = null;

  3586	  2465	   276	  } catch {

  3588	  2467	   278	  }

  3590	  2469	   280	    throw new FencingError(

  3592	  2471	   282	    );
  3593	  2472	   283	  }
  3594	  2473	   284	  return fn();
  3595	  2474	   285	}
  3596	  2475	   286	
  3597	  2476	   287	/**
  3598	  2477	   288	 * Explicit recovery. `force` is an intent flag only — it never changes the
  3599	  2478	   289	 * decision: exactly one state recovers (provably-dead same-host owner).
  3600	  2479	   290	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {{force?: boolean}} [opts]
  3601	  2480	   291	 * @returns {{recovered: boolean, refusedReason: string | null}}
  3602	  2481	   292	 */
  3603	  2482	   293	export function recoverLock(root, io, opts = {}) {
  3604	  2483	   294	  void opts;
  3605	  2484	   295	  const p = lockPaths(root);
  3606	  2485	   296	  // Jail before recovery (gate-2 iter-2 B2): recoverLock removes the lock dir,
  3607	  2486	   297	  // so a symlinked managed tree must be refused first — even with force, a
  3608	  2487	   298	  // symlink is never provably safe to delete through.
  3609	  2488	   299	  const safe = checkHandoffTree(root, io);
  3610	  2489	   300	  if (!safe.ok) return { recovered: false, refusedReason: `${safe.problem} — refusing recovery` };
  3611	  2490	   301	  const s = inspect(io, p);
  3612	  2491	   302	  switch (s.state) {
  3613	  2492	   303	    case 'free':
  3614	  2493	   304	      return { recovered: true, refusedReason: null };
  3615	  2494	   305	    case 'dead': {
  3616	  2495	   306	      // Reclaim atomically via a single acquire() attempt + release, NOT an
  3617	  2496	   307	      // inspect-then-rmSync (iter-4 I1): the old bare rmSync had a TOCTOU — a
  3618	  2497	   308	      // competitor could win the rename-arbitrated dead-reclaim between this
  3619	  2498	   309	      // inspect() and the rmSync, publish a LIVE owner, and recovery would then
  3620	  2499	   310	      // delete a lock whose owner is alive. acquire() re-inspects atomically and
  3621	  2500	   311	      // shares the SAME rename arbitration, so recovery and a concurrent takeover
  3622	  2501	   312	      // are mutually exclusive: acquire either reclaims a still-dead lock (and
  3623	  2502	   313	      // journals the takeover under the lock) or throws because it is now
  3624	  2503	   314	      // live/torn — in which case we refuse rather than steal. release() then
  3625	  2504	   315	      // leaves the slot clear.
  3626	  2505	   316	      let token;
  3627	  2506	   317	      try {
  3628	  2507	   318	        token = acquire(io, p);
  3629	  2508	   319	      } catch (err) {
  3630	  2509	   320	        return { recovered: false, refusedReason: /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err) };
  3631	  2510	   321	      }
  3632	  2511	   322	      release(io, p, token);
  3633	  2512	   323	      return { recovered: true, refusedReason: null };
  3634	  2513	   324	    }
  3635	  2514	   325	    case 'live':
  3636	  2515	   326	      return {
  3637	  2516	   327	        recovered: false,
  3638	  2517	   328	        refusedReason: `lock is held by a live process (pid ${s.owner.pid} on ${s.owner.host}) — terminate that process first.`,
  3639	  2518	   329	      };
  3640	  2519	   330	    case 'cross-host':
  3641	  2520	   331	      return {
  3642	  2521	   332	        recovered: false,
  3643	  2522	   333	        refusedReason: `lock is held from another host ('${s.owner.host}', this is '${io.host}') — cross-host locks are never provably safe to steal, even with force. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
  3644	  2523	   334	      };
  3645	  2524	   335	    case 'torn':
  3646	  2525	   336	      return {
  3647	  2526	   337	        recovered: false,
  3648	  2527	   338	        refusedReason: `${s.cause} — unsupported for automatic recovery, even with force. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
  3649	  2528	   339	      };
  3650	  2529	   340	    /* c8 ignore next 2 */
  3651	  2530	   341	    default:
  3652	  2531	   342	      return { recovered: false, refusedReason: 'unreachable lock state' };
  3653	  2532	   343	  }
  3654	  2533	   344	}

  3815	  2694	    87	
  3816	  2695	    88	/** Event-shaped: an object carrying a string `type`. */

  3818	  2697	    90	
  3819	  2698	    91	/**
  3820	  2699	    92	 * Tolerant stdin parse (live /baton:handoff failure: a model sent one event
  3821	  2700	    93	 * per line and the whole narrative checkpoint silently failed). Accept the
  3822	  2701	    94	 * canonical single JSON value, a bare array of events, or NDJSON where every
  3823	  2702	    95	 * line is an event object or a {schema, events} wrapper. All-or-nothing: one
  3824	  2703	    96	 * non-event element fails the whole parse — never a partial apply.
  3825	  2704	    97	 * @param {string} text @returns {{ok: true, raw: any} | {ok: false, why?: string}}
  3826	  2705	    98	 */
  3827	  2706	    99	function parseStdin(text) {
  3828	  2707	   100	  let single;
  3829	  2708	   101	  let singleOk = false;
  3830	  2709	   102	  try {
  3831	  2710	   103	    single = JSON.parse(text);
  3832	  2711	   104	    singleOk = true;
  3833	  2712	   105	  } catch {
  3834	  2713	   106	    singleOk = false;
  3835	  2714	   107	  }
  3836	  2715	   108	  if (singleOk) {
  3837	  2716	   109	    if (Array.isArray(single)) {
  3838	  2717	   110	      return single.every(isEventShaped) ? { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: single } } : { ok: false };
  3839	  2718	   111	    }
  3840	  2719	   112	    // A closest-miss of the documented wrapper — an events array whose schema
  3841	  2720	   113	    // key is missing or wrong — must ERROR, never silently degrade to a junk
  3842	  2721	   114	    // note with ok:true (the model cannot self-correct from a success
  3843	  2722	   115	    // envelope while its narrative was discarded).

  3846	  2725	   118	    }
  3847	  2726	   119	    // A single bare event object (string `type`, none of the raw-hook payload
  3848	  2727	   120	    // markers) is one of the two most likely readings of "pipe events on
  3849	  2728	   121	    // stdin" — accept it as that event instead of degrading it to a junk note.
  3850	  2729	   122	    if (
  3851	  2730	   123	      isEventShaped(single) &&
  3852	  2731	   124	      single.schema === undefined &&

  3858	  2737	   130	    }
  3859	  2738	   131	    return { ok: true, raw: single };
  3860	  2739	   132	  }

  3862	  2741	   134	  if (lines.length === 0) return { ok: false };
  3863	  2742	   135	  /** @type {any[]} */
  3864	  2743	   136	  const events = [];

  3866	  2745	   138	    let v;
  3867	  2746	   139	    try {
  3868	  2747	   140	      v = JSON.parse(line);
  3869	  2748	   141	    } catch {
  3870	  2749	   142	      return { ok: false };
  3871	  2750	   143	    }

  3873	  2752	   145	      if (!v.events.every(isEventShaped)) return { ok: false };
  3874	  2753	   146	      events.push(...v.events);
  3875	  2754	   147	    } else if (isEventShaped(v)) {
  3876	  2755	   148	      events.push(v);
  3877	  2756	   149	    } else {
  3878	  2757	   150	      return { ok: false };
  3879	  2758	   151	    }
  3880	  2759	   152	  }

  4761	  3640	   127	  // COMMAND (iter-5 A3) — inspect the actual command/commandWindows fields, not
  4762	  3641	   128	  // the serialized blob (a matcher/comment mentioning baton must not count). A
  4763	  3642	   129	  // file that references baton only in a session-start hook is installed but NOT
  4764	  3643	   130	  // checkpoint-enabled.
  4765	  3644	   131	  let enabled = false;
  4766	  3645	   132	  try {
  4767	  3646	   133	    const cfg = JSON.parse(/** @type {string} */ (text));
  4768	  3647	   134	    // Match the bare `baton checkpoint` form AND the absolute
  4769	  3648	   135	    // `"<node>" "<…/baton.mjs>" checkpoint` form init now writes (the entry
  4770	  3649	   136	    // script may be quote-terminated: `baton.mjs" checkpoint`).
  4771	  3650	   137	    enabled = hookCommands(cfg?.hooks?.[checkpointEvent]).some((c) => /\bbaton(?:\.mjs)?["']?\s+checkpoint\b/.test(c));
  4772	  3651	   138	  } catch {
  4773	  3652	   139	    enabled = false;
  4774	  3653	   140	  }
  4775	  3654	   141	  // observed: a mechanical checkpoint from THIS platform's CHECKPOINT hook is
  4776	  3655	   142	  // recorded — the journal entry must be platform-sourced AND carry
  4777	  3656	   143	  // payload.trigger === checkpointEvent (iter-5 A3). normalize stamps the hook
  4778	  3657	   144	  // event name as payload.trigger, so a SessionStart/PreCompact/triggerless
  4779	  3658	   145	  // entry no longer masquerades as the per-turn Stop canary.
  4780	  3659	   146	  let observed = false;
  4781	  3660	   147	  try {
  4782	  3661	   148	    for (const e of readAllTolerant(io.fs, p.journal).entries) {
  4783	  3662	   149	      const mine = String(e?.writerId ?? '').startsWith(`${platform}-`) || e?.source === platform;
  4784	  3663	   150	      if (mine && e?.payload?.trigger === checkpointEvent) {
  4785	  3664	   151	        observed = true;
  4786	  3665	   152	        break;
  4787	  3666	   153	      }
  4788	  3667	   154	    }
  4789	  3668	   155	  } catch {
  4790	  3669	   156	    observed = false;
  4791	  3670	   157	  }
  4792	  3671	   158	  const states = { installed: true, enabled, trusted: 'unknown', observed };
  4793	  3672	   159	  // The ≤1-turn claim needs the checkpoint hook DECLARED (enabled) AND OBSERVED —
  4794	  3673	   160	  // neither alone suffices.
  4795	  3674	   161	  const fidelityHolds = enabled && observed;
  4796	  3675	   162	  const enabledNote = enabled ? `${checkpointEvent} checkpoint hook enabled` : `${checkpointEvent} checkpoint hook NOT declared (enabled=false)`;
  4797	  3676	   163	  return {
  4798	  3677	   164	    id,
  4799	  3678	   165	    ok: true,
  4800	  3679	   166	    states,
  4801	  3680	   167	    detail: fidelityHolds
  4802	  3681	   168	      ? `installed, ${enabledNote}; trusted=unknown (not externally verifiable); execution OBSERVED (canary) — the ≤1-turn mechanical-staleness claim holds`
  4803	  3682	   169	      : `installed, ${enabledNote}; trusted=unknown — ${trustNote}; ${observed ? 'execution observed but' : 'execution not yet observed —'} the ≤1-turn fidelity claim is gated on the ${checkpointEvent} canary + enablement`,
  4804	  3683	   170	  };
  4805	  3684	   171	}

  4807	  3686	   173	// Noninteractive status probes per platform (docs/design/platform-notes.md CLIs).
  4808	  3687	   174	// capOnSuccess caps what a clean exit PROVES (gate-2 iter-2 M3): `claude

  4810	  3689	   176	// that auth is valid, so its capability is capped at "installed". The codex/

  4821	  3700	   187	  /co-authored-by:[^\n]*\b(claude|gpt|copilot|codex)\b/i,

  4826	  3705	   192	/** @param {any} io @param {string} path @returns {string | null} */
  4827	  3706	   193	function readOrNull(io, path) {
  4828	  3707	   194	  try {
  4829	  3708	   195	    return io.fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
  4830	  3709	   196	  } catch {
  4831	  3710	   197	    return null;
  4832	  3711	   198	  }
  4833	  3712	   199	}
  4834	  3713	   200	
  4835	  3714	   201	/**
  4836	  3715	   202	 * Classify one probe invocation per the two-dimension record: capability is
  4837	  3716	   203	 * the ordered ladder verified as far as the evidence goes; outcome is what the
  4838	  3717	   204	 * probe itself did. A server-issued limit response proves authentication.
  4839	  3718	   205	 * @param {{platform: string, bin: string, args: string[], capOnSuccess?: string}} probe @param {any} io @param {any} table
  4840	  3719	   206	 */
  4841	  3720	   207	async function runProbe(probe, io, table) {
  4842	  3721	   208	  try {
  4843	  3722	   209	    await io.execFile(probe.bin, probe.args, { timeout: PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS });
  4844	  3723	   210	    return { platform: probe.platform, capability: probe.capOnSuccess ?? 'reachable', outcome: 'ok' };
  4845	  3724	   211	  } catch (err) {
  4846	  3725	   212	    const e = /** @type {any} */ (err);
  4847	  3726	   213	    if (e?.code === 'ENOENT') return { platform: probe.platform, capability: null, outcome: 'error' };
  4848	  3727	   214	    if (e?.killed === true) return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'timeout' };
  4849	  3728	   215	    const text = `${e?.stdout ?? ''}\n${e?.stderr ?? ''}`;
  4850	  3729	   216	    if (table && classify({ text, exitCode: 1, platform: probe.platform, table, structured: null }).class === 'usage-limit') {
  4851	  3730	   217	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'authenticated', outcome: 'rate-limited' };
  4852	  3731	   218	    }
  4853	  3732	   219	    if (/authenticated as|logged in as/i.test(text) && /unreachable|ECONN|offline|network/i.test(text)) {
  4854	  3733	   220	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'authenticated', outcome: 'error' };
  4855	  3734	   221	    }
  4856	  3735	   222	    if (/not logged in|log ?in first|unauthorized|authenticat/i.test(text)) {
  4857	  3736	   223	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'error' };
  4858	  3737	   224	    }
  4859	  3738	   225	    return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'error' };
  4860	  3739	   226	  }
  4861	  3740	   227	}

  4863	  3742	   229	/** @param {any} io @param {string} root @returns {Promise<{id: string, ok: boolean, detail?: string}>} */
  4864	  3743	   230	async function gitGuardCheck(io, root) {
  4865	  3744	   231	  let log;
  4866	  3745	   232	  try {
  4867	  3746	   233	    log = await io.execFile('git', ['log', '-n', String(GUARD_COMMIT_BOUND), '--format=%h %s%n%n%b'], { cwd: root, timeout: 5000 });
  4868	  3747	   234	  } catch {
  4869	  3748	   235	    return { id: 'git-guard', ok: true, detail: 'git unavailable — commit scan skipped' };
  4870	  3749	   236	  }
  4871	  3750	   237	  // Chunks start at a line beginning with an abbreviated sha + space.
  4872	  3751	   238	  const chunks = log.stdout.split(/^(?=[0-9a-f]{7,40} )/m).filter((/** @type {string} */ c) => c.trim() !== '');
  4873	  3752	   239	  for (const chunk of chunks) {
  4874	  3753	   240	    if (TRAILER_PATTERNS.some((re) => re.test(chunk))) {
  4875	  3754	   241	      const sha = chunk.slice(0, chunk.indexOf(' '));
  4876	  3755	   242	      return {
  4877	  3756	   243	        id: 'git-guard',
  4878	  3757	   244	        ok: false,
  4879	  3758	   245	        detail: `commit ${sha} carries an AI attribution trailer — rewrite it before publishing (git rebase -i / git commit --amend)`,
  4880	  3759	   246	      };
  4881	  3760	   247	    }
  4882	  3761	   248	  }
  4883	  3762	   249	  return { id: 'git-guard', ok: true, detail: `no AI trailers in the last ${GUARD_COMMIT_BOUND} commits` };
  4884	  3763	   250	}

  6109	  4988	     2	
  6110	  4989	     3	Authoritative plan: `docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md` (Gate-1 approved).   6111	  4990	     4	
  6112	  4991	     5	## Language and tooling
  6113	  4992	     6	
  6114	  4993	     7	Plain ESM JavaScript (`.mjs`) with JSDoc types, checked by `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` (dev-only). No build step: hooks invoke source directly. Zero runtime dependencies; strict spec-based flag parsing (`parseFlagsStrict` in commands/shared.mjs — unknown flags, stray positionals, and missing string-flag values are exit-2 usage errors, so a garbled safety flag can never silently lose intent); `node:test` with a small golden-file helper (`UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 npm test` regenerates). Node >= 20.
  6115	  4994	     8	
  6116	  4995	     9	Testability backbone: every command's `run()` takes an injected `io` object — `{ cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now }`. Pure logic (reducers, renderers, resolvers, classifiers) takes plain data and returns plain data. Unit tests run over an in-memory fs fake (`tests/helpers/memfs.mjs`); a thin integration layer uses `fs.mkdtemp` on the real fs.

  6161	  5040	    54	## Bundle schema (`baton/bundle@1`)
  6162	  5041	    55	
  6163	  5042	    56	`bundle.json` fields: `schema`, `bundleId`, `generation`, `createdAt/updatedAt`, `origin {platform, model, sessionHint, unstable}`, `task {goal, constraints[], acceptance[]}`, `plan.steps[] {id, title, status: pending|active|done|blocked, note}`, `decisions[] {seq, ts, summary, detail(capped)}`, `files {touched[] {path, op, lastTs}, truncated}`, `roles.assignments`, `git {branch, headSha, dirty, dirtySummary[], contentDigest, summaryTruncated} | null`, `handoff {status: open|sealed|received, reason, reasonClass, toPlatformHint, finalizedAt, receive_log[]}`, `journalSeq`, `compaction {droppedDecisions, note}`, `dedupeRing: string[]` (merge idempotency ring, capped 500, oldest evicted), transcript field (opt-in, redacted).
  6164	  5043	    57	
  6165	  5044	    58	`journal.ndjson` entry: `{seq, ts, type, dedupeKey, writerId, source, payload}`. Types: `decision | plan.set | plan.step | file.touch | note | roles.remap | task.update | git.update`. Every type is self-applicable for replay over `emptyBundle()`.
  6166	  5045	    59	
  6167	  5046	    60	Size budget (pure `compact.mjs`): decisions capped first-20 + last-150 + marker; `detail` <= 2000 chars; `files.touched` <= 300 (LRU by `lastTs`, sets `files.truncated: true`); `git.dirtySummary` <= 100 lines (sets `git.summaryTruncated: true`; skipped when `git` is null). Deterministic truncation only — no LLM summarization.
  6168	  5047	    61

  6221	  5100	   114	## Per-module test lists
  6222	  5101	   115	
  6223	  5102	   116	- **fsx**: atomic write visible-only-after-rename; `.bak` rotation; leftover `.tmp` ignored/cleaned; `safeReadJson` on garbage; Windows rename-retry (EPERM).
  6224	  5103	   117	- **jsonl/ids**: append+read roundtrip; torn last line dropped with warning; seq monotonic; dedupeKey stable across key order.
  6225	  5104	   118	- **schema**: empty bundle validates; pathed error per missing field; unknown fields tolerated; `@2` rejected by migrate.
  6226	  5105	   119	- **merge**: each event type mutates its section; double-apply = identical bundle; unknown type degrades to note; seq ordering.
  6227	  5106	   120	- **compact**: over-budget collapse deterministic (byte-identical); under-budget identity; truncation markers.
  6228	  5107	   121	- **store**: snapshot+replay equals pure reduction; corrupt snapshot -> `.bak` recovery; both corrupt -> journal rebuild; torn tail; marker-based rotation roll-forward/back; kill-mid-write sim.
  6229	  5108	   122	- **lock**: mutual exclusion; provably-dead takeover; live same-host owner refused (incl. `--force`); torn metadata refused; pause-after-final-fence-check; crash between creation and metadata publication.
  6230	  5109	   123	- **normalize**: `baton/event@1` passthrough; per-harness fixture extraction (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor payloads); malformed-input fuzz never throws.
  6231	  5110	   124	- **render / receive-prompt**: goldens (minimal, mid-session, finalized, stale, degraded-role); char caps; attribution invariant; determinism.
  6232	  5111	   125	- **signatures/classifier**: verbatim positive fixtures per platform; negative/near-miss corpus; ANSI stripping; precedence; reset-hint extraction; exit-code interplay matrix; non-limit failing-process fixtures; overlay override; bad-regex rejection; time guard.
  6233	  5112	   126	- **matrix/resolve**: config validation (pathed errors); chain walking with avoid/disabled/rate-limited skips; native/delegated/forced-default/unavailable; probe-eligibility rules; determinism.
  6234	  5113	   127	- **txn**: token binds journalSeq + intake + config digest + session + probe snapshot + content-sensitive git digest; one rejection test per bound input; `sealed->received` and `open->received` (degraded seal); ownership adoption + new generation; chained A->B->C; competing receivers; double-commit.
  6235	  5114	   128	- **scaffold**: gitignore variants (covering pattern no-op, CRLF, trailing newline, idempotent double-run); managed-block replace/append/corrupt-marker-refuse with outside-bytes invariance; attribution merge (absent/present/non-empty/malformed-refuse); `--dry-run` zero writes; real-fs `mkdtemp` + `git init` integration.
  6236	  5115	   129	- **git**: snapshot on clean/dirty/detached/not-a-repo/timeout; guard trailer fixtures incl. word-boundary false-positive ("Claudette Smith" not flagged).
  6237	  5116	   130	- **doctor**: check aggregation; `--strict` exit; probe states; version floors; network-FS warning.
  6238	  5117	   131	- **purge-transcript**: whole-tree secret removal (snapshot, bak, journal, history, log); interruption resume via marker; packaged-bin invocation.
  6239	  5118	   132	- **invariants**: no AI-credit strings in any rendered output, golden, or template.
  6240	  5119	   133	- **integration**: e2e failover (init -> 25 checkpoints -> kill-mid-write -> finalize usage-limit -> receive on second platform -> golden prompt); chained A->B->C; six-direction contract matrix; cli-spawn exit codes and `--json` stdout purity.
  6241	  5120	   134	
  6242	  5121	   135	## CLI contract

  6244	  5123	   137	Commands: `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover`, `session-start`.   6927	  5806	    68	  const out = [];

  7174	  6053	    18	//   prepare(root, opts, io) -> { token, prompt, assignments, warnings }
  7175	  6054	    19	//   commit(root, token, opts, io) -> { adopted, generation, archivedTo }
  7176	  6055	    20	//   Both are SYNCHRONOUS. The plan pins that the receive COMMAND wires

  7180	  6059	    24	//   opts (same shape for prepare and commit):

  7183	  6062	    27	//       reason,         // intake: why the switch happened (free text)

  7185	  6064	    29	//       probes,         // optional probe map for resolveRoles (default null)

  7187	  6066	    31	//
  7188	  6067	    32	// TOKEN BINDING (THE pin). prepare captures a REVISION FINGERPRINT and returns it
  7189	  6068	    33	//   as an opaque token. It binds every one of these inputs (one rejection test per
  7190	  6069	    34	//   input below — verifier fold F3 completed the set):
  7191	  6070	    35	//     - bundle REVISION: generation + journalSeq (as loadBundle reports them)
  7192	  6071	    36	//     - intake: origin + reason
  7193	  6072	    37	//     - config digest: a hash of the baton.config.json bytes at <root>
  7194	  6073	    38	//     - GIT digest: a hash of the WHOLE opts.gitSnapshot object (PIN — the git
  7195	  6074	    39	//       state is bound by hashing the caller-passed object, so headSha, dirty,

  7197	  6076	    41	//       contentDigest still drifts the token, and vice versa)

  7199	  6078	    43	//     - target platform (opts.platform)
