   762	   302	    12	
   763	   303	    13	1. **First milestone**: cross-platform failover layer. Loop-creator and dual-worktree pipelines are later milestones; leave seams.
   764	   304	    14	2. **Capture**: continuous checkpointing via harness hooks **plus** an explicit `/handoff` finalize command that records reason-for-switching.
   765	   305	    15	3. **Platforms**: all three from v1. Claude Code gets the deep integration (plugin with hooks); Codex and Cursor get lighter native adapters.
   766	   306	    16	4. **Receive flow**: intake (original platform + reason) → load bundle → role-matrix remap → auto-continue the task.
   767	   307	    17	5. **Bundle home**: gitignored `.handoff/` directory inside the repo.
   768	   308	    18	6. **Architecture**: one repo — harness-agnostic core Node CLI + three native adapters + templates + tests.
   769	   309	    19	7. **Attribution (hard invariant)**: ZERO AI mentions in git history — no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated with Claude Code" — permanently. During initial construction (pre-v1), all commits are authored solely by `SakshamUboweja <ssakshamu@gmail.com>` with frequent, regular commits to main (contributions accrue to his GitHub profile); external human OSS contributors are welcome post-v1. Enforced via `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` in Claude Code settings (the old `includeCoAuthoredBy` boolean is deprecated) + a doctor check.
   770	   310	    20	8. **AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md**: the tool scaffolds an ideal pair into any project (this repo dogfoods them). Design grounded in the official Fable 5 and GPT 5.6 prompting guides (fetched; distilled below). Strongest models get latitude on the design.
   771	   311	    21	9. **Development methodology** (governs building this repo AND is encoded in the templates as the product's workflow):
   772	   312	    22	   - Fable 5 writes the plan doc → **GPT 5.6 Sol xhigh reviews it (Gate 1)**.
   773	   313	    23	   - Decompose into tasks/subtasks.
   774	   314	    24	   - Per subtask: **Opus 4.8 writes unit tests first, GPT 5.5 xhigh verifies the tests**; the two keep each other in line during implementation.
   775	   315	    25	   - At the end: **GPT 5.6 Sol xhigh and Fable 5 xhigh run independent reviews**; feedback is collated and implemented.
   776	   316	    26	   - Overall: a goal with genuine constraints, looped until the constraints are met. Review artifacts under `reviews/<task-id>/` with verdicts `{APPROVED, APPROVED_WITH_NOTES, BLOCKED}` (pattern from Saksham's wt-* repos).
   777	   317	    27	
   778	   318	    28	## Research findings that shape the design (verified 2026-07-11)
   779	   319	    29	
   780	   320	    30	- **Codex plugin (installed, v1.0.4) is the implementation pattern**: single Node entrypoint invoked as `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/<x>.mjs" <subcmd>`; hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` (SessionStart/SessionEnd/Stop) read event JSON on stdin and can emit `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`; commands/agents/skills as markdown with frontmatter; per-workspace state dir; structured-output JSON schemas for reviews. It has **no usage-limit handling** — our failover logic is net-new.
   781	   321	    31	- **Superpowers plugin (installed) is the cross-harness packaging pattern**: one repo ships `hooks/hooks.json` (Claude) + `hooks-cursor.json` (Cursor, camelCase events), a polyglot `run-hook.cmd`, and `.codex-plugin` / `.cursor-plugin` / `AGENTS.md` descriptors. Hook output differs per harness (Claude: `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`; Cursor: `additional_context`) — branch on `$CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT`.
   782	   322	    32	- **Limit-detection signals** (Gate-1 verified, 2026-07-11): structured signals FIRST, text signatures as fallback tier.
   783	   323	    33	  - Claude Code: **`StopFailure` hook event** fires when a turn ends on an API error, with matcher filtering by error type (`rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `billing_error`, `server_error`, …) — the primary, structured limit-death signal. Output/exit code ignored (observability-only), so a checkpoint there is safe by construction. Text fallback: the stable strings `You've hit your session limit · resets …` / `weekly limit` / `Opus limit`.
   784	   324	    34	  - Codex (>= 0.144): **lifecycle hooks exist** (`SessionStart`, `PreToolUse`, `PostToolUse`, `PreCompact`, `PostCompact`, `UserPromptSubmit`, `SubagentStop`, `Stop`; configured via `~/.codex/hooks.json`, `<repo>/.codex/hooks.json`, or config.toml `[hooks]`; stdin JSON with `session_id`, `cwd`, `model`, `transcript_path`). No StopFailure equivalent → limit death bounded by last Stop checkpoint. Text fallback: `You've hit your usage limit…`; `codex exec --json` exits non-zero.
   785	   325	    35	  - Cursor: weakest — BYO-key returns `{"error":"Too Many Requests", …}`; managed-billing schema undocumented. Heuristics + timeouts, `confidence: low`.
   786	   326	    36	- **Session handoff prior art**: HANDOFF.md markdown is the accepted lossy-universal mechanism; schema-level session transplants (authsec-bridge) are brittle — v1 stays markdown+JSON, no session-file surgery.
   787	   327	    37	- **Local surfaces available on this machine**: `codex` CLI (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh) with empty-but-supported `~/.codex/prompts/`; `cursor-agent` CLI (reads AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md natively); `.agents/skills` is the official Codex skills path; Cursor project hooks via `.cursor/hooks.json` (onPreEdit/onPostEdit/onPreCommit/onApprove).
   788	   328	    38	- **Running the methodology's models from Claude Code**: Agent tool model overrides (opus/fable) + codex companion (`… codex-companion.mjs task --model gpt-5.6-sol|gpt-5.5 --effort xhigh`, read-only sandbox, structured output).
   789	   329	    39	
   790	   330	    40	## Prompting-guide distillation (for the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md templates)
   791	   331	    41	
   792	   332	    42	- **Fable 5** (platform.claude.com guide): strong instruction-following — brief steering beats enumeration; state boundaries (pause only for destructive/irreversible/scope-change/user-only input); "when you have enough information to act, act"; audit progress claims against tool evidence; parallel subagents with async communication; provide a memory/notes location; fresh-context verifier subagents beat self-critique; over-prescriptive skills degrade output; never instruct reasoning echo (triggers refusals).
   793	   333	    43	- **GPT 5.6** (developers.openai.com guide): hierarchy Role → Goal → Success criteria → Constraints → Tools → Stop rules; outcome definition over process prescription; trimming repeated rules improved evals 10–15% and cut tokens 41–66%; ALWAYS/NEVER only for true invariants; state each policy once; name the current phase for long work; explicit validation guidance; avoid contradictions, universal defaults, blanket brevity, personality words.
   794	   334	    44	- **Template consequence**: shared invariants live exactly once in AGENTS.md (lean, hierarchical); CLAUDE.md is an `@AGENTS.md` import plus a short Claude-specific block (memory location, subagent guidance); any Codex-specific steering gets its own clearly-scoped short section.
   795	   335	    45	
   796	   336	    46	## Design
   797	   337	    47	
   798	   338	    48	_(Sections below synthesized from two Plan-agent designs — core engine; adapters/templates/methodology — merged after Gate-1 review.)_
   799	   339	    49	
   800	   340	    50	### Core engine (`core/`)
   801	   341	    51	
   802	   342	    52	**Language/tooling**: plain ESM JavaScript (`.mjs`) + JSDoc types checked by `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` (dev-only dep). No build step — hooks invoke source directly (`node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…"`), same as the proven codex plugin. **Zero runtime dependencies**; arg parsing via `node:util` `parseArgs`; **`node:test`** as the framework (golden-file helper ~40 lines with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`). Node >= 20. Every command's `run()` takes an injected `io` object (`{cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now}`); pure logic (reducers/renderers/resolvers/classifiers) is data-in/data-out; tests run over an in-memory fs fake plus a thin real-fs integration layer.
   803	   343	    53	
   804	   344	    54	**CLI surface** (`baton <cmd> --json`): `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover` (forced lock recovery). Frozen exit-code contract: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json` mode prints exactly one envelope `{ok, data, warnings, error}` on stdout. `baton wrap -- <cmd>` (PTY supervisor) is **deferred post-v1** — hook-driven detection suffices; the name/contract is reserved.
   805	   345	    55	
   806	   346	    56	**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
   807	   347	    57	
   808	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
   809	   349	    59	
   810	   350	    60	**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker. On load, a present marker deterministically rolls the rotation forward (if the snapshot landed) or back (if not); the same marker pattern governs interrupted forced takeovers and interrupted purges (purge resumes from its marker until the whole tree is clean). Retention: last 10 rotations pruned with the history. Doctor warns at journal > 5 MB; perf test: 10k-event replay < 1 s. **Filesystem support boundary: v1 supports local filesystems only** — lock and rename atomicity are not guaranteed on network/shared mounts (NFS/SMB/cloud-sync folders); doctor detects and warns, README states it.
   811	   351	    61	
   812	   352	    62	**Root discovery & degraded modes** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): repo root = nearest ancestor containing `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree-aware: linked worktrees resolve to their own toplevel, shared state stays per-worktree), else cwd — `--root <path>` overrides; nested/monorepo launches therefore resolve to the same bundle deterministically, but **discovery never crosses the boundary of a nested independent git repository** (a `.git` between cwd and a candidate root stops the walk) unless `--root` says otherwise. Non-git directories: supported — `git` section is null, git-dependent features degrade with explicit warnings. Read-only sandboxes (EACCES/EROFS on `.handoff/`): checkpoint fails open with a warning naming the user-executed fallback (`baton checkpoint` run manually outside the sandbox; `receive --print-prompt` never needs writes until `--commit`). All git invocations carry a 5 s timeout (configurable); timeout → git section marked `unavailable`, never a hang.
   813	   353	    63	
   814	   354	    64	**Transcript policy** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): transcript-tail capture at PreCompact is **opt-in and off by default** (`capture.transcriptTail` in `baton.config.json`), bounded (last 10 messages, 8 KB cap), passed through a secret-redaction filter (common credential/token patterns; fixtures with planted secrets prove redaction), stored in a dedicated bundle field excluded from HANDOFF.md by default. `baton purge-transcript` removes the field from **every retained copy** — active snapshot, `.bak`, journal (rewrite-and-rotate under lock), and all `history/` freezes — with a test asserting planted secrets are absent from the entire `.handoff/` tree afterward. **Diagnostics logging contract (iteration 4)**: `.handoff/log/` entries are metadata-only and redacted — raw hook payloads never enter them (fixture-proven) — with bounded retention (last 50 entries / 7 days) and inclusion in the whole-tree purge test.
   815	   355	    65	
   816	   356	    66	**Checkpoint engine**: adapters send pre-normalized `baton/event@1` on stdin (the real API); raw hook payloads get best-effort per-platform extraction (`normalize.mjs`) that never throws — unknowns degrade to `note` events. Idempotent via dedupe keys; journal append always, snapshot rewrite throttled (≥10 events / 30 s / important event types). **Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on all soft failures** so a checkpoint can never break the host harness (`--strict` for CI). `finalize --reason "…" [--reason-class] [--to]` records the switch reason (class inferred from text via the classifier when omitted), refreshes git state, freezes history.
   817	   357	    67	
   818	   358	    68	**Limit detector**: two tiers — **structured signals first** (Claude Code `StopFailure` matcher error types; documented limit-specific fields in codex JSON output), text signatures as fallback. **Exit-code rule (iteration 3): a generic nonzero exit never classifies as usage-limit on its own** — exit 10 requires limit-specific structured or text evidence; nonzero without evidence = `other-error`. Fixture corpus includes non-limit failing processes. Signatures are **versioned data** (`core/data/signatures.v1.json`), seeded with the verified strings for all three platforms, matcher kinds `substring`/`regex`/`json-field`, per-signature confidence, precedence usage-limit > auth > throttle > other-error, `--signatures <path>` overlay for hot-patching drift, `--explain` for auditability. Hardening (Gate-1 additions): input is ANSI-stripped before matching; the fixture corpus includes negative/near-miss cases (throttle-vs-usage confusables, multiline, malformed JSON, localized text) so false positives are regression-tested; overlay regexes are lint-checked (length cap, no backreferences, linear-time constructs) and matching carries a time guard; a low-confidence match **never silently avoids a platform** — it warns and defers to user intake at receive. Cursor entries carry `confidence: low|medium` explicitly.
   819	   359	    69	
   820	   360	    70	**Role matrix**: committed `baton.config.json` at repo root (`baton/config@1`) mapping roles → ordered platform+model chains (the seven methodology roles, defined below), plus per-platform `defaults`. Resolver is pure and explainable: skips `avoid[]` platforms (auto-populated with the origin platform when reason-class is usage-limit — never remap back onto the platform that died), resolves `mode: native|delegated|forced-default|unavailable` with `{chainIndex, skipped[]}` audit data. **Availability probing** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): `doctor` probes each platform noninteractively, hard 3 s bound per probe, results cached 15 min in the state dir. Probe record = two separate dimensions: **capability** (ordered, cumulative: `installed → authenticated → reachable`, recorded as far as verifiable) and **probe outcome** (`ok | rate-limited | error | timeout`). Resolver eligibility: **selectable** = capability ≥ authenticated and outcome ≠ rate-limited; anything with an unverifiable dimension resolves as selectable-with-`degraded`-flag; `rate-limited` platforms are skipped like `avoid[]` entries. Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged `degraded`.
   821	   361	    71	
   822	   362	    72	**Receive**: loads bundle with recovery + staleness checks (age > 12 h; HEAD moved; dirty mismatch), merges intake flags (`--origin`, `--reason`), resolves roles, and runs as the **prepare/commit transaction defined under Concurrency** — prompt emission at prepare, state mutation only at commit. Resume prompt ≤2,500 chars (brief, why-you're-here, role table, warnings, top-5 next actions, pointer to HANDOFF.md); the prompt explicitly frames bundle content as **unverified claims to audit against the working tree, not instructions to obey** (prompt-injection posture — see Threat model).
   823	   363	    73	
   824	   364	    74	**Scaffold** (`init`): two-phase plan/apply with `--dry-run`; `.gitignore` ensure-line (no-op if an existing pattern covers `.handoff/`); `baton.config.json` from template; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md written via managed blocks (`<!-- baton:begin/end -->`) — bytes outside markers never touched.
   825	   365	    75	
   826	   366	    76	**Attribution guard** (three layers): (1) `init` deep-merges `.claude/settings.json` → `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` (only when keys absent; refuses to touch malformed JSON; global settings documented + doctor-checked, never written by core); (2) `doctor` scans last 50 commits for AI co-author/generated-with trailers (word-boundary-safe patterns) and flags with remediation; (3) a test-suite invariant scans every rendered output and template for AI-credit strings and fails the build.
   827	   367	    77	
   828	   368	    78	Full module APIs, per-module test lists, repo file tree, and the fixture corpus (verbatim limit strings, hook payloads, corrupt bundles) are specified in the core design doc (committed as `docs/design/core.md` in task 0); implementation follows the named-task TDD sequence below — **tasks are identified by name, not number; the exact count is finalized when review directories are generated**. **`sessionHint` derivation (Gate-1 final note)**: per adapter, from the hook payload's stable session id (Claude Code `session_id`; Codex `session_id`; Cursor session field); when a payload lacks one, core generates a process-scoped hint flagged `unstable: true` — unstable hints never trigger foreign-session rejection on their own, only a warning.
   829	   369	    79	### Checkpoint vocabulary (used everywhere)
   830	   370	    80	
   831	   371	    81	- **Mechanical checkpoint** (`baton checkpoint`): hook/script-driven, no LLM — git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, timestamps, source platform/model, files touched. <1 s, safe per-turn.
   832	   372	    82	- **Narrative seal** (`baton finalize`, surfaced as `/handoff`): model-written — decisions + rationale, verified-done vs claimed-done, next steps, gotchas, reason for switching.
   833	   373	    83	
   834	   374	    84	Claude Code DOES emit a structured limit-death event (`StopFailure` with a `rate_limit` matcher); Codex and Cursor do not. The design is therefore: event-driven detection where it exists, rolling mechanical checkpoints everywhere (last coherent turn always captured), narrative seals at milestones, and receive compensating for a missing seal by asking the user why they switched and re-deriving git facts live, auditing HANDOFF.md claims against them.
   835	   375	    85	
   836	   376	    86	### Claude Code adapter (Tier A — highest fidelity)
   837	   377	    87	
   838	   378	    88	Plugin root = **repo root**: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (author: SakshamUboweja) with path overrides pointing at `adapters/claude-code/{commands,skills,agents,hooks}` so `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` reaches `core/bin/baton.mjs` directly; `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` makes the repo its own single-entry marketplace (same shape as `openai/codex-plugin-cc`). **Spike task 0 verifies path-override support**; fallback = CI copy step vendoring `core/` under the adapter.
   839	   379	    89	
   840	   380	    90	Hooks (all fail-open — errors log to `.handoff/log/`, exit 0; a checkpoint must never break a session):
   841	   381	    91	
   842	   382	    92	| Event | Use | Timeout |
   843	   383	    93	|---|---|---|
   844	   384	    94	| `StopFailure` (matcher enum — e.g. `rate_limit`, `billing_error`, `server_error` — **snapshot verbatim from the official hooks reference during task 0**; fixtures generated from that canonical list; unknown future values normalize to `unknown` safely) | **The limit-death signal.** Classifies the error (matcher + payload through `baton detect`), writes a fail-open mechanical checkpoint stamped `trigger: stop-failure/<type>`, and on `rate_limit` marks the bundle limit-hit so the next SessionStart (any platform) surfaces it. Output/exit code are ignored by the harness — safe by construction. Tests cover the full snapshot enum. | 30 s |
   845	   385	    95	| `Stop` | Routine mechanical checkpoint per assistant turn (proven codex stop-gate pattern; never emits `decision: block`) | 30 s |
   846	   386	    96	| `PreCompact` | Snapshot context boundary before compaction; transcript-tail capture is **opt-in, off by default** (see core §transcript policy) | 60 s |
   847	   387	    97	| `SessionEnd` | Clean-exit checkpoint | 30 s |
   848	   388	    98	| `SessionStart` | Not a checkpoint: if a sealed or limit-hit bundle from another platform exists, inject "handoff pending — suggest `/baton:receive`" context | 10 s |
   849	   389	    99	
   850	   390	   100	`PostToolUse` rejected: per-tool-call spawns for incoherent mid-turn state; Stop gives the same worst-case staleness (one turn) at a fraction of the cost.
   851	   391	   101	
   852	   392	   102	Commands: **`/baton:handoff`** (model-invocable so Claude can propose it near limits; writes the narrative — auditing every "done" claim against tool evidence — then seals via finalize, then prints the destination's resume command); **`/baton:receive`** (`disable-model-invocation: true`; runs receive → one AskUserQuestion with two questions: origin platform with detected option first, reason for switch → ack runs the core commit transaction (received seal archived, this session adopted as owner, fresh `open` generation; double-receive prevented by the one-time token; command tests assert the active/open + archived/received outcome) → evidence audit of bundle git snapshot vs live HEAD/status → announce role-remap table → auto-continue next step, pausing only per AGENTS.md boundaries); **`/baton:baton-setup`** (doctor + choose surfaces + init + template scaffold with diff preview). Receive-side continuation is a **skill** (`handoff-protocol`), not an agent — the main thread must inherit the task; a subagent would strand context. Optional v2 `handoff-verifier` agent (fresh-context bundle audit) is out of v1 scope.
   853	   393	   103	
   854	   394	   104	### Codex adapter (Tier A− — hook-driven as of Codex >= 0.144)
   855	   395	   105	
   856	   396	   106	Gate-1 correction: Codex now ships lifecycle hooks, so the adapter is redesigned around them. Surfaces: (1) **repo `.codex/hooks.json`** (written by `init --codex`, merged never clobbered): `Stop` → mechanical checkpoint, `PreCompact` → context-boundary checkpoint, `SessionStart` → pending-handoff notice via injected context. No StopFailure equivalent exists on Codex, so a limit death is bounded by the last Stop checkpoint (one turn worst case). (2) `.agents/skills/baton-handoff/SKILL.md` per the Agent Skills standard — carries the receive/handoff protocol, invoked as `$baton-handoff` or by description match. (3) Repo `AGENTS.md` Handoff Protocol section as the always-on instruction layer (narrative checkpoints after subtasks / before risky ops / at wind-down). (4) `~/.codex/prompts/*.md` demoted to **legacy fallback only** (deprecated upstream), written only with `--with-legacy-prompts`. The notify shim is **cut** — hooks make it obsolete; `~/.codex/config.toml` is never touched. **Trust gate** (verified, Gate-1 iteration 2): Codex requires per-definition review of non-managed command hooks — trust is recorded against the hook's hash, and new/changed hooks are skipped until re-trusted via `/hooks`. Setup and doctor therefore report four distinct states per hook — installed / enabled / **trusted** / observed-executing (canary event) — and the fidelity claim is gated on the canary, with setup guiding the user through `/hooks` when review is pending. Hook definitions include `commandWindows` overrides. Fidelity statement ships verbatim in README + doctor: mechanical staleness ≤ 1 turn via Stop hook **once trusted**; narrative staleness bounded by protocol compliance; git state always re-derived at receive. Requires codex-cli >= 0.144 (doctor enforces; older versions fall back to protocol-only Tier C with an explicit warning).
   857	   397	   107	
   858	   398	   108	### Cursor adapter (Tier A− — hook-driven; event names verified against official docs, Gate-1 iteration 2)
   859	   399	   109	
   860	   400	   110	Surfaces: `.cursor/hooks.json` (project-level, `{"version":1,"hooks":{...}}`) with the **verified** events — `stop` → mechanical checkpoint per agent turn (same semantics as Claude Code `Stop`); `afterFileEdit` → debounced checkpoint (debounce enforced by the CLI, one real checkpoint per 2 min); `beforeShellExecution` with a git-commit matcher → checkpoint before agent-issued commits (**documented limitation: commits made through the SCM UI are invisible to hooks — no pre-commit event exists**); `sessionStart` → pending-handoff notice; `preCompact` → context-boundary checkpoint. Plus `.cursor/commands/{receive,handoff,baton-setup}.md` (CLI loading unconfirmed — convenience layer; every behavior also reachable via AGENTS.md, which cursor-agent reads natively, and via the universal fallback **`baton receive --print-prompt`**) and a ≤5-line `.cursor/rules/baton-handoff.mdc` (`alwaysApply: true`). hooks.json written only after explicit confirmation, merged not clobbered; project hooks require a **trusted workspace** — doctor checks trust and gates the fidelity claim on an observed hook canary. Fidelity: mechanical staleness ≤ 1 turn via `stop` when trusted; untrusted/cloud contexts degrade to protocol-only with an explicit warning.
   861	   401	   111	
   862	   402	   112	### Templates: ideal AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md
   863	   403	   113	
   864	   404	   114	Design rule resolving the two-model-family tension: **every shared invariant appears exactly once in AGENTS.md**; model-specific steering is quarantined (short Claude block in CLAUDE.md; scoped Codex notes only if ever needed). Budget: AGENTS.md ≤220 lines (handoff section ≤25), enforced by a template test.   1007	   547	 succeeded in 0ms:
  1008	   548	    50	### Core engine (`core/`)
  1009	   549	    51	
  1010	   550	    52	**Language/tooling**: plain ESM JavaScript (`.mjs`) + JSDoc types checked by `tsc --noEmit --checkJs` (dev-only dep). No build step — hooks invoke source directly (`node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…"`), same as the proven codex plugin. **Zero runtime dependencies**; arg parsing via `node:util` `parseArgs`; **`node:test`** as the framework (golden-file helper ~40 lines with `UPDATE_GOLDEN=1`). Node >= 20. Every command's `run()` takes an injected `io` object (`{cwd, env, stdin, stdout, stderr, fs, execFile, now}`); pure logic (reducers/renderers/resolvers/classifiers) is data-in/data-out; tests run over an in-memory fs fake plus a thin real-fs integration layer.
  1011	   551	    53	
  1012	   552	    54	**CLI surface** (`baton <cmd> --json`): `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover` (forced lock recovery). Frozen exit-code contract: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json` mode prints exactly one envelope `{ok, data, warnings, error}` on stdout. `baton wrap -- <cmd>` (PTY supervisor) is **deferred post-v1** — hook-driven detection suffices; the name/contract is reserved.
  1013	   553	    55	
  1014	   554	    56	**Bundle** (`.handoff/`): single active bundle = `bundle.json` (atomic tmp+rename snapshot, `.bak` of previous good) + `journal.ndjson` (append-only events, torn-tail tolerant) + rendered `HANDOFF.md` + `history/` (unified retention: last 10 entries **per type** — finalize freezes, takeover archives, receive archives — each = frozen snapshot plus rotated journal; receipts needed for replay/audit are always preserved within retained entries). Load = snapshot + replay journal entries past `journalSeq`; recovery paths: `.bak` + replay, or full journal rebuild. Schema `baton/bundle@1`: origin platform/model, task goal/constraints/acceptance, plan steps with status, capped decisions log, files touched, role assignments, git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, handoff finalize block (`status: open|sealed|received` + `receive_log[]`), compaction markers. Size discipline is **deterministic truncation only** (decisions capped first-20+last-150 with marker; no LLM summarization).
  1015	   555	    57	
  1016	   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.
  1017	   557	    59	
  1018	   558	    60	**Journal rotation & crash recovery** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): on every finalize, crash-safe order = write a rotation marker → write frozen snapshot to `history/` → rename `journal.ndjson` alongside it → start a fresh journal seeded with the snapshot's `journalSeq` → clear marker. On load, a present marker deterministically rolls the rotation forward (if the snapshot landed) or back (if not); the same marker pattern governs interrupted forced takeovers and interrupted purges (purge resumes from its marker until the whole tree is clean). Retention: last 10 rotations pruned with the history. Doctor warns at journal > 5 MB; perf test: 10k-event replay < 1 s. **Filesystem support boundary: v1 supports local filesystems only** — lock and rename atomicity are not guaranteed on network/shared mounts (NFS/SMB/cloud-sync folders); doctor detects and warns, README states it.
  1019	   559	    61	
  1020	   560	    62	**Root discovery & degraded modes** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): repo root = nearest ancestor containing `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`, else `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (worktree-aware: linked worktrees resolve to their own toplevel, shared state stays per-worktree), else cwd — `--root <path>` overrides; nested/monorepo launches therefore resolve to the same bundle deterministically, but **discovery never crosses the boundary of a nested independent git repository** (a `.git` between cwd and a candidate root stops the walk) unless `--root` says otherwise. Non-git directories: supported — `git` section is null, git-dependent features degrade with explicit warnings. Read-only sandboxes (EACCES/EROFS on `.handoff/`): checkpoint fails open with a warning naming the user-executed fallback (`baton checkpoint` run manually outside the sandbox; `receive --print-prompt` never needs writes until `--commit`). All git invocations carry a 5 s timeout (configurable); timeout → git section marked `unavailable`, never a hang.
  1021	   561	    63	
  1022	   562	    64	**Transcript policy** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): transcript-tail capture at PreCompact is **opt-in and off by default** (`capture.transcriptTail` in `baton.config.json`), bounded (last 10 messages, 8 KB cap), passed through a secret-redaction filter (common credential/token patterns; fixtures with planted secrets prove redaction), stored in a dedicated bundle field excluded from HANDOFF.md by default. `baton purge-transcript` removes the field from **every retained copy** — active snapshot, `.bak`, journal (rewrite-and-rotate under lock), and all `history/` freezes — with a test asserting planted secrets are absent from the entire `.handoff/` tree afterward. **Diagnostics logging contract (iteration 4)**: `.handoff/log/` entries are metadata-only and redacted — raw hook payloads never enter them (fixture-proven) — with bounded retention (last 50 entries / 7 days) and inclusion in the whole-tree purge test.
  1023	   563	    65	
  1024	   564	    66	**Checkpoint engine**: adapters send pre-normalized `baton/event@1` on stdin (the real API); raw hook payloads get best-effort per-platform extraction (`normalize.mjs`) that never throws — unknowns degrade to `note` events. Idempotent via dedupe keys; journal append always, snapshot rewrite throttled (≥10 events / 30 s / important event types). **Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on all soft failures** so a checkpoint can never break the host harness (`--strict` for CI). `finalize --reason "…" [--reason-class] [--to]` records the switch reason (class inferred from text via the classifier when omitted), refreshes git state, freezes history.
  1025	   565	    67	
  1026	   566	    68	**Limit detector**: two tiers — **structured signals first** (Claude Code `StopFailure` matcher error types; documented limit-specific fields in codex JSON output), text signatures as fallback. **Exit-code rule (iteration 3): a generic nonzero exit never classifies as usage-limit on its own** — exit 10 requires limit-specific structured or text evidence; nonzero without evidence = `other-error`. Fixture corpus includes non-limit failing processes. Signatures are **versioned data** (`core/data/signatures.v1.json`), seeded with the verified strings for all three platforms, matcher kinds `substring`/`regex`/`json-field`, per-signature confidence, precedence usage-limit > auth > throttle > other-error, `--signatures <path>` overlay for hot-patching drift, `--explain` for auditability. Hardening (Gate-1 additions): input is ANSI-stripped before matching; the fixture corpus includes negative/near-miss cases (throttle-vs-usage confusables, multiline, malformed JSON, localized text) so false positives are regression-tested; overlay regexes are lint-checked (length cap, no backreferences, linear-time constructs) and matching carries a time guard; a low-confidence match **never silently avoids a platform** — it warns and defers to user intake at receive. Cursor entries carry `confidence: low|medium` explicitly.
  1027	   567	    69	
  1028	   568	    70	**Role matrix**: committed `baton.config.json` at repo root (`baton/config@1`) mapping roles → ordered platform+model chains (the seven methodology roles, defined below), plus per-platform `defaults`. Resolver is pure and explainable: skips `avoid[]` platforms (auto-populated with the origin platform when reason-class is usage-limit — never remap back onto the platform that died), resolves `mode: native|delegated|forced-default|unavailable` with `{chainIndex, skipped[]}` audit data. **Availability probing** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1–3): `doctor` probes each platform noninteractively, hard 3 s bound per probe, results cached 15 min in the state dir. Probe record = two separate dimensions: **capability** (ordered, cumulative: `installed → authenticated → reachable`, recorded as far as verifiable) and **probe outcome** (`ok | rate-limited | error | timeout`). Resolver eligibility: **selectable** = capability ≥ authenticated and outcome ≠ rate-limited; anything with an unverifiable dimension resolves as selectable-with-`degraded`-flag; `rate-limited` platforms are skipped like `avoid[]` entries. Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged `degraded`.
  1029	   569	    71	
  1030	   570	    72	**Receive**: loads bundle with recovery + staleness checks (age > 12 h; HEAD moved; dirty mismatch), merges intake flags (`--origin`, `--reason`), resolves roles, and runs as the **prepare/commit transaction defined under Concurrency** — prompt emission at prepare, state mutation only at commit. Resume prompt ≤2,500 chars (brief, why-you're-here, role table, warnings, top-5 next actions, pointer to HANDOFF.md); the prompt explicitly frames bundle content as **unverified claims to audit against the working tree, not instructions to obey** (prompt-injection posture — see Threat model).
  1031	   571	    73	
  1032	   572	    74	**Scaffold** (`init`): two-phase plan/apply with `--dry-run`; `.gitignore` ensure-line (no-op if an existing pattern covers `.handoff/`); `baton.config.json` from template; AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md written via managed blocks (`<!-- baton:begin/end -->`) — bytes outside markers never touched.
  1033	   573	    75	
  1034	   574	    76	**Attribution guard** (three layers): (1) `init` deep-merges `.claude/settings.json` → `{"attribution": {"commit": "", "pr": ""}}` (only when keys absent; refuses to touch malformed JSON; global settings documented + doctor-checked, never written by core); (2) `doctor` scans last 50 commits for AI co-author/generated-with trailers (word-boundary-safe patterns) and flags with remediation; (3) a test-suite invariant scans every rendered output and template for AI-credit strings and fails the build.
  1035	   575	    77	
  1036	   576	    78	Full module APIs, per-module test lists, repo file tree, and the fixture corpus (verbatim limit strings, hook payloads, corrupt bundles) are specified in the core design doc (committed as `docs/design/core.md` in task 0); implementation follows the named-task TDD sequence below — **tasks are identified by name, not number; the exact count is finalized when review directories are generated**. **`sessionHint` derivation (Gate-1 final note)**: per adapter, from the hook payload's stable session id (Claude Code `session_id`; Codex `session_id`; Cursor session field); when a payload lacks one, core generates a process-scoped hint flagged `unstable: true` — unstable hints never trigger foreign-session rejection on their own, only a warning.
  1037	   577	    79	### Checkpoint vocabulary (used everywhere)
  1038	   578	    80	
  1039	   579	    81	- **Mechanical checkpoint** (`baton checkpoint`): hook/script-driven, no LLM — git branch/HEAD/dirty summary, timestamps, source platform/model, files touched. <1 s, safe per-turn.
  1040	   580	    82	- **Narrative seal** (`baton finalize`, surfaced as `/handoff`): model-written — decisions + rationale, verified-done vs claimed-done, next steps, gotchas, reason for switching.
  1041	   581	    83	
  1042	   582	    84	Claude Code DOES emit a structured limit-death event (`StopFailure` with a `rate_limit` matcher); Codex and Cursor do not. The design is therefore: event-driven detection where it exists, rolling mechanical checkpoints everywhere (last coherent turn always captured), narrative seals at milestones, and receive compensating for a missing seal by asking the user why they switched and re-deriving git facts live, auditing HANDOFF.md claims against them.

  1181	   721	   147	When only one vendor is reachable, test-author/verifier fall back to different models in fresh sessions and every review artifact header carries `degraded: single-vendor` — weakening is auditable, never silent. Review artifacts extend the wt-* convention exactly: `reviews/<task-id>/{gate-1-plan, subtask-NN-tests, gate-2-final/{reviewer-a, reviewer-b, findings.md}}/iteration-NN/{prompt.md, verdict.md}`, templates ported from `wt-supervisor/reviews/_templates/`. The loop: plan doc in `docs/plans/` with goal + genuine constraints (falsifiable acceptance criteria) → Gate 1 → per-subtask test-first with the implementer forbidden from weakening/deleting tests (modifications re-enter verification) → dual independent fresh-context final reviews → collate `findings.md` → fix blocking items, re-review by the raising reviewer → loop until acceptance constraints are met with evidence attached. **Iteration budget (Saksham's rule): every review gate loops at most 5 times — hard stop after the 5th iteration; on exhaustion, the gate ends with the outstanding findings escalated to Saksham for a human decision instead of a 6th run.** This cap is encoded in the AGENTS.md template's review-gates section and applies to building this repo too.

  2759	  2299	   110	/** @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p */

  2791	  2331	   142	      );

  2799	  2339	   150	    case 'dead': {
  2800	  2340	   151	      // Atomic dead-lock reclaim (gate-2 iter-2 B1, hardened iter-3 finding-1).

  2808	  2348	   159	      // transient contention. The fencing token stays the write-time backstop.

  2850	  2390	   201	/**
  2851	  2391	   202	 * Fence-guarded release: the lock dir is removed only while owner.json still
  2852	  2392	   203	 * carries OUR token. A holder that paused past a takeover must not delete the
  2853	  2393	   204	 * competitor's lock on its way out — release is a write like any other.
  2854	  2394	   205	 * @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p @param {string} token
  2855	  2395	   206	 */
  2856	  2396	   207	function release(io, p, token) {
  2857	  2397	   208	  try {
  2858	  2398	   209	    const current = JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(p.owner, 'utf8'));
  2859	  2399	   210	    if (current.fencingToken !== token) return; // a competitor took over — their lock, not ours
  2860	  2400	   211	  } catch {

  2862	  2402	   213	  }
  2863	  2403	   214	  io.fs.rmSync(p.lockDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
  2864	  2404	   215	}
  2865	  2405	   216	
  2866	  2406	   217	// A live same-host holder is transient by design — operation-scoped locks are
  2867	  2407	   218	// held for milliseconds — so contention waits instead of dropping the
  2868	  2408	   219	// operation (gate-2 fix 12: simultaneous checkpoints must all land). The budget
  2869	  2409	   220	// is generous (≈15 s): under heavy load a writer may be starved of scheduling
  2870	  2410	   221	// for seconds, and waiting is strictly safer than silently dropping its work.
  2871	  2411	   222	// Every other contended state (torn, cross-host) stays fail-fast: waiting
  2872	  2412	   223	// cannot make those provably safe.
  2873	  2413	   224	const DEFAULT_RETRY = { attempts: 600, delayMs: 25 };

  2876	  2416	   227	const sleepMs = (/** @type {number} */ ms) => {
  2877	  2417	   228	  Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms);
  2878	  2418	   229	};

  2881	  2421	   232	 * Acquire → run fn(token) → release (also on throw). Synchronous by design:

  2883	  2423	   234	 * a bounded budget (override via io.lockRetry = {attempts, delayMs}).

  2886	  2426	   237	export function withLock(root, io, fn) {
  2887	  2427	   238	  const p = lockPaths(root);
  2888	  2428	   239	  // Jail BEFORE any lock mutation (gate-2 iter-2 B2): a symlinked .handoff or

  2899	  2439	   250	      break;

  2906	  2446	   257	    }

  2912	  2452	   263	  }
  2913	  2453	   264	}

  2915	  2455	   266	/**
  2916	  2456	   267	 * Fast-abort layer: re-read the published token immediately before a write; a
  2917	  2457	   268	 * holder that paused past its last check aborts instead of clobbering.

  2920	  2460	   271	export function guardedWrite(root, io, token, fn) {

  2922	  2462	   273	  let current = null;

  2942	  2482	   293	export function recoverLock(root, io, opts = {}) {
  2943	  2483	   294	  void opts;

  2945	  2485	   296	  // Jail before recovery (gate-2 iter-2 B2): recoverLock removes the lock dir,
  2946	  2486	   297	  // so a symlinked managed tree must be refused first — even with force, a
  2947	  2487	   298	  // symlink is never provably safe to delete through.
  2948	  2488	   299	  const safe = checkHandoffTree(root, io);
  2949	  2489	   300	  if (!safe.ok) return { recovered: false, refusedReason: `${safe.problem} — refusing recovery` };

  2952	  2492	   303	    case 'free':

  2954	  2494	   305	    case 'dead': {

  2956	  2496	   307	      // inspect-then-rmSync (iter-4 I1): the old bare rmSync had a TOCTOU — a
  2957	  2497	   308	      // competitor could win the rename-arbitrated dead-reclaim between this

  2959	  2499	   310	      // delete a lock whose owner is alive. acquire() re-inspects atomically and

  2961	  2501	   312	      // are mutually exclusive: acquire either reclaims a still-dead lock (and
  2962	  2502	   313	      // journals the takeover under the lock) or throws because it is now
  2963	  2503	   314	      // live/torn — in which case we refuse rather than steal. release() then
  2964	  2504	   315	      // leaves the slot clear.
  2965	  2505	   316	      let token;
  2966	  2506	   317	      try {
  2967	  2507	   318	        token = acquire(io, p);
  2968	  2508	   319	      } catch (err) {
  2969	  2509	   320	        return { recovered: false, refusedReason: /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err) };
  2970	  2510	   321	      }
  2971	  2511	   322	      release(io, p, token);
  2972	  2512	   323	      return { recovered: true, refusedReason: null };
  2973	  2513	   324	    }
  2974	  2514	   325	    case 'live':
  2975	  2515	   326	      return {
  2976	  2516	   327	        recovered: false,
  2977	  2517	   328	        refusedReason: `lock is held by a live process (pid ${s.owner.pid} on ${s.owner.host}) — terminate that process first.`,
  2978	  2518	   329	      };
  2979	  2519	   330	    case 'cross-host':
  2980	  2520	   331	      return {
  2981	  2521	   332	        recovered: false,
  2982	  2522	   333	        refusedReason: `lock is held from another host ('${s.owner.host}', this is '${io.host}') — cross-host locks are never provably safe to steal, even with force. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
  2983	  2523	   334	      };
  2984	  2524	   335	    case 'torn':

  3084	  2624	    17	const THROTTLE_EVENT_COUNT = 10;
  3085	  2625	    18	
  3086	  2626	    19	// Transcript tail bounds (plan §Transcript policy): last 10 messages, 8 KB cap,
  3087	  2627	    20	// opt-in via baton.config.json capture.transcriptTail, PreCompact only.
  3088	  2628	    21	const TAIL_MESSAGES = 10;
  3089	  2629	    22	const TAIL_BYTES = 8192;
  3090	  2630	    23	
  3091	  2631	    24	/**
  3092	  2632	    25	 * Opt-in transcript-tail capture (gate-2 fix 10). Returns the bounded,
  3093	  2633	    26	 * redacted tail or null when the gate is closed: config off (the default),
  3094	  2634	    27	 * not a PreCompact payload, no usable transcript_path, or an unreadable /
  3095	  2635	    28	 * symlinked file. The path comes from an untrusted hook payload — it is read
  3096	  2636	    29	 * only under explicit opt-in, must lstat as a regular file, and its content
  3097	  2637	    30	 * passes the secret-redaction filter before storage.
  3098	  2638	    31	 * @param {string} root @param {any} raw parsed hook payload @param {any} io
  3099	  2639	    32	 * @returns {string | null}
  3100	  2640	    33	 */
  3101	  2641	    34	function captureTranscriptTail(root, raw, io) {
  3102	  2642	    35	  const cfg = safeReadJson(io.fs, `${root}/baton.config.json`);
  3103	  2643	    36	  if (!cfg.ok || cfg.value?.capture?.transcriptTail !== true) return null;
  3104	  2644	    37	
  3105	  2645	    38	  const eventName = raw && typeof raw === 'object' ? (raw.hook_event_name ?? raw.event) : null;
  3106	  2646	    39	  if (typeof eventName !== 'string' || !/precompact/i.test(eventName)) return null;
  3107	  2647	    40	  const path = raw.transcript_path;
  3108	  2648	    41	  if (typeof path !== 'string' || path.length === 0) return null;
  3109	  2649	    42	
  3110	  2650	    43	  try {
  3111	  2651	    44	    if (!io.fs.lstatSync(path).isFile()) return null;
  3112	  2652	    45	    // Allowlist the transcript path (gate-2 iter-2 m1): the payload is
  3113	  2653	    46	    // untrusted, so its resolved realpath must sit under the repo root, the
  3114	  2654	    47	    // user's ~/.claude tree (where Claude Code actually writes transcripts),
  3115	  2655	    48	    // or a configured capture.transcriptDir — never an arbitrary readable file.
  3116	  2656	    49	    const fileReal = io.fs.realpathSync(path);
  3117	  2657	    50	    // On POSIX a backslash is a LEGAL filename character, not a separator, so
  3118	  2658	    51	    // normalizing '\\'→'/' in the containment check (isContained) could make an
  3119	  2659	    52	    // out-of-tree sibling like '/repo\\evil/f' appear contained (iter-4 I9).
  3120	  2660	    53	    // The transcript path is the one fully-untrusted path that reaches
  3121	  2661	    54	    // containment, so refuse a backslash-bearing realpath off Windows.
  3122	  2662	    55	    if (io.platform !== 'win32' && String(fileReal).includes('\\')) return null;
  3123	  2663	    56	    /** @type {string[]} */
  3124	  2664	    57	    const allowed = [root];
  3125	  2665	    58	    const home = io.env?.HOME;
  3126	  2666	    59	    if (typeof home === 'string' && home.length > 0) allowed.push(`${home}/.claude`);
  3127	  2667	    60	    const dir = cfg.value?.capture?.transcriptDir;
  3128	  2668	    61	    if (typeof dir === 'string' && dir.length > 0) allowed.push(dir);
  3129	  2669	    62	    const under = (/** @type {string} */ base) => {
  3130	  2670	    63	      let baseReal;
  3131	  2671	    64	      try {
  3132	  2672	    65	        baseReal = io.fs.realpathSync(base);
  3133	  2673	    66	      } catch {
  3134	  2674	    67	        baseReal = base;
  3135	  2675	    68	      }
  3136	  2676	    69	      // Compare on normalized forward-slash spellings (iter-3 F9): raw Windows
  3137	  2677	    70	      // backslash realpaths never satisfy a forward-slash containment, so
  3138	  2678	    71	      // opt-in capture would silently never fire.
  3139	  2679	    72	      return isContained(baseReal, fileReal);
  3140	  2680	    73	    };
  3141	  2681	    74	    if (!allowed.some(under)) return null;
  3142	  2682	    75	
  3143	  2683	    76	    const text = io.fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
  3144	  2684	    77	    const lines = text.split('\n').filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l.trim() !== '');
  3145	  2685	    78	    let tail = lines.slice(-TAIL_MESSAGES).join('\n');
  3146	  2686	    79	    if (Buffer.byteLength(tail) > TAIL_BYTES) {
  3147	  2687	    80	      tail = Buffer.from(tail).subarray(-TAIL_BYTES).toString('utf8');
  3148	  2688	    81	    }
  3149	  2689	    82	    return redactSecrets(tail);
  3150	  2690	    83	  } catch {
  3151	  2691	    84	    return null; // unreadable transcript is never a checkpoint failure
  3152	  2692	    85	  }
  3153	  2693	    86	}
  3154	  2694	    87	
  3155	  2695	    88	/** Event-shaped: an object carrying a string `type`. */
  3156	  2696	    89	const isEventShaped = (/** @type {any} */ v) => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) && typeof v.type === 'string';
  3157	  2697	    90	
  3158	  2698	    91	/**
  3159	  2699	    92	 * Tolerant stdin parse (live /baton:handoff failure: a model sent one event
  3160	  2700	    93	 * per line and the whole narrative checkpoint silently failed). Accept the
  3161	  2701	    94	 * canonical single JSON value, a bare array of events, or NDJSON where every
  3162	  2702	    95	 * line is an event object or a {schema, events} wrapper. All-or-nothing: one
  3163	  2703	    96	 * non-event element fails the whole parse — never a partial apply.
  3164	  2704	    97	 * @param {string} text @returns {{ok: true, raw: any} | {ok: false, why?: string}}
  3165	  2705	    98	 */
  3166	  2706	    99	function parseStdin(text) {
  3167	  2707	   100	  let single;
  3168	  2708	   101	  let singleOk = false;
  3169	  2709	   102	  try {
  3170	  2710	   103	    single = JSON.parse(text);
  3171	  2711	   104	    singleOk = true;
  3172	  2712	   105	  } catch {
  3173	  2713	   106	    singleOk = false;
  3174	  2714	   107	  }
  3175	  2715	   108	  if (singleOk) {
  3176	  2716	   109	    if (Array.isArray(single)) {
  3177	  2717	   110	      return single.every(isEventShaped) ? { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: single } } : { ok: false };
  3178	  2718	   111	    }
  3179	  2719	   112	    // A closest-miss of the documented wrapper — an events array whose schema
  3180	  2720	   113	    // key is missing or wrong — must ERROR, never silently degrade to a junk
  3181	  2721	   114	    // note with ok:true (the model cannot self-correct from a success
  3182	  2722	   115	    // envelope while its narrative was discarded).
  3183	  2723	   116	    if (single !== null && typeof single === 'object' && Array.isArray(single.events) && single.schema !== 'baton/event@1') {
  3184	  2724	   117	      return { ok: false, why: `stdin carries an events array but schema is ${single.schema === undefined ? 'missing' : JSON.stringify(single.schema)} — use {"schema":"baton/event@1","events":[…]}` };
  3185	  2725	   118	    }
  3186	  2726	   119	    // A single bare event object (string `type`, none of the raw-hook payload
  3187	  2727	   120	    // markers) is one of the two most likely readings of "pipe events on
  3188	  2728	   121	    // stdin" — accept it as that event instead of degrading it to a junk note.
  3189	  2729	   122	    if (
  3190	  2730	   123	      isEventShaped(single) &&
  3191	  2731	   124	      single.schema === undefined &&
  3192	  2732	   125	      !('hook_event_name' in single) &&
  3193	  2733	   126	      !('session_id' in single) &&
  3194	  2734	   127	      !('event' in single)
  3195	  2735	   128	    ) {
  3196	  2736	   129	      return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: [single] } };
  3197	  2737	   130	    }
  3198	  2738	   131	    return { ok: true, raw: single };
  3199	  2739	   132	  }
  3200	  2740	   133	  const lines = text.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l !== '');
  3201	  2741	   134	  if (lines.length === 0) return { ok: false };
  3202	  2742	   135	  /** @type {any[]} */
  3203	  2743	   136	  const events = [];
  3204	  2744	   137	  for (const line of lines) {
  3205	  2745	   138	    let v;
  3206	  2746	   139	    try {
  3207	  2747	   140	      v = JSON.parse(line);
  3208	  2748	   141	    } catch {
  3209	  2749	   142	      return { ok: false };
  3210	  2750	   143	    }
  3211	  2751	   144	    if (v && typeof v === 'object' && v.schema === 'baton/event@1' && Array.isArray(v.events)) {
  3212	  2752	   145	      if (!v.events.every(isEventShaped)) return { ok: false };
  3213	  2753	   146	      events.push(...v.events);
  3214	  2754	   147	    } else if (isEventShaped(v)) {
  3215	  2755	   148	      events.push(v);
  3216	  2756	   149	    } else {
  3217	  2757	   150	      return { ok: false };
  3218	  2758	   151	    }
  3219	  2759	   152	  }
  3220	  2760	   153	  return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events } };
  3221	  2761	   154	}
  3222	  2762	   155	
  3223	  2763	   156	/**
  3224	  2764	   157	 * `baton checkpoint` — mechanical checkpoint from a hook payload on stdin.
  3225	  2765	   158	 * Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on every soft failure so a checkpoint can never
  3226	  2766	   159	 * break the host harness; `--strict` opts into hard failures (CI).
  3227	  2767	   160	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
  3228	  2768	   161	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
  3229	  2769	   162	 */
  3230	  2770	   163	export async function cmdCheckpoint(args, io) {
  3231	  2771	   164	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { platform: 'string', model: 'string', trigger: 'string', debounce: 'string', strict: 'boolean', 'take-over': 'boolean' });
  3232	  2772	   165	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'checkpoint', parsed.error);
  3233	  2773	   166	  const flags = parsed.flags;
  3234	  2774	   167	  const strict = flags.strict === true;
  3235	  2775	   168	  const platform = typeof flags.platform === 'string' ? flags.platform : null;
  3236	  2776	   169	  if (!platform) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', '--platform <claude-code|codex|cursor> is required');
  3237	  2777	   170	  const pErr = platformError(platform);
  3238	  2778	   171	  if (pErr) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', pErr);
  3239	  2779	   172	
  3240	  2780	   173	  try {
  3241	  2781	   174	    return await run(flags, platform, io);
  3242	  2782	   175	  } catch (err) {
  3243	  2783	   176	    const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err);
  3244	  2784	   177	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'checkpoint-failed', msg } });
  3245	  2785	   178	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: ${msg}\n`);
  3246	  2786	   179	    return strict ? 1 : 0;
  3247	  2787	   180	  }
  3248	  2788	   181	}
  3249	  2789	   182	
  3250	  2790	   183	/**
  3251	  2791	   184	 * @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
  3252	  2792	   185	 * @param {string} platform
  3253	  2793	   186	 * @param {any} io
  3254	  2794	   187	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
  3255	  2795	   188	 */
  3256	  2796	   189	async function run(flags, platform, io) {
  3257	  2797	   190	  const strict = flags.strict === true;
  3258	  2798	   191	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
  3259	  2799	   192	  const paths = bundlePaths(root);
  3260	  2800	   193	  // The --json contract (gate-2 fix 11): exactly one envelope on stdout for
  3261	  2801	   194	  // every exit path — the exit code stays governed by hook-safety.
  3262	  2802	   195	  const finish = (/** @type {any} */ env, /** @type {number} */ code) => {
  3263	  2803	   196	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, env);
  3264	  2804	   197	    return code;
  3265	  2805	   198	  };
  3266	  2806	   199	
  3267	  2807	   200	  const parsed = parseStdin(typeof io.stdin === 'string' ? io.stdin : '');
  3268	  2808	   201	  if (!parsed.ok) {
  3269	  2809	   202	    const why = parsed.why ?? 'send one JSON value ({"schema":"baton/event@1","events":[…]}), a JSON array of events, or NDJSON event lines';
  3270	  2810	   203	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: stdin could not be parsed — ${why}\n`);
  3271	  2811	   204	    return finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'bad-stdin', msg: why } }, strict ? 1 : 0);
  3272	  2812	   205	  }
  3273	  2813	   206	  const raw = parsed.raw;
  3274	  2814	   207	
  3275	  2815	   208	  const session = { host: io.host, pid: io.pid, startTime: io.startTime };
  3276	  2816	   209	  // The hook command declares which event it is (--trigger), so event identity
  3277	  2817	   210	  // never depends on parsing each harness's payload shape (Cursor's stop payload
  3278	  2818	   211	  // names the event nowhere normalize could find it).
  3279	  2819	   212	  const explicitEvent = typeof flags.trigger === 'string' ? flags.trigger : undefined;
  3280	  2820	   213	  const events = normalizeHookPayload(raw, platform, session, explicitEvent);
  3281	  2821	   214	  if (events.length === 0) return finish({ ok: true, data: { events: 0, rewritten: false } }, 0);
  3282	  2822	   215	
  3283	  2823	   216	  // Opt-in transcript tail (gate-2 fix 10): rides the journal as its own
  3284	  2824	   217	  // IMPORTANT event so the snapshot rewrite below persists it, and purge can
  3285	  2825	   218	  // strip it from every retained copy by its property name.
  3286	  2826	   219	  const tail = captureTranscriptTail(root, raw, io);
  3287	  2827	   220	  if (tail !== null) {
  3288	  2828	   221	    events.push({
  3289	  2829	   222	      type: 'transcript.set',
  3290	  2830	   223	      payload: { transcript: { capturedAt: io.now(), tail } },
  3291	  2831	   224	      source: platform,
  3292	  2832	   225	      sessionHint: events[0]?.sessionHint,
  3293	  2833	   226	      unstable: events[0]?.unstable ?? true,
  3294	  2834	   227	    });
  3295	  2835	   228	  }
  3296	  2836	   229	
  3297	  2837	   230	  const { bundle, warnings, unsafe } = loadBundle(root, io);
  3298	  2838	   231	  for (const w of warnings) io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: ${w}\n`);
  3299	  2839	   232	
  3300	  2840	   233	  // An unsafe managed tree (symlinked .handoff — gate-2 fix 6) is NOT "no
  3301	  2841	   234	  // bundle yet": seeding here would write through the link. Refuse everything;
  3302	  2842	   235	  // hook-safety keeps the refusal soft outside --strict.
  3303	  2843	   236	  if (unsafe === true) {
  3304	  2844	   237	    io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: managed tree failed the symlink/realpath jail — nothing written\n');
  3305	  2845	   238	    return finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'unsafe-tree', msg: warnings[0] ?? 'managed tree failed the jail check' } }, strict ? 1 : 0);
  3306	  2846	   239	  }
  3307	  2847	   240	
  3308	  2848	   241	  // Opt-in debounce (gate-2 major 14; Cursor afterFileEdit fires per edit):
  3309	  2849	   242	  // at most one real checkpoint per window, tracked by a per-platform stamp.
  3310	  2850	   243	  // The read-and-set runs UNDER the repo lock (gate-2 iter-2 M5) so two
  3311	  2851	   244	  // simultaneous afterFileEdit hooks can't both observe no stamp and both
  3312	  2852	   245	  // checkpoint — exactly one wins the window.
  3313	  2853	   246	  if (flags.debounce !== undefined) {
  3314	  2854	   247	    const seconds = Number(flags.debounce);
  3315	  2855	   248	    if (!Number.isFinite(seconds) || seconds <= 0) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', '--debounce <seconds> must be a positive number');
  3316	  2856	   249	    const stampPath = `${paths.logDir}/debounce-${platform}.json`;
  3317	  2857	   250	    const proceed = withLock(root, io, () => {
  3318	  2858	   251	      const stamp = safeReadJson(io.fs, stampPath);
  3319	  2859	   252	      if (stamp.ok && typeof stamp.value?.at === 'string' && Date.parse(io.now()) - Date.parse(stamp.value.at) < seconds * 1000) {
  3320	  2860	   253	        return false;
  3321	  2861	   254	      }
  3322	  2862	   255	      ensureDir(io.fs, paths.logDir);
  3323	  2863	   256	      atomicWriteJson(io.fs, stampPath, { at: io.now() });
  3324	  2864	   257	      return true;
  3325	  2865	   258	    });
  3326	  2866	   259	    if (!proceed) return finish({ ok: true, data: { events: 0, rewritten: false, debounced: true } }, 0);
  3327	  2867	   260	  }
  3328	  2868	   261	
  3329	  2869	   262	  let active = bundle;
  3330	  2870	   263	  let mustRewrite = false;
  3331	  2871	   264	
  3332	  2872	   265	  // Semantic isolation (plan §Concurrency): a stable foreign session or a
  3333	  2873	   266	  // mismatched origin platform must not merge into the active bundle. Checked
  3334	  2874	   267	  // before ANY write so a rejection leaves the whole tree untouched.
  3335	  2875	   268	  const originHint = active?.origin?.sessionHint;
  3336	  2876	   269	  const hasStableOwner = active !== null && typeof originHint === 'string' && originHint.length > 0 && active.origin.unstable !== true;
  3337	  2877	   270	  const stableIncoming = events.find(
  3338	  2878	   271	    (/** @type {any} */ e) => typeof e.sessionHint === 'string' && e.sessionHint.length > 0 && e.unstable === false,
  3339	  2879	   272	  );
  3340	  2880	   273	  const unstableIncoming = events.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e.unstable === true);
  3341	  2881	   274	
  3342	  2882	   275	  if (hasStableOwner) {
  3343	  2883	   276	    // Foreign = a different stable session, OR any platform mismatch — the
  3344	  2884	   277	    // platform is provable even when the events carry no session hint (audit
  3345	  2885	   278	    // finding: a hint-less /baton:handoff narrative from claude-code silently
  3346	  2886	   279	    // merged into — then sealed — a codex-owned bundle, corrupting the origin
  3347	  2887	   280	    // the receive-side role avoidance keys on).
  3348	  2888	   281	    const incomingLabel = stableIncoming ? stableIncoming.sessionHint : '(no session hint)';
  3349	  2889	   282	    const foreign = stableIncoming
  3350	  2890	   283	      ? stableIncoming.sessionHint !== originHint || platform !== active.origin.platform
  3351	  2891	   284	      : platform !== active.origin.platform;
  3352	  2892	   285	    if (foreign && flags['take-over'] !== true) {
  3353	  2893	   286	      io.stderr.write(
  3354	  2894	   287	        `baton checkpoint: event from a foreign session/origin (${platform}/${incomingLabel} vs active ${active.origin.platform}/${originHint}) — rejected to keep sessions isolated; rerun with --take-over to archive the active bundle and start fresh\n`,
  3355	  2895	   288	      );
  3356	  2896	   289	      return finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'foreign-session', msg: 'event from a foreign session/origin rejected; rerun with --take-over' } }, 0);
  3357	  2897	   290	    }
  3358	  2898	   291	    if (foreign) {
  3359	  2899	   292	      rotateJournal(root, 'takeover', io);
  3360	  2900	   293	      const fresh = emptyBundle(
  3361	  2901	   294	        { platform, model: typeof flags.model === 'string' ? flags.model : 'unknown', goal: active.task?.goal ?? 'unknown' },
  3362	  2902	   295	        io.now(),
  3363	  2903	   296	      );
  3364	  2904	   297	      if (stableIncoming) fresh.origin.sessionHint = stableIncoming.sessionHint;
  3365	  2905	   298	      writeSnapshot(root, fresh, io);
  3366	  2906	   299	      io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: took over — prior bundle archived to history/, fresh bundle owned by ${platform}/${incomingLabel}\n`);
  3367	  2907	   300	      active = fresh;
  3368	  2908	   301	      mustRewrite = true;
  3369	  2909	   302	    }
  3370	  2910	   303	  }
  3371	  2911	   304	
  3372	  2912	   305	  if (unstableIncoming) {
  3373	  2913	   306	    io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: event carries an unstable (generated) session hint — ownership unverifiable; applied with this warning only\n');
  3374	  2914	   307	  }
  3375	  2915	   308	
  3376	  2916	   309	  if (active === null) {
  3377	  2917	   310	    active = emptyBundle(
  3378	  2918	   311	      { platform, model: typeof flags.model === 'string' ? flags.model : 'unknown', goal: 'unknown' },
  3379	  2919	   312	      io.now(),
  3380	  2920	   313	    );
  3381	  2921	   314	    writeSnapshot(root, active, io);
  3382	  2922	   315	    // Self-applying seed event (gate-2 iter-2 B6): a journal-only rebuild
  3383	  2923	   316	    // (snapshot + .bak both lost) must restore the bundle's identity, not the
  3384	  2924	   317	    // "unknown" placeholder resolveBase seeds. bundle.seed carries bundleId,
  3385	  2925	   318	    // origin, task, and generation and is applied on replay.
  3386	  2926	   319	    appendJournal(
  3387	  2927	   320	      root,
  3388	  2928	   321	      {
  3389	  2929	   322	        ts: io.now(),
  3390	  2930	   323	        type: 'bundle.seed',
  3391	  2931	   324	        payload: {
  3392	  2932	   325	          bundleId: active.bundleId,
  3393	  2933	   326	          generation: active.generation,
  3394	  2934	   327	          createdAt: active.createdAt,

  4032	  3572	    59	/** @param {string} platform @param {string | null} v @returns {{id: string, ok: boolean, detail: string}} */
  4033	  3573	    60	function versionCheck(platform, v) {

  4035	  3575	    62	  if (v === null) {

  4037	  3577	    64	  }

  4041	  3581	    68	  }

  4048	  3588	    75	/**
  4049	  3589	    76	 * Recursively collect every `command`/`commandWindows` STRING under a hook
  4050	  3590	    77	 * definition (codex nests hooks[].hooks[].command; cursor is [].command). Only
  4051	  3591	    78	 * real command fields — never matchers, comments, or serialized metadata — so
  4052	  3592	    79	 * enablement keys on an actual invocation (iter-5 A3).
  4053	  3593	    80	 * @param {any} def @returns {string[]}
  4054	  3594	    81	 */
  4055	  3595	    82	function hookCommands(def) {
  4056	  3596	    83	  /** @type {string[]} */
  4057	  3597	    84	  const out = [];
  4058	  3598	    85	  const walk = (/** @type {any} */ node) => {
  4059	  3599	    86	    if (Array.isArray(node)) {
  4060	  3600	    87	      for (const n of node) walk(n);
  4061	  3601	    88	    } else if (node && typeof node === 'object') {
  4062	  3602	    89	      if (typeof node.command === 'string') out.push(node.command);
  4063	  3603	    90	      if (typeof node.commandWindows === 'string') out.push(node.commandWindows);
  4064	  3604	    91	      if (Array.isArray(node.hooks)) walk(node.hooks);
  4065	  3605	    92	    }
  4066	  3606	    93	  };
  4067	  3607	    94	  walk(def);
  4068	  3608	    95	  return out;
  4069	  3609	    96	}
