  4071	  3611	    98	/**
  4072	  3612	    99	 * Codex/Cursor hook surface: installed / enabled / trusted / observed-executing.
  4073	  3613	   100	 * `installed` = the hooks file references baton at all; `enabled` = the
  4074	  3614	   101	 * mechanical-checkpoint hook (the `checkpointEvent` key: codex `Stop`, cursor
  4075	  3615	   102	 * `stop`) declares a `baton checkpoint` COMMAND (iter-5 A3); `trusted` is not
  4076	  3616	   103	 * externally verifiable → 'unknown'; `observed` = a platform-sourced checkpoint
  4077	  3617	   104	 * whose payload.trigger is the checkpointEvent (the per-turn Stop canary). The
  4078	  3618	   105	 * ≤1-turn fidelity claim is gated on enabled AND observed.
  4079	  3619	   106	 * @param {any} io @param {string} root @param {any} p bundlePaths
  4080	  3620	   107	 * @param {string} platform @param {string} relPath @param {string} checkpointEvent @param {string} trustNote
  4081	  3621	   108	 */
  4082	  3622	   109	function hookSurfaceCheck(io, root, p, platform, relPath, checkpointEvent, trustNote) {
  4083	  3623	   110	  const id = `${platform}-hooks`;
  4084	  3624	   111	  let text = null;
  4085	  3625	   112	  try {
  4086	  3626	   113	    text = io.fs.readFileSync(`${root}/${relPath}`, 'utf8');
  4087	  3627	   114	  } catch {
  4088	  3628	   115	    text = null;
  4089	  3629	   116	  }
  4090	  3630	   117	  const installed = text !== null && text.includes('baton');
  4091	  3631	   118	  if (!installed) {
  4092	  3632	   119	    return {
  4093	  3633	   120	      id,
  4094	  3634	   121	      ok: true,
  4095	  3635	   122	      states: { installed: false, enabled: false, trusted: 'unknown', observed: false },
  4096	  3636	   123	      detail: `not installed — run 'baton init --${platform}' to write ${relPath}`,
  4097	  3637	   124	    };
  4098	  3638	   125	  }
  4099	  3639	   126	  // enabled: the checkpoint hook itself is declared with a `baton checkpoint`
  4100	  3640	   127	  // COMMAND (iter-5 A3) — inspect the actual command/commandWindows fields, not
  4101	  3641	   128	  // the serialized blob (a matcher/comment mentioning baton must not count). A
  4102	  3642	   129	  // file that references baton only in a session-start hook is installed but NOT
  4103	  3643	   130	  // checkpoint-enabled.
  4104	  3644	   131	  let enabled = false;
  4105	  3645	   132	  try {
  4106	  3646	   133	    const cfg = JSON.parse(/** @type {string} */ (text));
  4107	  3647	   134	    // Match the bare `baton checkpoint` form AND the absolute
  4108	  3648	   135	    // `"<node>" "<…/baton.mjs>" checkpoint` form init now writes (the entry
  4109	  3649	   136	    // script may be quote-terminated: `baton.mjs" checkpoint`).
  4110	  3650	   137	    enabled = hookCommands(cfg?.hooks?.[checkpointEvent]).some((c) => /\bbaton(?:\.mjs)?["']?\s+checkpoint\b/.test(c));
  4111	  3651	   138	  } catch {
  4112	  3652	   139	    enabled = false;
  4113	  3653	   140	  }
  4114	  3654	   141	  // observed: a mechanical checkpoint from THIS platform's CHECKPOINT hook is
  4115	  3655	   142	  // recorded — the journal entry must be platform-sourced AND carry
  4116	  3656	   143	  // payload.trigger === checkpointEvent (iter-5 A3). normalize stamps the hook
  4117	  3657	   144	  // event name as payload.trigger, so a SessionStart/PreCompact/triggerless
  4118	  3658	   145	  // entry no longer masquerades as the per-turn Stop canary.
  4119	  3659	   146	  let observed = false;
  4120	  3660	   147	  try {
  4121	  3661	   148	    for (const e of readAllTolerant(io.fs, p.journal).entries) {
  4122	  3662	   149	      const mine = String(e?.writerId ?? '').startsWith(`${platform}-`) || e?.source === platform;
  4123	  3663	   150	      if (mine && e?.payload?.trigger === checkpointEvent) {
  4124	  3664	   151	        observed = true;
  4125	  3665	   152	        break;
  4126	  3666	   153	      }
  4127	  3667	   154	    }
  4128	  3668	   155	  } catch {
  4129	  3669	   156	    observed = false;
  4130	  3670	   157	  }
  4131	  3671	   158	  const states = { installed: true, enabled, trusted: 'unknown', observed };
  4132	  3672	   159	  // The ≤1-turn claim needs the checkpoint hook DECLARED (enabled) AND OBSERVED —
  4133	  3673	   160	  // neither alone suffices.
  4134	  3674	   161	  const fidelityHolds = enabled && observed;
  4135	  3675	   162	  const enabledNote = enabled ? `${checkpointEvent} checkpoint hook enabled` : `${checkpointEvent} checkpoint hook NOT declared (enabled=false)`;
  4136	  3676	   163	  return {
  4137	  3677	   164	    id,
  4138	  3678	   165	    ok: true,
  4139	  3679	   166	    states,
  4140	  3680	   167	    detail: fidelityHolds
  4141	  3681	   168	      ? `installed, ${enabledNote}; trusted=unknown (not externally verifiable); execution OBSERVED (canary) — the ≤1-turn mechanical-staleness claim holds`
  4142	  3682	   169	      : `installed, ${enabledNote}; trusted=unknown — ${trustNote}; ${observed ? 'execution observed but' : 'execution not yet observed —'} the ≤1-turn fidelity claim is gated on the ${checkpointEvent} canary + enablement`,
  4143	  3683	   170	  };
  4144	  3684	   171	}

  4146	  3686	   173	// Noninteractive status probes per platform (docs/design/platform-notes.md CLIs).

  4174	  3714	   201	/**
  4175	  3715	   202	 * Classify one probe invocation per the two-dimension record: capability is
  4176	  3716	   203	 * the ordered ladder verified as far as the evidence goes; outcome is what the
  4177	  3717	   204	 * probe itself did. A server-issued limit response proves authentication.
  4178	  3718	   205	 * @param {{platform: string, bin: string, args: string[], capOnSuccess?: string}} probe @param {any} io @param {any} table
  4179	  3719	   206	 */
  4180	  3720	   207	async function runProbe(probe, io, table) {
  4181	  3721	   208	  try {
  4182	  3722	   209	    await io.execFile(probe.bin, probe.args, { timeout: PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS });
  4183	  3723	   210	    return { platform: probe.platform, capability: probe.capOnSuccess ?? 'reachable', outcome: 'ok' };
  4184	  3724	   211	  } catch (err) {
  4185	  3725	   212	    const e = /** @type {any} */ (err);
  4186	  3726	   213	    if (e?.code === 'ENOENT') return { platform: probe.platform, capability: null, outcome: 'error' };
  4187	  3727	   214	    if (e?.killed === true) return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'timeout' };
  4188	  3728	   215	    const text = `${e?.stdout ?? ''}\n${e?.stderr ?? ''}`;
  4189	  3729	   216	    if (table && classify({ text, exitCode: 1, platform: probe.platform, table, structured: null }).class === 'usage-limit') {
  4190	  3730	   217	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'authenticated', outcome: 'rate-limited' };
  4191	  3731	   218	    }
  4192	  3732	   219	    if (/authenticated as|logged in as/i.test(text) && /unreachable|ECONN|offline|network/i.test(text)) {
  4193	  3733	   220	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'authenticated', outcome: 'error' };
  4194	  3734	   221	    }
  4195	  3735	   222	    if (/not logged in|log ?in first|unauthorized|authenticat/i.test(text)) {
  4196	  3736	   223	      return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'error' };
  4197	  3737	   224	    }
  4198	  3738	   225	    return { platform: probe.platform, capability: 'installed', outcome: 'error' };
  4199	  3739	   226	  }
  4200	  3740	   227	}

 15901	  8111	  6990	     6	// Contract choices for roles/resolve.mjs. Source of truth: docs/design/core.md
 15902	  8112	  6991	     7	// §Module APIs (resolveRoles signature + assignment shape); plan §Core engine —
 15903	  8113	  6992	     8	// Role matrix + Availability probing (capability/outcome dimensions, avoid[],
 15904	  8114	  6993	     9	// native/delegated/forced-default/unavailable, chainIndex + skipped audit data).
 15905	  8115	  6994	    10	// resolveRoles is PURE and explainable.
 15906	  8116	  6995	    11	//
 15907	  8117	  6996	    12	// INPUT: resolveRoles({config, to, avoid = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null}).
 15908	  8118	  6997	    13	//   `config` is the PARSED config (roles as arrays of {platform, model, effort},
 15909	  8119	  6998	    14	//   as loadConfig returns) — built inline here so this file's red phase is
 15910	  8120	  6999	    15	//   attributable to resolve.mjs alone (not matrix.mjs).
 15911	  8121	  7000	    16	//
 15912	  8122	  7001	    17	// RETURN: { assignments: {[role]: Assignment}, notes: [] }.
 15913	  8123	  7002	    18	//   Assignment = {platform, model, effort, mode, chainIndex, skipped[], degraded?}.
 15914	  8124	  7003	    19	//   modes: 'native' | 'delegated' | 'forced-default' | 'unavailable'.
 15915	  8125	  7004	    20	//
 15916	  8126	  7005	    21	// PINS:
 15917	  8127	  7006	    22	//   1. CHAIN WALK. For each role, walk entries in order; the FIRST eligible
 15918	  8128	  7007	    23	//      (surviving) entry is selected. skipped[] records each passed-over entry
 15919	  8129	  7008	    24	//      as {chainIndex, platform, model, why} (extra fields tolerated).
 15920	  8130	  7009	    25	//      why values: 'avoided' | 'unknown-platform' | 'disabled' | 'rate-limited' | 'unauthenticated'.
 15921	  8131	  7010	    26	//   2. ELIGIBILITY / skip reasons:
 15922	  8132	  7011	    27	//        - platform ∈ avoid                          -> skip, why 'avoided'
 15923	  8133	  7012	    28	//        - platform NOT a key of config.platforms    -> skip, why 'unknown-platform'
 15924	  8134	  7013	    29	//        - config.platforms[p].enabled === false     -> skip, why 'disabled'
 15925	  8135	  7014	    30	//        - probes given & probes[p].outcome==='rate-limited' -> skip, why 'rate-limited'
 15926	  8136	  7015	    31	//        - probes given & capability==='installed' AND outcome!=='ok' (a VERIFIED
 15927	  8137	  7016	    32	//          auth/reachability FAILURE)                 -> skip, why 'unauthenticated'
 15928	  8138	  7017	    33	//          (iter-3 F1: a capped SUCCESS {installed, ok} leaves auth UNVERIFIED —
 15929	  8139	  7018	    34	//          it stays selectable and is flagged degraded, it is NOT skipped)
 15930	  8140	  7019	    35	//      A platform with capability ∈ {authenticated, reachable} AND outcome
 15931	  8141	  7020	    36	//      ≠ 'rate-limited' is eligible.
 15932	  8142	  7021	    37	//   3. DEGRADED. If probes is a non-null object but has NO entry for the chosen
 15933	  8143	  7022	    38	//      platform (unverifiable), the entry is selectable with degraded === true.
 15934	  8144	  7023	    39	//      probes === null means OFFLINE resolution: still selectable, but every
 15935	  8145	  7024	    40	//      selection is flagged degraded (gate-2 iter-2 M3; plan: offline always degraded).
 15936	  8146	  7025	    41	//      Non-degraded assignments have a falsy `degraded` (absent or false).
 15937	  8147	  7026	    42	//   4. MODE. First surviving entry: mode 'native' iff entry.platform === to,
 15938	  8148	  7027	    43	//      else 'delegated'. chainIndex = that entry's index in the ORIGINAL chain.
 15939	  8149	  7028	    44	//   5. nativeOnly restricts consideration to entries with platform === to; if
 15940	  8150	  7029	    45	//      none survive it MAY fall back to config.defaults[to] with mode
 15941	  8151	  7030	    46	//      'forced-default' (platform=to, model=defaults[to], effort=null,
 15942	  8152	  7031	    47	//      chainIndex=null) — but ONLY when the destination `to` is itself
 15943	  8153	  7032	    48	//      probe-eligible (PIN 2). When `to` is probe-INELIGIBLE (e.g. rate-limited),
 15944	  8154	  7033	    49	//      the forced-default is SUPPRESSED and the role resolves 'unavailable', the
 15945	  8155	  7034	    50	//      ineligibility audited in skipped[] (why 'rate-limited'). (fold C1-1)
 15946	  8156	  7035	    51	//   6. UNAVAILABLE. In normal (non-nativeOnly) mode, when NOTHING survives:
 15947	  8157	  7036	    52	//      mode 'unavailable', platform null, model null, effort null,
 15948	  8158	  7037	    53	//      chainIndex null, and skipped[] carries the full passed-over list.
 15949	  8159	  7038	    54	//   7. DETERMINISM. Same input -> deep-equal output; input config is not mutated.
 15950	  8160	  7039	    55	//      assignments object keys are in the CONFIG'S ROLE ORDER.
 15951	  8161	  7040	    56	//   8. avoid[] auto-population is the CALLER'S job; resolve only honors the list.
 15952	  8162	  7041	    57	// ===========================================================================

 17975	    89	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
 17976	    90	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token

 17986	   100	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
 17987	   101	  const flags = {};

 17989	   103	    const a = args[i];

 17991	   105	    const key = a.slice(2);
 17992	   106	    const kind = full[key];
 17993	   107	    if (kind === undefined) return { flags, error: `unknown flag --${key}` };
 17994	   108	    if (kind === 'boolean') {
 17995	   109	      // A following token that is not a flag would have been this flag's
 17996	   110	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.

 18636	    73	/**
 18637	    74	 * The revision fingerprint the receipt token derives from. Every field is a
 18638	    75	 * bound input: any drift between prepare and commit re-derives a different
 18639	    76	 * token, so a stale receipt can never commit (plan §Concurrency).
 18640	    77	 * @param {string} root @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
 18641	    78	 * @returns {Record<string, any>}

 18643	    80	function tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io) {
 18644	    81	  let configDigest = 'absent';
 18645	    82	  try {
 18646	    83	    configDigest = dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(`${root}/baton.config.json`, 'utf8'));
 18647	    84	  } catch {
 18648	    85	    // no config — 'absent' is itself a bound value
 18649	    86	  }
 18650	    87	  return {
 18651	    88	    generation: bundle.generation,
 18652	    89	    journalSeq: bundle.journalSeq,

 18654	    91	    // that lands between this token's derivation and its commit changes

 18672	   109	/**
 18673	   110	 * Structured receipt token: a fixed-order join of per-input digests. Equality
 18674	   111	 * still gates commit exactly as the old opaque hash did; the structure only
 18675	   112	 * buys DIAGNOSIS — a mismatch can name the drifted input(s).

 18679	   116	  const inputs = tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io);
 18680	   117	  return `${TOKEN_PREFIX}.` + TOKEN_FIELDS.map(([key]) => dedupeKey(inputs[key] ?? null).slice(0, 10)).join('.');
 18681	   118	}

 18683	   120	/**
 18684	   121	 * Name the inputs whose digests differ between two structured tokens.

 18781	   218	/**
 18782	   219	 * Phase 2: one atomic transition. Re-derives every bound input from current
 18783	   220	 * disk state + opts and rejects ANY drift (throws, zero mutation). On match:
 18784	   221	 * writes the received seal, archives it via a 'receive' rotation, then opens a
 18785	   222	 * fresh writable generation owned by the receiving platform/session.

 18787	   224	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
 18788	   225	 */
 18789	   226	export function commit(root, token, opts, io) {
 18790	   227	  // ONE operation-scoped lock across revalidation and every mutation (gate-2
 18791	   228	  // fix: reviewers a#1/b#11): two competing receivers serialize here, and the
 18792	   229	  // loser's re-derivation sees the winner's generation/status/receive_log.
 18793	   230	  return withLock(root, io, (fence) => commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence));
 18794	   231	}

 18796	   233	/**
 18797	   234	 * @param {string} root @param {string} token @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io @param {string} fence
 18798	   235	 * @returns {{adopted: boolean, generation: number, archivedTo: string | null, alreadyCommitted?: boolean}}
 18799	   236	 */
 18800	   237	function commitLocked(root, token, opts, io, fence) {
 18801	   238	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
 18802	   239	  if (bundle === null) throw new Error(`no handoff bundle under ${root}/.handoff — nothing to receive; run receive --prepare first`);
 18803	   240	  opts = effectiveIntake(bundle, opts);
 18804	   241	
 18805	   242	  const expected = deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io);
 18806	   243	  if (expected !== token) {
 18807	   244	    // Idempotency first (audit finding: duplicate-receive corruption): if THIS
 18808	   245	    // exact receipt already landed — its digest is recorded on a receive_log
 18809	   246	    // entry — the retry is a lost-output re-send, not drift. Report success
 18810	   247	    // with zero mutation instead of sending the model into a re-prepare +
 18811	   248	    // re-commit loop that executes a second full receive.
 18812	   249	    const receipt = dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16);
 18813	   250	    const landed = Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) && bundle.handoff.receive_log.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e?.receipt === receipt);
 18814	   251	    if (landed) {
 18815	   252	      return { adopted: false, alreadyCommitted: true, generation: bundle.generation, archivedTo: null };
 18816	   253	    }
 18817	   254	    const drifted = driftedInputs(token, expected);
 18818	   255	    const detail = drifted.length > 0 ? `drifted input(s): ${drifted.join(', ')}` : 'a bound input drifted since prepare';
 18819	   256	    throw new Error(
 18820	   257	      `receipt token is stale — ${detail}. Re-prepare and retry, passing the SAME intake flags (--origin/--reason/--reason-class) to both prepare and --commit`,
 18821	   258	    );
 18822	   259	  }
 18823	   260	
 18824	   261	  const degraded = bundle.handoff.status !== 'sealed';
 18825	   262	  const receiveEntry = {
 18826	   263	    origin: opts.origin,
 18827	   264	    reason: opts.reason,
 18828	   265	    at: io.now(),
 18829	   266	    // The receipt digest keys the idempotent-retry detection above.
 18830	   267	    receipt: dedupeKey(token).slice(0, 16),
 18831	   268	    ...(degraded ? { degradedSeal: true } : {}),
 18832	   269	  };
 18833	   270	
 18834	   271	  // The degraded seal must NOT persist a LOW-confidence classification (iter-3
 18835	   272	  // F10): a sealed reasonClass is trusted as high-confidence by the next
 18836	   273	  // prepare, so laundering a low-confidence heuristic here would silently
 18837	   274	  // auto-avoid the origin one hop later. Explicit intake is high-confidence and
 18838	   275	  // seals; a live classification seals ONLY at medium+ confidence, else null
 18839	   276	  // (the next receive re-classifies the reason text at its true confidence).
 18840	   277	  let sealedReasonClass = null;
 18841	   278	  if (degraded) {
 18842	   279	    if (typeof opts.reasonClass === 'string') {
 18843	   280	      sealedReasonClass = opts.reasonClass;
 18844	   281	    } else {
 18845	   282	      const v = classifyReason(opts.reason, opts.origin, io);
 18846	   283	      sealedReasonClass = v.confidence === 'low' ? null : v.class;
 18847	   284	    }
 18848	   285	  }
 18849	   286	
 18850	   287	  const receivedSeal = {
 18851	   288	    ...bundle,
 18852	   289	    updatedAt: io.now(),
 18853	   290	    handoff: {
 18854	   291	      ...bundle.handoff,
 18855	   292	      status: 'received',
 18856	   293	      ...(degraded
 18857	   294	        ? {
 18858	   295	            reason: opts.reason,
 18859	   296	            reasonClass: sealedReasonClass,
 18860	   297	            finalizedAt: io.now(),
 18861	   298	          }
 18862	   299	        : {}),
 18863	   300	      receive_log: [...bundle.handoff.receive_log, receiveEntry],
 18864	   301	    },
 18865	   302	  };
 18866	   303	
 18867	   304	  // Freeze order: the received seal is written first so the 'receive' rotation
 18868	   305	  // archives exactly that state (never the pre-commit bundle). All three
 18869	   306	  // mutations run under the SAME lock acquisition, fence-checked per write.
 18870	   307	  writeSnapshotIn(root, receivedSeal, io, fence);
 18871	   308	  const archivedTo = rotateJournalIn(root, 'receive', io, fence);
 18872	   309	
 18873	   310	  const { config } = loadConfig(root, io);
 18874	   311	  const next = {
 18875	   312	    ...receivedSeal,
 18876	   313	    generation: bundle.generation + 1,
 18877	   314	    origin: {
 18878	   315	      platform: opts.platform,
 18879	   316	      model: config?.defaults?.[opts.platform] ?? 'unknown',
 18880	   317	      sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
 18881	   318	      unstable: opts.sessionUnstable === true,
 18882	   319	    },
 18883	   320	    // The fresh writable generation has NO switch reason yet (iter-4 I3): the
 18884	   321	    // sealed reason/reasonClass/finalizedAt/toPlatformHint describe the PRIOR
 18885	   322	    // handoff, not this one. Carrying them forward made the next prepare trust a
 18886	   323	    // stale class as a high-confidence seal (silently auto-avoiding the healthy
 18887	   324	    // adopted origin) and poisoned both the 12 h staleness reference and the
 18888	   325	    // sessionStart limit-hit signal. Keep only receive_log (the audit chain).
 18889	   326	    handoff: { ...receivedSeal.handoff, status: 'open', reason: null, reasonClass: null, finalizedAt: null, toPlatformHint: null },
 18890	   327	  };
 18891	   328	  writeSnapshotIn(root, next, io, fence);
 18892	   329	
 18893	   330	  return { adopted: true, generation: next.generation, archivedTo };
 18894	   331	}

 19348	   110	/** @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p */
 19349	   111	function acquire(io, p) {
 19350	   112	  io.fs.mkdirSync(p.dir, { recursive: true });
 19351	   113	  try {
 19352	   114	    io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
 19353	   115	    return publishOwner(io, p);
 19354	   116	  } catch (err) {
 19355	   117	    if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code !== 'EEXIST') throw err;
 19356	   118	  }
 19357	   119	
 19358	   120	  const s = inspect(io, p);
 19359	   121	  switch (s.state) {
 19360	   122	    case 'free':
 19361	   123	      // Raced a release between mkdir failure and inspection; retry once. A
 19362	   124	      // competitor can win THIS mkdir too (gate-2 fix 12: observed under real
 19363	   125	      // barrier-released contention) — that is contention, not corruption.
 19364	   126	      try {
 19365	   127	        io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
 19366	   128	      } catch (err) {
 19367	   129	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') {
 19368	   130	          throw new LockHeldError('lock was re-acquired by a competitor mid-inspection — transient contention');
 19369	   131	        }
 19370	   132	        throw err;
 19371	   133	      }
 19372	   134	      return publishOwner(io, p);
 19373	   135	    case 'live':
 19374	   136	      throw new LockHeldError(
 19375	   137	        `lock is held by a live process (pid ${s.owner.pid} on ${s.owner.host}) — terminate that process first.`,
 19376	   138	      );
 19377	   139	    case 'cross-host':
 19378	   140	      throw new Error(
 19379	   141	        `lock is held from another host ('${s.owner.host}', this is '${io.host}') — cross-host locks are never provably safe to steal. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
 19380	   142	      );
 19381	   143	    case 'torn':
 19382	   144	      // During ACQUIRE, torn metadata is usually a competitor caught between
 19383	   145	      // its mkdir and owner.json publication — transient by construction, so
 19384	   146	      // LockHeldError lets withLock wait it out (gate-2 fix 12). A genuinely
 19385	   147	      // crashed publisher exhausts the retry budget and surfaces this same
 19386	   148	      // message; recovery semantics (recoverLock) are unchanged: never steal.
 19387	   149	      throw new LockHeldError(`${s.cause} — unsupported for automatic recovery. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`);
 19388	   150	    case 'dead': {
 19389	   151	      // Atomic dead-lock reclaim (gate-2 iter-2 B1, hardened iter-3 finding-1).
 19390	   152	      // rm-then-mkdir is NOT mutually exclusive: two contenders can both observe
 19391	   153	      // 'dead' before either removes the stale dir, then both rm+mkdir — the
 19392	   154	      // second silently clobbers the first, yielding two simultaneous holders and
 19393	   155	      // two takeover notes. rename() is the atomic arbiter instead: the stale
 19394	   156	      // lock dir has exactly one name, so only one process can move it aside (the
 19395	   157	      // rest get ENOENT). Winning the rename IS winning the reclaim; a contender
 19396	   158	      // that recreated the dir via the 'free' path first makes our mkdir EEXIST →
 19397	   159	      // transient contention. The fencing token stays the write-time backstop.
 19398	   160	      const aside = `${p.lockDir}.reclaim-${io.pid}-${io.newFencingToken()}`;
 19399	   161	      try {
 19400	   162	        io.fs.renameSync(p.lockDir, aside);
 19401	   163	      } catch (err) {
 19402	   164	        // Source already gone → another contender is reclaiming it; wait+retry.
 19403	   165	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'ENOENT') {
 19404	   166	          throw new LockHeldError('a competitor is reclaiming the dead lock — transient contention');
 19405	   167	        }
 19406	   168	        throw err;
 19407	   169	      }
 19408	   170	      io.fs.rmSync(aside, { recursive: true, force: true });
 19409	   171	      try {
 19410	   172	        io.fs.mkdirSync(p.lockDir);
 19411	   173	      } catch (err) {
 19412	   174	        if (/** @type {any} */ (err)?.code === 'EEXIST') {
 19413	   175	          throw new LockHeldError('a competitor re-claimed the dead lock first — transient contention');
 19414	   176	        }
 19415	   177	        throw err;
 19416	   178	      }
 19417	   179	      const token = publishOwner(io, p);
 19418	   180	      // Journal the takeover only now — we HOLD the lock (fresh dir + published
 19419	   181	      // owner), so the note's seq is allocated while holding it (plan
 19420	   182	      // §Concurrency "sequence numbers are allocated under the lock"), never
 19421	   183	      // racing a free-path competitor's concurrent append (iter-3 F2). The note
 19422	   184	      // is best-effort (0-or-1) and MUST NOT abort acquisition (iter-4 I7): if it
 19423	   185	      // threw here — after publishOwner, before the token is returned to withLock
 19424	   186	      // — the release finally would never run and the lock would leak with a live
 19425	   187	      // owner. Swallow it; the reclaim already succeeded.
 19426	   188	      try {
 19427	   189	        journalNote(io, p, `lock takeover: took over stale lock from dead pid ${s.owner.pid} (start time ${s.owner.startTime})`);
 19428	   190	      } catch {
 19429	   191	        // audit note is best-effort
 19430	   192	      }
 19431	   193	      return token;
 19432	   194	    }
 19433	   195	    /* c8 ignore next 2 */
 19434	   196	    default:
 19435	   197	      throw new Error('unreachable lock state');
 19436	   198	  }
 19437	   199	}

 19439	   201	/**
 19440	   202	 * Fence-guarded release: the lock dir is removed only while owner.json still
 19441	   203	 * carries OUR token. A holder that paused past a takeover must not delete the
 19442	   204	 * competitor's lock on its way out — release is a write like any other.
 19443	   205	 * @param {any} io @param {ReturnType<typeof lockPaths>} p @param {string} token
 19444	   206	 */
 19445	   207	function release(io, p, token) {
 19446	   208	  try {
 19447	   209	    const current = JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(p.owner, 'utf8'));
 19448	   210	    if (current.fencingToken !== token) return; // a competitor took over — their lock, not ours
 19449	   211	  } catch {
 19450	   212	    return; // owner metadata gone or torn mid-hold — never guess; leave it for recovery
 19451	   213	  }
 19452	   214	  io.fs.rmSync(p.lockDir, { recursive: true, force: true });
 19453	   215	}
 19454	   216	
 19455	   217	// A live same-host holder is transient by design — operation-scoped locks are
 19456	   218	// held for milliseconds — so contention waits instead of dropping the
 19457	   219	// operation (gate-2 fix 12: simultaneous checkpoints must all land). The budget
 19458	   220	// is generous (≈15 s): under heavy load a writer may be starved of scheduling
 19459	   221	// for seconds, and waiting is strictly safer than silently dropping its work.
 19460	   222	// Every other contended state (torn, cross-host) stays fail-fast: waiting
 19461	   223	// cannot make those provably safe.
 19462	   224	const DEFAULT_RETRY = { attempts: 600, delayMs: 25 };
 19463	   225	
 19464	   226	/** Synchronous sleep without burning a core: Atomics.wait on a throwaway buffer. */
 19465	   227	const sleepMs = (/** @type {number} */ ms) => {
 19466	   228	  Atomics.wait(new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4)), 0, 0, ms);
 19467	   229	};

 19469	   231	/**
 19470	   232	 * Acquire → run fn(token) → release (also on throw). Synchronous by design:
 19471	   233	 * everything the lock guards is sync fs work. Live-held locks are retried on
 19472	   234	 * a bounded budget (override via io.lockRetry = {attempts, delayMs}).
 19473	   235	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {(token: string) => any} fn
 19474	   236	 */
 19475	   237	export function withLock(root, io, fn) {
 19476	   238	  const p = lockPaths(root);
 19477	   239	  // Jail BEFORE any lock mutation (gate-2 iter-2 B2): a symlinked .handoff or
 19478	   240	  // .handoff/lock must never be created into or removed through — that would
 19479	   241	  // reach outside the repository. Checked once here, ahead of acquire.
 19480	   242	  const safe = checkHandoffTree(root, io);
 19481	   243	  if (!safe.ok) throw new Error(`${safe.problem} — refusing to acquire the lock`);
 19482	   244	  const retry = io.lockRetry ?? DEFAULT_RETRY;
 19483	   245	  /** @type {string} */
 19484	   246	  let token;
 19485	   247	  for (let attempt = 0; ; attempt++) {
 19486	   248	    try {
 19487	   249	      token = acquire(io, p);
 19488	   250	      break;
 19489	   251	    } catch (err) {
 19490	   252	      if (err instanceof LockHeldError && attempt < retry.attempts) {
 19491	   253	        sleepMs(retry.delayMs);
 19492	   254	        continue;
 19493	   255	      }
 19494	   256	      throw err;
 19495	   257	    }
 19496	   258	  }
 19497	   259	  try {
 19498	   260	    return fn(token);
 19499	   261	  } finally {
 19500	   262	    release(io, p, token);
 19501	   263	  }
 19502	   264	}

 19504	   266	/**
 19505	   267	 * Fast-abort layer: re-read the published token immediately before a write; a
 19506	   268	 * holder that paused past its last check aborts instead of clobbering.
 19507	   269	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {string} token @param {() => any} fn
 19508	   270	 */
 19509	   271	export function guardedWrite(root, io, token, fn) {
 19510	   272	  const p = lockPaths(root);
 19511	   273	  let current = null;

 19513	   275	    current = JSON.parse(io.fs.readFileSync(p.owner, 'utf8'));
 19514	   276	  } catch {
 19515	   277	    throw new FencingError('lock owner metadata is gone — fencing check failed; aborting write');
 19516	   278	  }
 19517	   279	  if (current.fencingToken !== token) {
 19518	   280	    throw new FencingError(
 19519	   281	      `fencing token changed (held '${token}', current '${current.fencingToken}') — another process took over; aborting write`,
 19520	   282	    );
 19521	   283	  }
 19522	   284	  return fn();
 19523	   285	}

 19525	   287	/**
 19526	   288	 * Explicit recovery. `force` is an intent flag only — it never changes the
 19527	   289	 * decision: exactly one state recovers (provably-dead same-host owner).
 19528	   290	 * @param {string} root @param {any} io @param {{force?: boolean}} [opts]
 19529	   291	 * @returns {{recovered: boolean, refusedReason: string | null}}
 19530	   292	 */
 19531	   293	export function recoverLock(root, io, opts = {}) {
 19532	   294	  void opts;
 19533	   295	  const p = lockPaths(root);
 19534	   296	  // Jail before recovery (gate-2 iter-2 B2): recoverLock removes the lock dir,
 19535	   297	  // so a symlinked managed tree must be refused first — even with force, a
 19536	   298	  // symlink is never provably safe to delete through.
 19537	   299	  const safe = checkHandoffTree(root, io);
 19538	   300	  if (!safe.ok) return { recovered: false, refusedReason: `${safe.problem} — refusing recovery` };
 19539	   301	  const s = inspect(io, p);
 19540	   302	  switch (s.state) {
 19541	   303	    case 'free':
 19542	   304	      return { recovered: true, refusedReason: null };
 19543	   305	    case 'dead': {
 19544	   306	      // Reclaim atomically via a single acquire() attempt + release, NOT an
 19545	   307	      // inspect-then-rmSync (iter-4 I1): the old bare rmSync had a TOCTOU — a
 19546	   308	      // competitor could win the rename-arbitrated dead-reclaim between this
 19547	   309	      // inspect() and the rmSync, publish a LIVE owner, and recovery would then
 19548	   310	      // delete a lock whose owner is alive. acquire() re-inspects atomically and
 19549	   311	      // shares the SAME rename arbitration, so recovery and a concurrent takeover
 19550	   312	      // are mutually exclusive: acquire either reclaims a still-dead lock (and
 19551	   313	      // journals the takeover under the lock) or throws because it is now
 19552	   314	      // live/torn — in which case we refuse rather than steal. release() then
 19553	   315	      // leaves the slot clear.
 19554	   316	      let token;
 19555	   317	      try {
 19556	   318	        token = acquire(io, p);
 19557	   319	      } catch (err) {
 19558	   320	        return { recovered: false, refusedReason: /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err) };
 19559	   321	      }
 19560	   322	      release(io, p, token);
 19561	   323	      return { recovered: true, refusedReason: null };
 19562	   324	    }
 19563	   325	    case 'live':
 19564	   326	      return {
 19565	   327	        recovered: false,
 19566	   328	        refusedReason: `lock is held by a live process (pid ${s.owner.pid} on ${s.owner.host}) — terminate that process first.`,
 19567	   329	      };
 19568	   330	    case 'cross-host':
 19569	   331	      return {
 19570	   332	        recovered: false,
 19571	   333	        refusedReason: `lock is held from another host ('${s.owner.host}', this is '${io.host}') — cross-host locks are never provably safe to steal, even with force. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
 19572	   334	      };
 19573	   335	    case 'torn':
 19574	   336	      return {
 19575	   337	        recovered: false,
 19576	   338	        refusedReason: `${s.cause} — unsupported for automatic recovery, even with force. ${ESCAPE_HATCH}`,
 19577	   339	      };
 19578	   340	    /* c8 ignore next 2 */
 19579	   341	    default:
 19580	   342	      return { recovered: false, refusedReason: 'unreachable lock state' };
 19581	   343	  }
 19582	   344	}

 19784	     5	// discovery & degraded modes).
 19785	     6	const GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
 19786	     7	// The untracked digest is bounded: beyond this many paths, entries fold in by
 19787	     8	// name only, keeping prepare-time hashing cheap on huge untracked trees.
 19788	     9	const UNTRACKED_CAP = 200;
 19789	    10	// NUL separator: cannot occur in diffs, sizes, hex hashes, or file paths, so
 19790	    11	// joined digest inputs cannot collide across field boundaries.
 19791	    12	const SEP = String.fromCharCode(0);
 19792	    13	const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
 19793	    14	
 19794	    15	const sha256 = (/** @type {string} */ s) => createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex');
 19795	    16	
 19796	    17	/**
 19797	    18	 * Capture the repo's git state plus a content-sensitive digest. The digest
 19798	    19	 * covers the staged diff, unstaged diff, and a bounded untracked-files digest
 19799	    20	 * (path + size + content hash) — NOT the HEAD sha, which the receive token
 19800	    21	 * binds as its own input, so a HEAD-only move is distinguishable from a
 19801	    22	 * content change.
 19802	    23	 * @param {{execFile: Function, cwd: string, fs: any}} deps
 19803	    24	 * @returns {Promise<{branch: string, headSha: string, dirty: boolean, dirtySummary: string[], contentDigest: string} | null>}
 19804	    25	 */
 19805	    26	export async function snapshot({ execFile, cwd, fs }) {
 19806	    27	  const git = (/** @type {string[]} */ args) => execFile('git', args, { cwd, timeout: GIT_TIMEOUT_MS });
 19807	    28	  let branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList;
 19808	    29	  try {
 19809	    30	    [branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList] = await Promise.all([
 19810	    31	      git(['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD']),
 19811	    32	      git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']),
 19812	    33	      git(['status', '--porcelain']),
 19813	    34	      git(['diff', '--cached']),
 19814	    35	      git(['diff']),
 19815	    36	      git(['ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard']),
 19816	    37	    ]);
 19817	    38	  } catch {
 19818	    39	    return null;
 19819	    40	  }
 19820	    41	
 19821	    42	  const nonEmptyLines = (/** @type {string} */ s) => s.split(NEWLINE).filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l !== '');
 19822	    43	  const dirtySummary = nonEmptyLines(status.stdout);
 19823	    44	  const untrackedPaths = nonEmptyLines(untrackedList.stdout);
 19824	    45	
 19825	    46	  const untrackedEntries = untrackedPaths.map((rel, i) => {
 19826	    47	    if (i >= UNTRACKED_CAP) return [rel, 'capped'].join(SEP);
 19827	    48	    try {
 19828	    49	      const content = fs.readFileSync(cwd + '/' + rel, 'utf8');
 19829	    50	      return [rel, String(Buffer.byteLength(content)), sha256(content)].join(SEP);
 19830	    51	    } catch {
 19831	    52	      // Listed but unreadable (deleted mid-flight): still digest its presence.
 19832	    53	      return [rel, 'absent'].join(SEP);
 19833	    54	    }
 19834	    55	  });
 19835	    56	
 19836	    57	  return {
 19837	    58	    branch: branch.stdout.trim(),
 19838	    59	    headSha: head.stdout.trim(),
 19839	    60	    dirty: dirtySummary.length > 0,
 19840	    61	    dirtySummary,

 19842	    63	  };
 19843	    64	}

 20638	    15	 * `baton session-start` — the cheap SessionStart gate the adapters call
 20639	    16	 * instead of full receive preparation (gate-2 fix 8). Inspects only
 20640	    17	 * pending-foreign state: a bundle that is sealed OR limit-hit AND from
 20641	    18	 * another platform yields a harness-shaped notice on stdout; every other state
 20642	    19	 * — own bundle, open non-limit bundle, no bundle, corrupt tree — is a quiet
 20643	    20	 * no-op. Soft paths ALWAYS exit 0 (a session-start notice must never break a
 20644	    21	 * session); a mis-parsed invocation is a broken hook manifest, which is loud
 20645	    22	 * (exit 2) so init/doctor drift gets noticed. With --json (surface-audit fold)
 20646	    23	 * the standard envelope wraps the outcome so machine consumers can tell "no
 20647	    24	 * pending handoff" from a swallowed failure: data = {pending, shaped}.

 20658	    35	    return 0;
 20659	    36	  };

 20661	    38	    const platform = typeof flags.platform === 'string' ? flags.platform : null;
 20662	    39	    if (!platform || platformError(platform) !== null) {
 20663	    40	      io.stderr.write('baton session-start: --platform <claude-code|codex|cursor> is required — emitting nothing\n');

 20665	    42	    }

 20669	    46	    // only as a post-snapshot journal note. Load warnings are deliberately
 20670	    47	    // not surfaced — this is a notice path, not a diagnostics path. An UNSAFE
 20671	    48	    // managed tree (symlinked .handoff — threat model / F12) is a quiet no-op:

 20876	     1	const PRECEDENCE = ['usage-limit', 'auth', 'throttle', 'other-error'];

 20878	     3	/** @type {Record<string, string>} */
 20879	     4	const STOP_FAILURE_MAP = {

 20881	     6	  overloaded: 'throttle',
 20882	     7	  authentication_failed: 'auth',
 20883	     8	  oauth_org_not_allowed: 'auth',

 20889	    14	
 20890	    15	/** @param {any} matcher @param {string} text */
 20891	    16	function matches(matcher, text) {
 20892	    17	  switch (matcher.kind) {
 20893	    18	    case 'substring':
 20894	    19	      return text.includes(matcher.value);
 20895	    20	    case 'regex':
 20896	    21	      return new RegExp(matcher.pattern, matcher.flags || '').test(text);
 20897	    22	    case 'json-field': {

 20899	    24	        let obj;
 20900	    25	        try {
 20901	    26	          obj = JSON.parse(line);
 20902	    27	        } catch {
 20903	    28	          continue;
 20904	    29	        }
 20905	    30	        const val = String(matcher.path)
 20906	    31	          .split('.')

 20908	    33	        if (val === matcher.equals) return true;

 20917	    42	/**
 20918	    43	 * Classify harness output. Structured evidence first (text and exit code are
 20919	    44	 * ignored when a recognized structured signal is present); text signatures as
 20920	    45	 * the fallback tier; exit code only breaks the no-match tie — a generic nonzero
 20921	    46	 * exit is never usage-limit on its own.
 20922	    47	 * @param {{text?: string, exitCode?: number, platform: string, table: any, structured?: {kind: string, errorType: string} | null}} input
 20923	    48	 * @returns {{class: string, signatureId: string | null, confidence: string | null, resetHint: string | null, tried?: string[]}}
 20924	    49	 */
 20925	    50	export function classify({ text = '', exitCode = 0, platform, table, structured = null }) {
 20926	    51	  if (structured) {
 20927	    52	    if (structured.kind === 'stop-failure') {
 20928	    53	      const cls = STOP_FAILURE_MAP[structured.errorType] ?? 'other-error';
 20929	    54	      return { class: cls, signatureId: `structured:${structured.errorType}`, confidence: 'high', resetHint: null };
 20930	    55	    }
 20931	    56	    if (structured.kind === 'exec-json') {
 20932	    57	      const cls = structured.errorType === 'usage_limit' ? 'usage-limit' : 'other-error';
 20933	    58	      return { class: cls, signatureId: `structured:${structured.errorType}`, confidence: 'high', resetHint: null };
 20934	    59	    }
 20935	    60	    // Unrecognized structured kind: fall through to the text tier.
 20936	    61	  }
 20937	    62	
 20938	    63	  const stripped = text.replace(ANSI, '');
 20939	    64	  const candidates = table.signatures.filter((/** @type {any} */ s) => s.platform === platform);
 20940	    65	  /** @type {any} */
 20941	    66	  let best = null;
 20942	    67	  for (const s of candidates) {
 20943	    68	    if (!matches(s.matcher, stripped)) continue;
 20944	    69	    if (best === null || PRECEDENCE.indexOf(s.class) < PRECEDENCE.indexOf(best.class)) best = s;
 20945	    70	  }
 20946	    71	
 20947	    72	  if (best) {
 20948	    73	    let resetHint = null;
 20949	    74	    if (typeof best.resetHint === 'string') {
 20950	    75	      const m = stripped.match(new RegExp(best.resetHint));
 20951	    76	      if (m) resetHint = m[1] ?? m[0];
 20952	    77	    }
 20953	    78	    return { class: best.class, signatureId: best.id, confidence: best.confidence, resetHint };
 20954	    79	  }
 20955	    80	
 20956	    81	  return {
 20957	    82	    class: exitCode !== 0 ? 'other-error' : 'ok',
 20958	    83	    signatureId: null,
 20959	    84	    confidence: null,
 20960	    85	    resetHint: null,
 20961	    86	  };
 20962	    87	}

docs/design/core.md:137:Commands: `checkpoint`, `finalize`, `detect`, `remap`, `receive`, `init`, `doctor`, `status`, `purge-transcript`, `recover`, `session-start`. Exit codes: `0` ok · `1` command failure · `2` usage error · `10` usage-limit · `11` throttle · `12` auth · `13` other-error. `--json`: exactly one `{ok, data, warnings, error}` envelope on stdout, diagnostics on stderr. Checkpoint soft-fails to exit 0 in hook contexts (`--strict` opts out). `session-start` is the cheap adapter SessionStart gate: soft paths always exit 0 and its BARE stdout is harness-shaped context (not an envelope); with `--json` it honors the envelope contract (`data: {pending, shaped}`). `wrap` is reserved, not implemented in v1.

     4	 * The --json contract: exactly one compact envelope line on stdout, nothing else.
     5	 * @param {any} io
     6	 * @param {{ok: boolean, data?: any, warnings?: any[], error?: {code: string, msg: string} | null}} env

     8	export function emitEnvelope(io, env) {
     9	  const full = { ok: env.ok, data: env.data ?? null, warnings: env.warnings ?? [], error: env.error ?? null };

    27	/**
    28	 * Repo-root discovery (plan §Root discovery): `--root` wins; else the nearest
    29	 * ancestor of io.cwd carrying `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`; else the
    30	 * nearest ancestor carrying `.git` (the repo toplevel — and a boundary the
    31	 * walk never crosses, so a nested repo resolves to itself); else io.cwd.
    32	 * @param {any} io @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
    33	 * @returns {string}
    34	 */
    35	export function resolveRoot(io, flags) {
    36	  if (typeof flags.root === 'string' && flags.root.length > 0) return flags.root;
    37	  // Normalize separators up front (gate-2 iter-2 M2): a Windows cwd arrives
    38	  // backslash-separated, but Node fs accepts forward slashes, so the ascent
    39	  // and the marker checks work in one forward-slash space. The last separator
    40	  // is either kind; the loop stops at a drive/UNC or filesystem root.
    41	  const start = normSep(io.cwd);
    42	  let dir = start;
    43	  while (true) {
    44	    try {
    45	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.handoff')) || io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, 'baton.config.json'))) return dir;
    46	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.git'))) return dir; // repo toplevel; never walk past a .git boundary
    47	    } catch {
    48	      break;
    49	    }
    50	    const cut = dir.lastIndexOf('/');
    51	    if (cut < 0) break;
    52	    const parent = cut === 0 ? '/' : dir.slice(0, cut);
    53	    // At a drive-relative ceiling ("C:") examine the drive ROOT ("C:/") once —
    54	    // a repo can live directly at C:/ (iter-3 F6) — then stop.
    55	    if (/^[A-Za-z]:$/.test(parent)) {
    56	      const driveRoot = `${parent}/`;
    57	      if (driveRoot !== dir) {
    58	        dir = driveRoot;
    59	        continue;
    60	      }
    61	      break;
    62	    }
    63	    if (parent === dir) break;
    64	    dir = parent;
    65	  }
    66	  return start;
    67	}

    85	/**
    86	 * Strict flag parser (surface-audit fold; docs/design/core.md §tooling always
    87	 * specified strict parsing). spec maps each flag name to 'string' | 'boolean';
    88	 * `json` and `root` are implied common flags. Errors — unknown flag, stray
    89	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
    90	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token
    91	 * flip SAFETY flags off (checkpoint/doctor --strict, remap --native-only,
    92	 * receive --print-prompt all read fail-dangerous exit 0).
    93	 * @param {string[]} args
    94	 * @param {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} spec
    95	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, error?: string}}
    96	 */
    97	export function parseFlagsStrict(args, spec) {
    98	  /** @type {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} */
    99	  const full = { json: 'boolean', root: 'string', ...spec };
   100	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   101	  const flags = {};
   102	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   103	    const a = args[i];
   104	    if (!a.startsWith('--')) return { flags, error: `unexpected argument '${a}' — flags are --name [value]` };
   105	    const key = a.slice(2);
   106	    const kind = full[key];
   107	    if (kind === undefined) return { flags, error: `unknown flag --${key}` };
   108	    if (kind === 'boolean') {
   109	      // A following token that is not a flag would have been this flag's
   110	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.
   111	      const next = args[i + 1];
   112	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   113	        return { flags, error: `unexpected token '${next}' after --${key} (a bare flag takes no value)` };
   114	      }
   115	      flags[key] = true;
   116	      continue;
   117	    }
   118	    const next = args[i + 1];
   119	    // A string flag consumes the next token unless it is itself a KNOWN flag
   120	    // (so `--commit --origin x` errors instead of eating '--origin').
   121	    if (next === undefined || (next.startsWith('--') && full[next.slice(2)] !== undefined)) {
   122	      return { flags, error: `--${key} requires a value` };
   123	    }
   124	    flags[key] = next;
   125	    i += 1;
   126	  }
   127	  return { flags };
   128	}
   129	
   130	/**
   131	 * Minimal flag parser: `--key value` pairs (value = next token not starting
   132	 * with --), bare `--key` booleans, positionals collected in order.
   133	 * @param {string[]} args
   134	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, positionals: string[]}}
   135	 */
   136	export function parseFlags(args) {
   137	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   138	  const flags = {};
   139	  /** @type {string[]} */
   140	  const positionals = [];
   141	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   142	    const a = args[i];
   143	    if (a.startsWith('--')) {
   144	      const key = a.slice(2);
   145	      const next = args[i + 1];
   146	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   147	        flags[key] = next;
   148	        i += 1;
   149	      } else {
   150	        flags[key] = true;
   151	      }
   152	    } else {
   153	      positionals.push(a);
   154	    }
   155	  }
   156	  return { flags, positionals };
   157	}

    34	function captureTranscriptTail(root, raw, io) {

    36	  if (!cfg.ok || cfg.value?.capture?.transcriptTail !== true) return null;
    37	
    38	  const eventName = raw && typeof raw === 'object' ? (raw.hook_event_name ?? raw.event) : null;
    39	  if (typeof eventName !== 'string' || !/precompact/i.test(eventName)) return null;
    40	  const path = raw.transcript_path;
    41	  if (typeof path !== 'string' || path.length === 0) return null;
    42	
    43	  try {
    44	    if (!io.fs.lstatSync(path).isFile()) return null;
    45	    // Allowlist the transcript path (gate-2 iter-2 m1): the payload is
    46	    // untrusted, so its resolved realpath must sit under the repo root, the
    47	    // user's ~/.claude tree (where Claude Code actually writes transcripts),
    48	    // or a configured capture.transcriptDir — never an arbitrary readable file.
    49	    const fileReal = io.fs.realpathSync(path);
    50	    // On POSIX a backslash is a LEGAL filename character, not a separator, so
    51	    // normalizing '\\'→'/' in the containment check (isContained) could make an
    52	    // out-of-tree sibling like '/repo\\evil/f' appear contained (iter-4 I9).
    53	    // The transcript path is the one fully-untrusted path that reaches
    54	    // containment, so refuse a backslash-bearing realpath off Windows.
    55	    if (io.platform !== 'win32' && String(fileReal).includes('\\')) return null;
    56	    /** @type {string[]} */
    57	    const allowed = [root];
    58	    const home = io.env?.HOME;
    59	    if (typeof home === 'string' && home.length > 0) allowed.push(`${home}/.claude`);
    60	    const dir = cfg.value?.capture?.transcriptDir;
    61	    if (typeof dir === 'string' && dir.length > 0) allowed.push(dir);
    62	    const under = (/** @type {string} */ base) => {
    63	      let baseReal;
    64	      try {
    65	        baseReal = io.fs.realpathSync(base);
    66	      } catch {
    67	        baseReal = base;
    68	      }
    69	      // Compare on normalized forward-slash spellings (iter-3 F9): raw Windows
    70	      // backslash realpaths never satisfy a forward-slash containment, so
    71	      // opt-in capture would silently never fire.
    72	      return isContained(baseReal, fileReal);
    73	    };
    74	    if (!allowed.some(under)) return null;
    75	
    76	    const text = io.fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    77	    const lines = text.split('\n').filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l.trim() !== '');
    78	    let tail = lines.slice(-TAIL_MESSAGES).join('\n');
    79	    if (Buffer.byteLength(tail) > TAIL_BYTES) {
    80	      tail = Buffer.from(tail).subarray(-TAIL_BYTES).toString('utf8');
    81	    }
    82	    return redactSecrets(tail);
    83	  } catch {
    84	    return null; // unreadable transcript is never a checkpoint failure
    85	  }
    86	}
    87	
    88	/** Event-shaped: an object carrying a string `type`. */
    89	const isEventShaped = (/** @type {any} */ v) => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) && typeof v.type === 'string';
    90	
    91	/**
    92	 * Tolerant stdin parse (live /baton:handoff failure: a model sent one event
    93	 * per line and the whole narrative checkpoint silently failed). Accept the
    94	 * canonical single JSON value, a bare array of events, or NDJSON where every
    95	 * line is an event object or a {schema, events} wrapper. All-or-nothing: one
    96	 * non-event element fails the whole parse — never a partial apply.
    97	 * @param {string} text @returns {{ok: true, raw: any} | {ok: false, why?: string}}
    98	 */
    99	function parseStdin(text) {
   100	  let single;
   101	  let singleOk = false;
   102	  try {
   103	    single = JSON.parse(text);
   104	    singleOk = true;
   105	  } catch {
   106	    singleOk = false;
   107	  }
   108	  if (singleOk) {
   109	    if (Array.isArray(single)) {
   110	      return single.every(isEventShaped) ? { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: single } } : { ok: false };
   111	    }
   112	    // A closest-miss of the documented wrapper — an events array whose schema
   113	    // key is missing or wrong — must ERROR, never silently degrade to a junk
   114	    // note with ok:true (the model cannot self-correct from a success
   115	    // envelope while its narrative was discarded).
   116	    if (single !== null && typeof single === 'object' && Array.isArray(single.events) && single.schema !== 'baton/event@1') {
   117	      return { ok: false, why: `stdin carries an events array but schema is ${single.schema === undefined ? 'missing' : JSON.stringify(single.schema)} — use {"schema":"baton/event@1","events":[…]}` };
   118	    }
   119	    // A single bare event object (string `type`, none of the raw-hook payload
   120	    // markers) is one of the two most likely readings of "pipe events on
   121	    // stdin" — accept it as that event instead of degrading it to a junk note.
   122	    if (
   123	      isEventShaped(single) &&
   124	      single.schema === undefined &&
   125	      !('hook_event_name' in single) &&
   126	      !('session_id' in single) &&
   127	      !('event' in single)
   128	    ) {
   129	      return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: [single] } };
   130	    }
   131	    return { ok: true, raw: single };
   132	  }
   133	  const lines = text.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l !== '');
   134	  if (lines.length === 0) return { ok: false };
   135	  /** @type {any[]} */
   136	  const events = [];
   137	  for (const line of lines) {
   138	    let v;
   139	    try {
   140	      v = JSON.parse(line);
   141	    } catch {
   142	      return { ok: false };
   143	    }
   144	    if (v && typeof v === 'object' && v.schema === 'baton/event@1' && Array.isArray(v.events)) {
   145	      if (!v.events.every(isEventShaped)) return { ok: false };
   146	      events.push(...v.events);
   147	    } else if (isEventShaped(v)) {
   148	      events.push(v);
   149	    } else {
   150	      return { ok: false };
   151	    }
   152	  }
   153	  return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events } };
   154	}

   156	/**
   157	 * `baton checkpoint` — mechanical checkpoint from a hook payload on stdin.
   158	 * Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on every soft failure so a checkpoint can never
   159	 * break the host harness; `--strict` opts into hard failures (CI).
   160	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
   161	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
   162	 */
   163	export async function cmdCheckpoint(args, io) {
   164	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { platform: 'string', model: 'string', trigger: 'string', debounce: 'string', strict: 'boolean', 'take-over': 'boolean' });
   165	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'checkpoint', parsed.error);
   166	  const flags = parsed.flags;
   167	  const strict = flags.strict === true;
   168	  const platform = typeof flags.platform === 'string' ? flags.platform : null;
   169	  if (!platform) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', '--platform <claude-code|codex|cursor> is required');
   170	  const pErr = platformError(platform);
   171	  if (pErr) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', pErr);
   172	
   173	  try {
   174	    return await run(flags, platform, io);
   175	  } catch (err) {
   176	    const msg = /** @type {any} */ (err)?.message ?? String(err);
   177	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'checkpoint-failed', msg } });
   178	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: ${msg}\n`);
   179	    return strict ? 1 : 0;
   180	  }
   181	}
   182	
   183	/**
   184	 * @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
   185	 * @param {string} platform
   186	 * @param {any} io
   187	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
   188	 */
   189	async function run(flags, platform, io) {
   190	  const strict = flags.strict === true;
   191	  const root = resolveRoot(io, flags);
   192	  const paths = bundlePaths(root);
   193	  // The --json contract (gate-2 fix 11): exactly one envelope on stdout for
   194	  // every exit path — the exit code stays governed by hook-safety.
   195	  const finish = (/** @type {any} */ env, /** @type {number} */ code) => {
   196	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, env);
   197	    return code;
   198	  };
   199	
   200	  const parsed = parseStdin(typeof io.stdin === 'string' ? io.stdin : '');
   201	  if (!parsed.ok) {
   202	    const why = parsed.why ?? 'send one JSON value ({"schema":"baton/event@1","events":[…]}), a JSON array of events, or NDJSON event lines';
   203	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: stdin could not be parsed — ${why}\n`);
   204	    return finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'bad-stdin', msg: why } }, strict ? 1 : 0);
   205	  }
   206	  const raw = parsed.raw;
   207	
   208	  const session = { host: io.host, pid: io.pid, startTime: io.startTime };
   209	  // The hook command declares which event it is (--trigger), so event identity
   210	  // never depends on parsing each harness's payload shape (Cursor's stop payload
   211	  // names the event nowhere normalize could find it).
   212	  const explicitEvent = typeof flags.trigger === 'string' ? flags.trigger : undefined;
   213	  const events = normalizeHookPayload(raw, platform, session, explicitEvent);
   214	  if (events.length === 0) return finish({ ok: true, data: { events: 0, rewritten: false } }, 0);
   215	
   216	  // Opt-in transcript tail (gate-2 fix 10): rides the journal as its own
   217	  // IMPORTANT event so the snapshot rewrite below persists it, and purge can
   218	  // strip it from every retained copy by its property name.
   219	  const tail = captureTranscriptTail(root, raw, io);
   220	  if (tail !== null) {
   221	    events.push({
   222	      type: 'transcript.set',
   223	      payload: { transcript: { capturedAt: io.now(), tail } },
   224	      source: platform,
   225	      sessionHint: events[0]?.sessionHint,
   226	      unstable: events[0]?.unstable ?? true,
   227	    });
   228	  }
   229	
   230	  const { bundle, warnings, unsafe } = loadBundle(root, io);
   231	  for (const w of warnings) io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: ${w}\n`);
   232	
   233	  // An unsafe managed tree (symlinked .handoff — gate-2 fix 6) is NOT "no
   234	  // bundle yet": seeding here would write through the link. Refuse everything;
   235	  // hook-safety keeps the refusal soft outside --strict.
   236	  if (unsafe === true) {
   237	    io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: managed tree failed the symlink/realpath jail — nothing written\n');
   238	    return finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'unsafe-tree', msg: warnings[0] ?? 'managed tree failed the jail check' } }, strict ? 1 : 0);
   239	  }
   240	
   241	  // Opt-in debounce (gate-2 major 14; Cursor afterFileEdit fires per edit):
   242	  // at most one real checkpoint per window, tracked by a per-platform stamp.
   243	  // The read-and-set runs UNDER the repo lock (gate-2 iter-2 M5) so two
   244	  // simultaneous afterFileEdit hooks can't both observe no stamp and both
   245	  // checkpoint — exactly one wins the window.
   246	  if (flags.debounce !== undefined) {
   247	    const seconds = Number(flags.debounce);
   248	    if (!Number.isFinite(seconds) || seconds <= 0) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', '--debounce <seconds> must be a positive number');
   249	    const stampPath = `${paths.logDir}/debounce-${platform}.json`;
   250	    const proceed = withLock(root, io, () => {
   251	      const stamp = safeReadJson(io.fs, stampPath);
   252	      if (stamp.ok && typeof stamp.value?.at === 'string' && Date.parse(io.now()) - Date.parse(stamp.value.at) < seconds * 1000) {
   253	        return false;
   254	      }
   255	      ensureDir(io.fs, paths.logDir);
   256	      atomicWriteJson(io.fs, stampPath, { at: io.now() });
   257	      return true;
   258	    });
   259	    if (!proceed) return finish({ ok: true, data: { events: 0, rewritten: false, debounced: true } }, 0);
   260	  }
   261	
   262	  let active = bundle;
   263	  let mustRewrite = false;
   264	
   265	  // Semantic isolation (plan §Concurrency): a stable foreign session or a
   266	  // mismatched origin platform must not merge into the active bundle. Checked
   267	  // before ANY write so a rejection leaves the whole tree untouched.
   268	  const originHint = active?.origin?.sessionHint;
   269	  const hasStableOwner = active !== null && typeof originHint === 'string' && originHint.length > 0 && active.origin.unstable !== true;
   270	  const stableIncoming = events.find(
   271	    (/** @type {any} */ e) => typeof e.sessionHint === 'string' && e.sessionHint.length > 0 && e.unstable === false,
   272	  );
   273	  const unstableIncoming = events.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => e.unstable === true);
   274	
   275	  if (hasStableOwner) {
   276	    // Foreign = a different stable session, OR any platform mismatch — the
   277	    // platform is provable even when the events carry no session hint (audit
   278	    // finding: a hint-less /baton:handoff narrative from claude-code silently
   279	    // merged into — then sealed — a codex-owned bundle, corrupting the origin
   280	    // the receive-side role avoidance keys on).
   281	    const incomingLabel = stableIncoming ? stableIncoming.sessionHint : '(no session hint)';
   282	    const foreign = stableIncoming
   283	      ? stableIncoming.sessionHint !== originHint || platform !== active.origin.platform
   284	      : platform !== active.origin.platform;
   285	    if (foreign && flags['take-over'] !== true) {
   286	      io.stderr.write(
   287	        `baton checkpoint: event from a foreign session/origin (${platform}/${incomingLabel} vs active ${active.origin.platform}/${originHint}) — rejected to keep sessions isolated; rerun with --take-over to archive the active bundle and start fresh\n`,
   288	      );
   289	      return finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'foreign-session', msg: 'event from a foreign session/origin rejected; rerun with --take-over' } }, 0);
   290	    }
   291	    if (foreign) {
   292	      rotateJournal(root, 'takeover', io);
   293	      const fresh = emptyBundle(
   294	        { platform, model: typeof flags.model === 'string' ? flags.model : 'unknown', goal: active.task?.goal ?? 'unknown' },
   295	        io.now(),
   296	      );
   297	      if (stableIncoming) fresh.origin.sessionHint = stableIncoming.sessionHint;
   298	      writeSnapshot(root, fresh, io);
   299	      io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: took over — prior bundle archived to history/, fresh bundle owned by ${platform}/${incomingLabel}\n`);
   300	      active = fresh;
   301	      mustRewrite = true;
   302	    }
   303	  }
   304	
   305	  if (unstableIncoming) {
   306	    io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: event carries an unstable (generated) session hint — ownership unverifiable; applied with this warning only\n');
   307	  }
   308	
   309	  if (active === null) {
   310	    active = emptyBundle(
   311	      { platform, model: typeof flags.model === 'string' ? flags.model : 'unknown', goal: 'unknown' },
   312	      io.now(),
   313	    );
   314	    writeSnapshot(root, active, io);
   315	    // Self-applying seed event (gate-2 iter-2 B6): a journal-only rebuild
   316	    // (snapshot + .bak both lost) must restore the bundle's identity, not the
   317	    // "unknown" placeholder resolveBase seeds. bundle.seed carries bundleId,
   318	    // origin, task, and generation and is applied on replay.
   319	    appendJournal(
   320	      root,
   321	      {
   322	        ts: io.now(),
   323	        type: 'bundle.seed',
   324	        payload: {
   325	          bundleId: active.bundleId,
   326	          generation: active.generation,
   327	          createdAt: active.createdAt,
   328	          origin: active.origin,
   329	          task: { goal: active.task.goal },
   330	          text: `[seed] auto-seeded a new bundle on ${platform} (model ${active.origin.model})`,
   331	        },
   332	        writerId: [platform, io.pid, 'seed'].join('-'),
   333	        dedupeKey: dedupeKey({ ts: io.now(), type: 'bundle.seed', bundleId: active.bundleId }),
   334	      },
   335	      io,
   336	    );
   337	    io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: no bundle found — auto-seeded a new one at .handoff/bundle.json\n');
   338	    mustRewrite = true;
   339	  }
   340	
   341	  // Ownership adoption (gate-2 fix 2): a bundle whose owner is unverified — a
   342	  // fresh seed (null hint) or a receive that defaulted to an unstable hint —
   343	  // adopts the first STABLE same-platform session as its owner, so semantic
   344	  // isolation engages from then on instead of never.
   345	  const ownerUnverified = active.origin.sessionHint === null || active.origin.unstable === true;
   346	  if (ownerUnverified && stableIncoming && active.origin.platform === platform) {
   347	    active = { ...active, origin: { ...active.origin, sessionHint: stableIncoming.sessionHint, unstable: false } };
   348	    writeSnapshot(root, active, io);
   349	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: adopted ${platform}/${stableIncoming.sessionHint} as the bundle owner (first verified session)\n`);
   350	    mustRewrite = true;
   351	  }
   352	
   353	  let lastSeq = 0;
   354	  for (const ev of events) {
   355	    const ts = typeof ev.ts === 'string' ? ev.ts : io.now();
   356	    const entry = {
   357	      ...ev,
   358	      ts,
   359	      dedupeKey:
   360	        typeof ev.dedupeKey === 'string' && ev.dedupeKey.length > 0
   361	          ? ev.dedupeKey
   362	          : dedupeKey({ ts, type: ev.type, payload: ev.payload, source: ev.source, sessionHint: ev.sessionHint }),
   363	      writerId: [platform, io.pid, ev.sessionHint ?? 'local'].join('-'),
   364	    };
   365	    lastSeq = appendJournal(root, entry, io);
   366	  }
   367	
   368	  const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, paths.snapshot);
   369	  const snapSeq = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.journalSeq === 'number' ? snap.value.journalSeq : 0;
   370	  const snapUpdated = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.updatedAt === 'string' ? Date.parse(snap.value.updatedAt) : 0;
   371	  const important = events.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => !ROUTINE_TYPES.has(e.type));
   372	  const elapsed = Date.parse(io.now()) - snapUpdated > THROTTLE_WINDOW_MS;
   373	  const accreted = lastSeq - snapSeq;
   374	
   375	  let rewritten = false;
   376	  if (mustRewrite || important || elapsed || accreted >= THROTTLE_EVENT_COUNT) {
   377	    // Bounded git refresh on EVERY snapshot rewrite (gate-2 iter-2 M1): a
   378	    // mechanical checkpoint carries branch/HEAD/dirty. Capture git BEFORE the
   379	    // lock — it is async and must not straddle the lock — then do ONE atomic
   380	    // read-modify-write UNDER the lock (iter-5 A1): reload the bundle inside the
   381	    // lock, apply git, and write with the fencing token. The old code loaded
   382	    // outside the lock, awaited git (yielding the event loop), then wrote the
   383	    // stale bundle, so a concurrent --take-over during the await was clobbered
   384	    // (origin rolled back, the new owner's event lost). Reloading inside the
   385	    // lock guarantees the write is built from current state.
   386	    const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   387	    rewritten = withLock(root, io, (token) => {
   388	      const merged = loadBundle(root, io).bundle;
   389	      if (!merged) return false;
   390	      if (git !== null) {
   391	        merged.git = git;
   392	      } else {
   393	        // git refresh failed/timed out (iter-4 I2/F5): NEVER retain the prior
   394	        // snapshot — stale HEAD/dirty presented as current corrupts the
   395	        // receive-side evidence audit. Clear to explicit unavailable (null) and
   396	        // warn; a repo that was never git (already null) warns nothing.
   397	        if (merged.git !== null) {
   398	          io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: git refresh failed — clearing stale git state (marked unavailable; receive re-derives it live)\n');
   399	        }
   400	        merged.git = null;
   401	      }
   402	      writeSnapshotIn(root, merged, io, token);
   403	      return true;
   404	    });
   405	  }
   406	  return finish({ ok: true, data: { events: events.length, rewritten } }, 0);
   407	}

     1	/**
     2	 * Pure, explainable role resolution over the committed matrix. Every decision
     3	 * is auditable: chosen entries carry their chainIndex; passed-over entries land
     4	 * in skipped[] with a why. avoid[] population is the caller's job.
     5	 * @param {{config: any, to: string, avoid?: string[], nativeOnly?: boolean, probes?: Record<string, {capability: string, outcome: string}> | null}} input
     6	 * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, any>, notes: string[]}}
     7	 */
     8	export function resolveRoles({ config, to, avoid = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null }) {
     9	  /** @type {string[]} */
    10	  const notes = [];
    11	
    12	  /**
    13	   * The eligibility verdict for a platform, or null when eligible.
    14	   * @param {string} platform @returns {string | null}
    15	   */
    16	  function skipReason(platform) {
    17	    if (avoid.includes(platform)) return 'avoided';
    18	    if (!(platform in (config.platforms ?? {}))) return 'unknown-platform';
    19	    if (config.platforms[platform]?.enabled === false) return 'disabled';
    20	    if (probes && probes[platform]) {
    21	      const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    22	      if (outcome === 'rate-limited') return 'rate-limited';
    23	      if (capability === 'not-installed') return 'not-installed';
    24	      // 'installed' means installation was PROVEN but the probe was capped there
    25	      // (capOnSuccess) — authentication is UNVERIFIED, not verified-failed. Only
    26	      // a probe that ran and did NOT succeed (outcome !== 'ok') is a verified
    27	      // auth/reachability failure worth skipping; a capped success stays
    28	      // selectable and is flagged degraded below (iter-3 F1, plan §Role matrix).
    29	      if (capability === 'installed' && outcome !== 'ok') return 'unauthenticated';
    30	    }
    31	    return null;
    32	  }
    33	
    34	  // A selection is degraded when its availability is UNVERIFIED (gate-2 iter-2
    35	  // M3, iter-3 F1): with no probe cache at all, resolution is offline and EVERY
    36	  // selection is degraded (plan: "Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged
    37	  // degraded"); with a partial cache, platforms the cache is missing are; and a
    38	  // platform probed only to 'installed' (auth unverified, e.g. a --version
    39	  // success) is degraded even though it stays selectable.
    40	  /** @param {string} platform */
    41	  const probeUnverified = (platform) => {
    42	    if (probes == null || !probes[platform]) return true;
    43	    const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    44	    // Degraded when ANY required dimension is unverified: a capped 'installed'
    45	    // (auth never confirmed) OR a non-ok outcome (iter-4 I6) — a selectable
    46	    // platform whose last probe ERRORED or TIMED OUT is presented as
    47	    // reachability-verified otherwise, which is exactly the silent-degradation
    48	    // the plan's degraded flag exists to surface. (rate-limited is skipped, not
    49	    // selected, so it never reaches here.)
    50	    return capability === 'installed' || outcome !== 'ok';
    51	  };
    52	
    53	  /** @type {Record<string, any>} */
    54	  const assignments = {};
    55	  for (const [role, chain] of Object.entries(config.roles)) {
    56	    /** @type {any[]} */
    57	    const skipped = [];
    58	    /** @type {any} */
    59	    let assignment = null;
    60	
    61	    for (let i = 0; i < chain.length; i += 1) {
    62	      const entry = chain[i];
    63	      if (nativeOnly && entry.platform !== to) {
    64	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'non-native' });
    65	        continue;
    66	      }
    67	      const why = skipReason(entry.platform);
    68	      if (why) {
    69	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why });
    70	        continue;
    71	      }
    72	      assignment = {
    73	        platform: entry.platform,
    74	        model: entry.model,
    75	        effort: entry.effort ?? null,
    76	        mode: entry.platform === to ? 'native' : 'delegated',
    77	        chainIndex: i,
    78	        skipped,
    79	      };
    80	      if (probeUnverified(entry.platform)) assignment.degraded = true;
    81	      break;
    82	    }
    83	
    84	    if (!assignment && nativeOnly) {
    85	      // Forced-default is only valid when the destination itself is eligible.
    86	      const whyTo = skipReason(to);
    87	      const model = config.defaults?.[to];
    88	      if (!whyTo && typeof model === 'string') {
    89	        assignment = { platform: to, model, effort: null, mode: 'forced-default', chainIndex: null, skipped };
    90	        if (probeUnverified(to)) assignment.degraded = true;
    91	      }
    92	    }
    93	
    94	    if (!assignment) {
    95	      assignment = { platform: null, model: null, effort: null, mode: 'unavailable', chainIndex: null, skipped };
    96	    }
    97	    assignments[role] = assignment;
    98	  }
    99	
   100	  return { assignments, notes };
   101	}

    57	const TOKEN_FIELDS = /** @type {const} */ ([

    59	  ['journalSeq', 'journal seq'],
    60	  ['handoffStatus', 'handoff status'],
    61	  ['receives', 'receive count'],

    67	  ['probesDigest', 'probe cache'],

    69	  ['sessionHint', 'target session'],
    70	]);

    73	/**
    74	 * The revision fingerprint the receipt token derives from. Every field is a
    75	 * bound input: any drift between prepare and commit re-derives a different
    76	 * token, so a stale receipt can never commit (plan §Concurrency).
    77	 * @param {string} root @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
    78	 * @returns {Record<string, any>}
    79	 */
    80	function tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io) {
    81	  let configDigest = 'absent';
    82	  try {
    83	    configDigest = dedupeKey(io.fs.readFileSync(`${root}/baton.config.json`, 'utf8'));
    84	  } catch {
    85	    // no config — 'absent' is itself a bound value
    86	  }
    87	  return {
    88	    generation: bundle.generation,
    89	    journalSeq: bundle.journalSeq,
    90	    // The seal state is a bound input too (gate-2 fix): a competing receiver
    91	    // that lands between this token's derivation and its commit changes
    92	    // status/receive_log, so the loser's token cannot re-derive.
    93	    handoffStatus: bundle.handoff?.status ?? null,
    94	    receives: Array.isArray(bundle.handoff?.receive_log) ? bundle.handoff.receive_log.length : 0,
    95	    origin: opts.origin,
    96	    reason: opts.reason,
    97	    // Explicit --reason-class is a bound intake input (gate-2 iter-2 M4): it
    98	    // changes the avoid[] decision, so a change between prepare and commit is
    99	    // drift that must re-prepare.
   100	    reasonClass: opts.reasonClass ?? null,
   101	    configDigest,
   102	    gitDigest: dedupeKey(opts.gitSnapshot ?? null),
   103	    probesDigest: dedupeKey(opts.probes ?? null),
   104	    platform: opts.platform,
   105	    sessionHint: opts.sessionHint,
   106	  };
   107	}

   109	/**
   110	 * Structured receipt token: a fixed-order join of per-input digests. Equality
   111	 * still gates commit exactly as the old opaque hash did; the structure only
   112	 * buys DIAGNOSIS — a mismatch can name the drifted input(s).
   113	 * @param {string} root @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io
   114	 */
   115	function deriveToken(root, bundle, opts, io) {
   116	  const inputs = tokenInputs(root, bundle, opts, io);
   117	  return `${TOKEN_PREFIX}.` + TOKEN_FIELDS.map(([key]) => dedupeKey(inputs[key] ?? null).slice(0, 10)).join('.');
   118	}

   120	/**
   121	 * Name the inputs whose digests differ between two structured tokens.
   122	 * @param {string} presented @param {string} expected @returns {string[]}
   123	 */
   124	function driftedInputs(presented, expected) {
   125	  const a = presented.split('.');
   126	  const b = expected.split('.');
   127	  if (a[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || b[0] !== TOKEN_PREFIX || a.length !== b.length) return [];
   128	  return TOKEN_FIELDS.filter((_, i) => a[i + 1] !== b[i + 1]).map(([, name]) => name);
   129	}

   131	/**
   132	 * @param {any} bundle @param {ReceiveOpts} opts @param {any} io

   135	function stalenessWarnings(bundle, opts, io) {
   136	  /** @type {string[]} */
   137	  const warnings = [];
   138	  if (bundle.handoff.status === 'open') {
   139	    warnings.push('source bundle is unsealed (open) — the handoff was never finalized; treating this as a degraded (limit-death) receive');
   140	  }
   141	  const ref = bundle.handoff.finalizedAt ?? bundle.updatedAt;
   142	  const ageMs = Date.parse(io.now()) - Date.parse(ref);
   143	  if (Number.isFinite(ageMs) && ageMs > STALE_AFTER_MS) {
   144	    warnings.push(`bundle finalized ${Math.round(ageMs / 3_600_000)}h ago (staleness threshold 12h) — re-verify before continuing`);
   145	  }
